teile.einleitung: Bulgaria is a country in south-eastern Europe on the Balkan Peninsula. It lies on the Black Sea and is known for its roses, its yoghurt and the Cyrillic script.
wichtigste: The capital of Bulgaria is Sofia.
Bulgaria lies in the east on the Black Sea.
People write with the Cyrillic script.
In the Rose Valley, valuable rose oil is made from rose petals.
Nodding the head often means “no” in Bulgaria.
The Danube forms most of the border with Romania.
Bulgaria has been a member of the EU since 2007.

abschnitte.text: Bulgaria lies on the **Balkan Peninsula**. In the east it has a coast on the **Black Sea**, where many people go on seaside holidays. In the north the **Danube** forms the border with Romania for about 470 kilometres. The capital **Sofia** lies at the foot of the mountain **Vitosha**. Its landmark is the **Alexander Nevsky Cathedral** with its gilded main dome.

In Bulgaria people write with **Cyrillic letters**. This script arose over 1,000 years ago in the Bulgarian empire of the time. Pupils of the monks Cyril and Methodius developed it further there. Today other countries such as Serbia, Russia and Ukraine also use Cyrillic letters. Every year on 24 May, Bulgaria celebrates a holiday in honour of writing and education.

In the **Rose Valley** in the middle of the country grow huge fields of roses. From the blossoms valuable **rose oil** is obtained, which is used for perfume. Bulgaria is also famous for its **yoghurt**. A bacterium that turns milk into yoghurt even bears the name of the country: Lactobacillus bulgaricus.

In the mountains lies the **Rila Monastery**. It is part of the **UNESCO World Heritage** and has many colourful paintings on its walls. There is a peculiarity in everyday life: in Bulgaria a **nod of the head** often means “no” and **shaking the head** “yes”. In Switzerland it is exactly the other way round. So anyone visiting Bulgaria should look carefully.

gewusst: In Bulgaria, nodding often means “no”, which can be quite confusing for visitors.
A yoghurt bacterium is named after Bulgaria.

teile.einleitung: A drought is a long period with far too little rain. In Europe, the Iberian Peninsula with Spain and Portugal is especially badly affected.
wichtigste: A 2022 study showed that the **Azores High** has expanded more than at any time in 1,200 years.
During drought, old structures appeared in empty reservoirs, for example the **Dolmen of Guadalperal**.
In February 2024, **Catalonia** declared a state of emergency because of the drought.
The wetland **Doñana** suffers from falling groundwater.
Coastal cities such as Barcelona use **seawater desalination**.
In 2023 **olive oil** became much more expensive worldwide because of drought and heat.

abschnitte.titel: Why the Iberian Peninsula is so dry
abschnitte.text: The **Azores High** is a high-pressure area over the Atlantic. It keeps rain clouds away from Spain and Portugal. A 2022 study showed that it has expanded more than at any time in 1,200 years. As a result less rain falls in winter. Together with the heat, soils, rivers and reservoirs dry out. In Switzerland too there have been very dry summers in recent years.

When reservoirs are almost empty, old things come to light again. In the **Valdecañas Reservoir** in Extremadura, the **Dolmen of Guadalperal** appeared, a circle of upright stones from prehistoric times. In the Catalan reservoir of **Sau**, a **Romanesque church** became almost completely visible in 2023. It had belonged to a village that was flooded when the reservoir was built.

abschnitte.titel: State of emergency and water from the sea
abschnitte.text: In February 2024 the region of **Catalonia** declared a state of emergency because of the drought. In Barcelona too, water had to be saved. To have enough drinking water, coastal cities use **seawater desalination**. In this the salt is removed from the sea water. This, however, takes a lot of energy.

The drought also hits farmers. In 2023 there were far fewer olives in Spain because of dryness and heat, and **olive oil** became much more expensive worldwide. The **Tagus Segura Aqueduct** carries water from the river Tagus to the dry south-east of Spain, and there is much dispute about it. In the wetland of **Doñana** in Andalusia, the groundwater is falling, partly because of wells for strawberry growing.

Several large rivers flow from Spain to Portugal, for example the Tagus and the Douro. In dry times it matters how much water reaches the neighbouring country. That is why both countries concluded the **Albufeira Convention** in 1998. In it they regulate how they use the water of their shared rivers, even during a drought.

gewusst: The Dolmen of Guadalperal is also called the “Spanish Stonehenge” and is several thousand years old.
Spain is the largest producer of olive oil in the world.

teile.einleitung: Butrint is an ancient archaeological site in the south of Albania. Buildings from many periods have been preserved here, which is why the place is part of the UNESCO World Heritage.
wichtigste: Butrint lies in the south of Albania, near the border with Greece.
The site has been part of the UNESCO World Heritage since 1992.
Buildings from Greek, Roman and Byzantine times have been preserved.
Butrint lies on a peninsula between a lake and a channel.
The ruins are surrounded by a national park.

abschnitte.text: **Butrint** lies in the far south of **Albania**, not far from the Greek border and opposite the island of Corfu. The ruins stand on a wooded peninsula. On one side lies a **lake**, on the other a channel that leads to the sea. Around the excavations there is a **national park** with wetlands and many birds.

Butrint was inhabited for many centuries. First **Greeks** lived here, then the **Romans**; later the place belonged to the **Byzantine Empire** and later still to Venice. Each period left traces. You can see, for example, a **theatre** from ancient times, city walls with a Lion Gate, remains of churches and a baptistery with floor mosaics.

Since **1992** Butrint has been part of the **UNESCO World Heritage**. With this, UNESCO protects places that are important for all humanity. Archaeologists are still digging at Butrint and keep finding new things. Because the place shows such different periods, it is sometimes called a history book in the open air.

gewusst: In Virgil’s Roman epic poem the “Aeneid”, Butrint appears as a place where Aeneas stops on his journey.

teile.einleitung: Avebury is a small village in southern England that lies in the middle of a huge Neolithic stone circle. It is not far from Stonehenge.
wichtigste: Avebury lies in the county of Wiltshire in southern England.
The largest stone circle in Europe stands here.
The monument dates from the Neolithic.
Part of the village lies inside the stone circle.
Together with Stonehenge, Avebury is part of the UNESCO World Heritage.

abschnitte.text: In **Avebury** stands the **largest stone circle in Europe**. A round bank with a deep ditch encloses a large circle of mighty, unshaped stones. Inside it lie two smaller stone circles. The monument is so large that part of the village and a road lie right in the middle of it.

The monument was built in the **Neolithic**, over 4,500 years ago. People at the time had no metal tools and no machines. What exactly the circle was used for is not known for certain. Experts suspect that it was a place for ceremonies and gatherings. Nearby lies **Silbury Hill**, a large artificial mound from the same period.

Over many centuries, stones were knocked over, buried or smashed and used as building material. In the 20th century, researchers had some stones set upright again. Since **1986** Avebury has been part of the **UNESCO World Heritage** together with **Stonehenge**. Unlike at Stonehenge, you can walk directly among the stones here.

gewusst: Silbury Hill near Avebury counts as the largest artificial prehistoric mound in Europe.
In Avebury, sheep often graze among the ancient stones.

teile.einleitung: Europe is one of the seven continents of the Earth. Switzerland also belongs to it, lying roughly in the middle. Europe is small, but very many people live here with many different languages.
wichtigste: Europe is a continent, that is, a part of the world.
Europe lies entirely in the northern hemisphere.
In the west lies the Atlantic, in the north the Arctic Ocean.
To the south, on the other side of the Mediterranean, lies Africa.
Europe is joined to Asia on land; together they are called Eurasia.
Europe is the second-smallest continent; only Australia is smaller.

abschnitte.text: According to the usual count at school, the Earth has **seven continents**: Europe, Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Australia and Antarctica. **Europe** is one of them. It is the **second-smallest** continent; only Australia is smaller. Even so there are very many countries, languages and cultures in Europe. Because Europe lies entirely north of the equator, it belongs to the **northern hemisphere**.

Europe is surrounded by water on three sides. In the west lies the **Atlantic Ocean**, with America on its other side. In the far north begins the cold **Arctic Ocean**, which is often full of ice. In the south lies the **Mediterranean**. Beyond it begins **Africa**, and between Spain and Morocco the sea is only narrow.

In the east there is no sea that separates Europe from **Asia**. The two continents together form a huge landmass called **Eurasia**. As the border people mostly take the **Ural Mountains**, the Ural River, the Caspian Sea and the Caucasus. Countries such as Russia and Turkey therefore lie partly in Europe and partly in Asia. The city of Istanbul even lies on both continents.

**Switzerland** lies roughly in the middle of Europe, in **central Europe**. It has no sea, but it has the **Alps**, the largest mountain range in the middle of Europe. In the Swiss Alps great rivers such as the **Rhine** and the **Rhône** rise. Neighbouring countries are Germany, France, Italy, Austria and Liechtenstein. From Switzerland you can reach many countries of Europe in a few hours by train.

The name Europe comes from a **Greek legend**. In it the god **Zeus**, in the form of a bull, carries the king’s daughter **Europa** across the sea to Crete. The continent gets its name from her. The picture of Europa on the bull can be found today on coins, stamps and statues. On the Greek 2-euro coin the legend is shown.

gewusst: The city of Istanbul lies on two continents, in Europe and in Asia.
On the Greek 2-euro coin you can see the king’s daughter Europa on a bull.

teile.einleitung: Albania is a country in south-eastern Europe on the Balkan Peninsula. It lies on the Adriatic Sea and the Ionian Sea, and its capital is Tirana.
wichtigste: The capital of Albania is Tirana.
In Albanian the country is called Shqipëria.
The flag shows a black double-headed eagle on a red background.
The national hero is Skanderbeg.
Albania lies on the Adriatic Sea and the Ionian Sea.
The currency is called the lek.

abschnitte.text: Albanians call their country **Shqipëria**. The name is often linked with the word for eagle. That is why Albania is also called the “land of the eagles”. On the red **flag** you can see a black **double-headed eagle**, an eagle with two heads. People pay with the **lek**, which is named after Alexander the Great.

**Tirana** is the capital and the largest city of the country. In the middle lies the large **Skanderbeg Square**. The airport is named after **Mother Teresa**, a nun with Albanian parents who helped poor people in India. The city of **Berat** is called the “city of a thousand windows”, because many white houses with windows stand one above the other on the slope.

Almost 600 years ago, **Skanderbeg** fought against the Ottoman Empire. He is regarded as the **national hero**. After that, Albania belonged to the Ottoman Empire for a long time until it became independent in 1912. After the Second World War, a communist **dictatorship** under Enver Hoxha ruled. It shut the country off and had small concrete bunkers built everywhere. Since 1991 Albania has been a democracy.

In the north Albania lies on the **Adriatic**, in the south on the **Ionian Sea**. On the coast there are beaches and clear water. Inland, Albania is very mountainous, and in the north the **Albanian Alps** rise. More and more holidaymakers are discovering the country.

Many people with Albanian roots live in Switzerland. Many of them come from **Kosovo** or from North Macedonia, where Albanian is also spoken. That is why you hear **Albanian** quite often in Switzerland. Some well-known Swiss footballers have Albanian roots.

gewusst: In Albania, many small concrete bunkers from the time of the dictatorship still stand today.
The currency lek is named after Alexander the Great.

teile.einleitung: Gothenburg is the second largest city in Sweden. It lies on the west coast by the sea and has the largest port in Scandinavia. The city is an important centre for trade and industry.
wichtigste: Gothenburg is the second largest city in Sweden.
It lies on the west coast, on the Kattegat.
Gothenburg has the largest port in Scandinavia.
This is where the river Göta älv flows into the sea.
The third largest city in Sweden is Malmö.

abschnitte.text: **Gothenburg** lies on the **west coast of Sweden**, on the **Kattegat**, a part of the sea between Sweden and Denmark. This is where the river **Göta älv** flows into the sea. After the capital Stockholm, Gothenburg is the **second largest city** in the country, ahead of **Malmö**. Because the city faces west towards the open sea, it has always been important for trade with other countries.

Gothenburg has the **largest port in Scandinavia**. Container ships, tankers and ferries arrive here. Many goods for the whole of Sweden and Norway are transferred here. Via the Göta älv and the **Göta Canal**, the city is also connected to the great lakes in the interior of the country.

Gothenburg was founded in **1621** by King **Gustav II Adolf**. Dutch builders helped with the construction, which is why the city centre has canals like those in Holland. Later Gothenburg became an important **industrial city**. The car company **Volvo**, for example, was founded here. The city is also home to **Liseberg**, one of the largest amusement parks in Scandinavia.

gewusst: The canals in the centre of Gothenburg were built on the Dutch model.
The car company Volvo comes from Gothenburg.

teile.einleitung: The Common Agricultural Policy, or CAP for short, governs farming in the European Union. It gives money to farmers and sets rules for the environment and animal welfare. It is one of the oldest and most expensive policies of the EU.
wichtigste: The Common Agricultural Policy came into force in 1962.
It is meant to secure the food supply and keep farmers' incomes stable.
The first pillar covers direct payments and market measures, and the second supports rural areas.
Guaranteed minimum prices led to butter mountains and milk lakes in the 1970s and 1980s.
The milk quota applied from 1984 to 2015.
Today around one third of the EU budget goes to agricultural policy.

abschnitte.text: The **Common Agricultural Policy** (CAP) came into force in **1962**, at that time in the European Economic Community (EEC). After the Second World War, people wanted to make sure there was enough food. At the same time, the **incomes of farmers** were to stay stable. The CAP is one of the oldest common policies in Europe.

At first the Community guaranteed farmers that it would buy their products at fixed **minimum prices**. As a result, more was produced than was needed. In the 1970s and 1980s huge surpluses built up, which were called **butter mountains** and **milk lakes**. They had to be stored at great expense or exported cheaply. To limit the amount of milk, the **milk quota** was introduced in **1984**. It ran out on 31 March **2015**.

With the **MacSharry reform** of **1992**, named after the agriculture commissioner Ray MacSharry, the guaranteed prices were lowered. In return, farmers received **direct payments**. The reform of **2003** brought **decoupling**: since then the payments no longer depend on the amount produced, but mainly on the area of land. Anyone who receives money has to follow rules on the environment, animals and food. This principle was called **cross-compliance**, and since 2023 it has been called **conditionality**.

abschnitte.titel: Two pillars and a lot of money
abschnitte.text: The CAP has two **pillars**. The first mainly covers direct payments and market measures. The second supports the **development of rural areas**, for example environmental programmes, investment and villages. In the 1980s more than half of the EU budget went to agriculture, but today it is about **one third**.

In the past the EU subsidised **exports** of surpluses. These were sold at prices below the cost of production. Critics complained that farmers in **developing countries** could not compete as a result. Today these export subsidies have largely been abolished. Switzerland is not in the EU and has its own agricultural policy, but it also has **direct payments** to farms.

gewusst: The butter surpluses in the 1980s were so large that people spoke of “butter mountains”.
For over 30 years the milk quota limited how much milk each farm was allowed to deliver.

teile.einleitung: Amsterdam is the capital of the Netherlands. The city is famous for its canals, narrow houses, many bridges and bicycles, and for well-known museums.
wichtigste: Amsterdam is the capital of the Netherlands.
The city is named after a dam in the River Amstel.
The “grachten” are canals that run like rings through the old town.
The canal ring was created in the 17th century and is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
Amsterdam has well over 1,000 bridges.
In the Rijksmuseum hangs Rembrandt’s “The Night Watch”.

abschnitte.text: Amsterdam grew up at a **dam** in the River **Amstel**. That is where the name comes from. The city is the **capital** of the Netherlands, but the government sits in The Hague. Typical are the **grachten**, canals with water that run like rings through the old town. In the past, ships carried goods right up to the houses. Because there are so many canals, Amsterdam needs well over 1,000 **bridges**.

In the **17th century** the Netherlands were a rich trading power. This time is called the **Golden Age**. It was then that the **canal ring** was laid out, where rich merchants built their houses. Since 2010 it has been a **UNESCO World Heritage** site. The painter **Rembrandt** also lived in Amsterdam at this time.

The old houses along the canals are **narrow and tall**. It is often said that in the past taxes depended on the width of the house. So people built narrow but high and deep. The stairs inside are very steep. At the top of the gable, many houses have a **hook**: with it, large pieces of furniture are hoisted up outside on a rope and brought in through the window.

In the **Rijksmuseum** hangs Rembrandt’s large painting “The Night Watch”. The **Van Gogh Museum** shows many paintings by **Vincent van Gogh**, such as his sunflowers. Particularly moving is the **Anne Frank House**. Anne Frank was a Jewish girl who in the Second World War had to hide with her family from the Nazis in a back house. There she wrote her famous **diary**.

In the canals lie about 2,500 **houseboats**. People live in them as in a flat. Even better known are the many **bicycles**: in Amsterdam very many people cycle to school, to work or to the shops. There are separate cycle paths and huge bicycle car parks by the station.

gewusst: Amsterdam is the capital of the Netherlands, but the government and parliament sit in The Hague.
Many old houses in Amsterdam stand on wooden piles that were driven deep into the soft ground.

teile.einleitung: Lake Lugano is a lake in the south of Switzerland that belongs partly to the canton of Ticino and partly to Italy. It winds like a long, branching arm between steep mountains. On its shore lie the city of Lugano and the special village of Campione d'Italia.
wichtigste: Lake Lugano lies in the canton of Ticino and in the Italian region of Lombardy.
It is about 49 square kilometres in area and up to 288 metres deep.
The best-known city on its shore is Lugano.
Campione d'Italia is an Italian village entirely surrounded by Switzerland.
A causeway at Melide carries road, railway and motorway across the lake.
In Italian the lake is called Lago di Lugano or also Ceresio.

abschnitte.text: Lake Lugano lies at about 271 metres above sea level between Lake Maggiore and Lake Como. About two thirds of its area belong to **Switzerland**, the rest to **Italy**. The lake has a winding shape with several arms, a little like a Z. Its water drains through the Tresa into Lake Maggiore.

Steep mountains rise around the lake, for example **Monte San Salvatore** and **Monte Brè** near Lugano. Funiculars run up both, and from the top you have a magnificent view. At the southern end rises Monte Generoso, which a cog railway climbs. Because the mountains stand so close to the shore, the lake is very deep in many places.

At Melide a **causeway** crosses the lake at its narrowest point. It was built in the 19th century and today carries the Gotthard railway line, a road and the A2 motorway. So the causeway is an important link between north and south. Right next to it in Melide lies the miniature park Swissminiatur.

On the east shore lies the village of **Campione d'Italia**. It belongs to Italy but is surrounded on all sides by Swiss territory and the lake. This kind of thing is called an **exclave**. The village is known for its large casino, and there people often pay in Swiss francs.

On the shore lie pretty villages such as **Morcote**, Gandria and Brusino. Many houses have arcades and gardens with palms, because the climate in Ticino is mild. Passenger boats link Lugano with the villages around the lake. Along the shore at Gandria runs a well-known walking trail, the Olive Trail.

begriffe.erklaerung: A piece of land of one state that is entirely surrounded by the territory of another state.
A banked-up ridge across a lake on which paths or railways run.
The old Italian name of Lake Lugano.
A railway whose cars are pulled up the mountain on rails by a cable.

gewusst: In Campione d'Italia Italian law applies, but from there you can walk into Switzerland without a border check.
Lake Lugano is so deep that a high-rise of over 280 metres would disappear completely in it.
Between Lake Lugano and Lake Como, at the narrowest point there are only a few kilometres of land.

teile.einleitung: Constanța is a port city in Romania on the Black Sea. It has the largest port in the country and is one of the oldest cities in Romania.
wichtigste: Constanța lies on the Black Sea in Romania.
It has the most important seaport in Romania.
A canal links the port with the Danube.
In ancient times the city was called Tomis.
The Roman poet Ovid lived here in exile.

abschnitte.text: **Constanța** is the most important **seaport** in Romania and one of the largest ports on the **Black Sea**. Goods from all over the world are handled here. Through the **Danube Black Sea Canal**, the port is linked to the Danube. This way ships can carry goods far into the interior of Europe.

Constanța is very old. Already in ancient times, **Greeks** founded a city here called **Tomis**. Later it belonged to the Roman Empire. The Roman poet **Ovid** was banished here by the emperor and spent the last years of his life in Tomis. Today a statue in the old town recalls him.

In the old town, right by the sea, stands the old **Casino**, a decorated building from the early 20th century. North of the city lies **Mamaia**, a well-known seaside resort with long sandy beaches. In summer many holidaymakers come to this coast.

gewusst: In Tomis the Roman poet Ovid wrote sad poems about his longing for Rome.

teile.einleitung: Edinburgh is the capital of Scotland. The city is famous for its castle on an old volcano, its old town and its big cultural festival in August.
wichtigste: **Edinburgh Castle** stands on an extinct volcano.
The **Royal Mile** links the castle with the royal palace.
In the middle of the city lies the hill **Arthur’s Seat**, also an old volcano.
Edinburgh lies on the inlet **Firth of Forth**.
The Scottish Parliament meets at **Holyrood**.
Every August a huge **theatre and arts festival** takes place.

abschnitte.text: Many millions of years ago there were active volcanoes here. Today they are long extinct. On such a volcanic rock, Castle Rock, stands **Edinburgh Castle**. In the middle of the city rises the hill **Arthur’s Seat**, which is also an old volcano. From the top you can see over the whole city to the **Firth of Forth**, a wide inlet of the North Sea.

The main street of the old town is called the **Royal Mile**. It leads downhill from the castle to the royal palace of **Holyrood**. It is about one Scottish mile long, hence the name. On the left and right stand old, tall stone houses and many narrow lanes. The Old Town and the planned New Town together are a **UNESCO World Heritage** site.

Edinburgh is the capital of **Scotland**, which belongs to the United Kingdom. Scotland has its own parliament, which has existed again since 1999. It meets in a modern building in the district of **Holyrood**, near the royal palace. It decides on many matters in Scotland, for example schools and health.

Every **August** Edinburgh turns into a huge stage. At the **Edinburgh Festival Fringe**, thousands of performers appear, with theatre, music, comedy and dance. It is regarded as the largest arts festival in the world. Edinburgh is also a city of books: the author **J. K. Rowling** wrote parts of her Harry Potter novels in cafés in the city.

gewusst: From Edinburgh Castle, a cannon is fired almost every day at 1 pm, the so-called One O’Clock Gun.
In 2004 Edinburgh was the first city to be named a City of Literature by UNESCO.

teile.einleitung: The Balearic Islands are a Spanish island group in the Mediterranean. They include Majorca, Minorca, Ibiza and Formentera, popular holiday destinations also for many Swiss families.
wichtigste: The Balearics lie in the Mediterranean and belong to Spain.
The largest island is Majorca, the second-largest Minorca.
The smallest of the four inhabited main islands is Formentera.
The capital is Palma.
Besides Spanish, Catalan is spoken.
You reach the islands by ship or aeroplane.

abschnitte.text: The **Balearics** lie in the **Mediterranean** east of the Spanish mainland. The largest island is **Majorca**, the second-largest **Minorca**. There are also **Ibiza** and **Formentera**, the smallest of the four inhabited main islands. South of Majorca lies the small, almost uninhabited island of **Cabrera**. It is a **national park** that protects land and sea.

The capital of the Balearics is **Palma** on Majorca. Above the harbour stands a large Gothic cathedral. On the islands people speak **Catalan** as well as Spanish. The Balearics are an **autonomous community** of Spain, a bit like a canton that can decide many things itself.

In the valley of **Sóller** on Majorca, **oranges** grow on many trees. Already in winter, around January and February, the **almond trees** bloom white and pink on Majorca. Then the island looks as if covered with snow. In the north-west, the **Serra de Tramuntana** mountains run along the coast. They are a UNESCO World Heritage site.

From the mainland you reach the Balearics by **ship** or by **aeroplane**. Ferries run, for example, from Barcelona and Valencia. The airport of Palma is among the busiest in Spain, especially in summer. **Tourism** is very important for the islands. Many people come for the beaches, the bays and the mountains.

gewusst: Majorca is larger than the canton of Ticino.
On Minorca stand many stone structures from the Bronze Age.

teile.einleitung: The Danube Delta lies where the Danube flows into the Black Sea. It is a huge landscape of river arms, lakes and reeds and a paradise for birds.
wichtigste: Most of the Danube Delta lies in **Romania**, a small part in Ukraine.
It is the second-largest delta in Europe; only the **Volga Delta** is larger.
Huge areas are covered with **reeds**.
In the delta, **pelicans** breed in the largest colony in Europe.
The Danube splits into three main arms; the **Sulina arm** was developed for ships.
Since 1991 the Danube Delta has been a UNESCO World Heritage site.

abschnitte.text: The Danube is one of the longest rivers in Europe. Shortly before the **Black Sea** it splits into three main arms: the Chilia arm, the **Sulina arm** and the Saint George arm. Between them lie countless small channels, lakes and islands. Such an area is called a **delta**, because on the map it looks similar to the Greek letter Δ. Most of it lies in **Romania**, a smaller part belongs to Ukraine.

The Danube carries a lot of **sand and mud**. At the mouth the water flows more slowly, and the particles sink. These deposited particles are called **sediments**. So the delta grows a little further out into the sea every year. The Danube Delta is the second-largest delta in Europe; only the **Volga Delta** in Russia is larger.

Large areas are covered with **reeds**. They form one of the largest continuous reed beds on Earth. In the delta live very many species of birds. Especially well known are the **pelicans**, which breed here in the largest colony in Europe. Many species of fish also live in the waters. Since 1991 the Danube Delta has been part of the **UNESCO World Heritage**.

In the delta there are only a few roads. Many villages can be reached only **by boat**. People there traditionally live from fishing and from reeds, which are used, for example, for roofs. So that large ships can sail from the sea up the Danube, the **Sulina arm** was straightened and deepened. The starting point for many boat trips is the town of Tulcea.

gewusst: The water arriving in the Danube Delta also comes in part from Switzerland: the Inn from the Engadine flows into the Danube.
Because the delta keeps growing, the old lighthouse of Sulina now stands some distance from the sea.

teile.einleitung: By “Energiewende” (energy transition), people in Germany mean the rebuilding of the energy supply: away from nuclear power, coal and oil, towards wind, sun and other renewable energies. The project has been going on for decades and is still much debated.
wichtigste: The term comes from a study by the Öko-Institut of 1980.
The Renewable Energy Sources Act (EEG) of 2000 supported wind and solar power with fixed payments.
After Fukushima in 2011, Germany decided on a rapid nuclear phase-out.
On 15 April 2023 the last three nuclear power stations were taken off the grid.
In 2023, for the first time, more than half of the electricity came from renewable sources.
Germany wants to be climate neutral by 2045.

abschnitte.text: In 1980 the **Öko-Institut** published a study with the title “Energie-Wende”. It showed how one could manage without oil and uranium. From 1991, the **Electricity Feed-in Act** required power suppliers to take and pay for electricity from renewable sources. This helped above all the first wind turbines. Today the word “Energiewende” is even used in English.

In 2000 the **Renewable Energy Sources Act**, **EEG** for short, came into force. Anyone who built a wind or solar plant received a fixed payment for the electricity for 20 years. For a long time this was paid for through the **EEG surcharge** on the electricity bill. Since July 2022 this surcharge no longer exists, and the support has since come from the federal budget. Many countries have taken the EEG as a model.

Already around 2000, a phase-out of **nuclear power** was agreed, but later the operating lives were extended. After the reactor disaster at **Fukushima** in Japan in March 2011, the government of Angela Merkel changed course. Eight reactors were taken off the grid immediately. On **15 April 2023**, Isar 2, Emsland and Neckarwestheim 2 were shut down. Since then Germany has produced no nuclear power.

abschnitte.titel: Wind in the north, consumption in the south
abschnitte.text: In 2023 renewable energies covered for the first time **more than half** of electricity consumption. The most important source is **wind energy**. A lot of wind blows in northern Germany and at sea, but many large factories stand in the south. That is why new **extra-high-voltage lines** such as **SuedLink** are needed, carrying electricity over hundreds of kilometres. Building such lines takes a long time and is often disputed.

Under the **Climate Protection Act**, Germany is to be climate neutral by **2045**, five years before the EU’s goal. The phase-out of coal has also been decided. Supporters see the Energiewende as an important contribution to climate protection. Critics point to high costs and to the question of how to have enough electricity when no wind is blowing. In **Switzerland** there is a similar goal with the **Energy Strategy 2050**.

gewusst: The word “Energiewende” is also often used untranslated in English texts.
Swiss voters accepted the Energy Strategy 2050 in 2017.

teile.einleitung: On the coasts of the seas, the water rises and falls regularly. This movement is called the tides, meaning high tide and low tide. It is caused mainly by the pull of the Moon's gravity.
wichtigste: Tides are the regular rising and falling of sea level.
When the water rises, it is called high tide, and when it falls, low tide.
The main cause is the Moon's gravitational pull, with the Sun adding a weaker effect.
On most coasts there are about two high tides and two low tides a day.
The difference between high and low water is called the tidal range.

abschnitte.titel: The Moon pulls on the water
abschnitte.text: The **Moon** pulls on the water of the oceans with its **gravity**. As a result, a **tidal bulge** forms on the side of the Earth facing the Moon. A tidal bulge also forms on the opposite side. Because the Earth turns, the coasts move through these bulges. That is why in many places there are about **two high tides a day** and two low tides.

The **Sun** also pulls on the water, but more weakly than the Moon, because it is much further away. When the Sun, Moon and Earth are in a line, at full moon and new moon, their forces add together. Then there are especially high tides, called **spring tides**. When the Sun and Moon are at a right angle to the Earth, they weaken each other. Then the tides are weaker, and these are called **neap tides**.

The difference in height between high water and low water is called the **tidal range**. It is different on every coast. In the open ocean it is often only small, while in narrow bays it can reach many metres. In the **Bay of Fundy** in Canada it is especially large. In the **Mediterranean**, on the other hand, the tides are rather weak.

On flat coasts the sea floor dries out at low tide. On the North Sea this creates the **Wadden Sea**, which is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Worms, mussels, crabs and many birds live there, searching for food at low tide. On the Swiss lakes you cannot notice the tides at all, because they are far too small.

gewusst: Because the Moon keeps moving, high tide comes a little later each day than the day before.
At low tide you can walk on the sea floor in the Wadden Sea, but only with an experienced guide.

teile.einleitung: Ankara is the capital of Turkey. It lies in the middle of the country in central Anatolia and was made the capital in 1923 by Mustafa Kemal Atatürk.
wichtigste: Ankara has been the capital of Turkey since 1923.
Mustafa Kemal Atatürk chose Ankara as the capital.
Ankara lies in central Anatolia.
After Istanbul, Ankara is the second-largest city in Turkey.
Atatürk is buried in the mausoleum Anıtkabir.
Its earlier name Angora survives in the names of animals.

abschnitte.text: After the end of the **Ottoman Empire**, **Mustafa Kemal Atatürk** founded the **Republic of Turkey** in 1923. He made Ankara the capital, although Istanbul was much larger and more famous. Ankara lay sheltered inland and had been an important place in the War of Independence. Today the government and parliament, the **Grand National Assembly**, have their seat here.

Ankara lies in **central Anatolia**, a high plateau in the Asian part of Turkey. The climate is dry, with hot summers and cold winters. A small town has grown into a huge metropolis. Today Ankara is, after **Istanbul**, the **second-largest city** in the country.

On a hill stands the large mausoleum **Anıtkabir**. Atatürk is buried there. Many Turks visit the place to honour him, and visiting heads of state also lay wreaths here. The complex includes a long path lined with lion figures and a museum.

Ankara is a very old city. In ancient times it was called **Ankyra**, and later in Europe for a long time **Angora**. This name survives in the **Angora cat**, the **Angora goat** and the **Angora rabbit**. The fine wool **mohair** is made from the hair of the Angora goat. Above the old town sits an old **citadel**, a fortress on a rock.

gewusst: Ankara was already an important city in Roman times.
With a large museum of Anatolian civilisations, Ankara shows finds from many thousands of years.

teile.einleitung: Elbrus is an extinct volcano in the Caucasus in Russia. At 5,642 metres it is often described as the highest mountain in Europe.
wichtigste: Elbrus has **two peaks**; the higher western peak is 5,642 metres high.
It is 836 metres higher than Mont Blanc at 4,806 metres.
It counts as the highest mountain in Europe because it lies north of the **Caucasus watershed**.
It belongs to the **Seven Summits**, the highest mountains of all the continents.
Elbrus is a **stratovolcano** that last erupted about 2,000 years ago.
It lies in the republics of **Kabardino-Balkaria** and **Karachay-Cherkessia**.

abschnitte.text: Elbrus lies in the **Caucasus**, a high mountain range between the Black Sea and the Caspian Sea. It has **two peaks**: the western peak is 5,642 metres high, the eastern peak somewhat lower. The mountain lies on the territory of the Russian republics of **Kabardino-Balkaria** and **Karachay-Cherkessia**. It is covered with thick glaciers.

Exactly where the border between Europe and Asia runs in the Caucasus is not defined entirely uniformly. Often the **watershed** of the Caucasus is taken as the border. This is the line that decides which side rainwater flows off to. Elbrus lies north of it and so counts as part of Europe. Then it is 836 metres higher than **Mont Blanc** and the highest mountain in Europe. So it also appears on the list of the **Seven Summits**.

Elbrus is a **stratovolcano**. It is built up of many layers of lava and ash that were laid on top of one another in eruptions. The last eruption was about 2,000 years ago. Today it is regarded as dormant. But in some places warm gases and springs still emerge.

In 1829 **Killar Khashirov** was the first to reach the eastern peak. He was part of a Russian research expedition. The higher western peak was first climbed in 1874, so in the **19th century**. A mountain guide from **St Niklaus** in Valais took part, together with British climbers. Today many people try to climb Elbrus every year.

gewusst: In 1874 a mountain guide from Valais stood on the highest peak of the Caucasus.
On Elbrus there are cable cars that lead up to well over 3,000 metres.

teile.einleitung: The Bosphorus is a narrow strait in Istanbul. It links the Black Sea with the Sea of Marmara and at the same time separates Europe from Asia.
wichtigste: The Bosphorus is a strait, that is, a narrow waterway between two pieces of land.
It links the Black Sea with the Sea of Marmara.
It separates Europe and Asia.
It is about 30 kilometres long and at its narrowest point about 700 metres wide.
Three large bridges cross it, opened in 1973, 1988 and 2016.
Since 2013 the Marmaray railway has run in a tunnel beneath it.

abschnitte.text: A **strait** is a narrow waterway between two pieces of land. The **Bosphorus** leads from the **Black Sea** in the north to the **Sea of Marmara** in the south. It is about **30 kilometres** long. At its narrowest point it is only about **700 metres** wide, so you can see across to the other bank easily. Together with the Dardanelles, it links the Black Sea with the Mediterranean.

The Bosphorus is a border between two **continents**: on the west side lies Europe, on the east side Asia. Right on this border lies the city of millions, **Istanbul**. One part of the city lies in Europe, another in Asia. Many people take the ferry every day from one continent to the other, for example to get to work.

Over the Bosphorus run **three large bridges**. They were opened in 1973, 1988 and 2016. Since **2013** the **Marmaray** railway has also run through a tunnel deep beneath the sea bed. It links the railway networks on the European and the Asian sides. Later a road tunnel for cars was added too.

The Greek name **Bosporos** literally means **ox ford**. According to legend, Io, who had been turned into a cow, swam through the sea here. The water in the Bosphorus flows in two directions. Great rivers such as the **Danube** flow into the Black Sea, so its water is less salty. At the **surface** it flows south into the Sea of Marmara, while in the depths saltier water flows north.

gewusst: The Bosphorus is one of the busiest waterways in the world; tens of thousands of ships pass through it every year.
In the Bosphorus the water flows in opposite directions at the top and the bottom.

teile.einleitung: The Barents Sea is a cold marginal sea of the Arctic Ocean. It lies north of Norway and Russia, east of the North Cape.
wichtigste: The Barents Sea lies east of the North Cape.
It is a marginal sea of the Arctic Ocean.
It borders Norway and Russia.
It is named after the navigator Willem Barents.
A branch of the warm North Atlantic Current keeps the south free of ice.

abschnitte.text: The **Barents Sea** lies in the far north of Europe, **east of the North Cape** in Norway. It is a **marginal sea of the Arctic Ocean**. In the south it borders the coasts of **Norway** and **Russia**. In the west and north lie the island group of Svalbard and Franz Josef Land, in the east the long double island of Novaya Zemlya.

The sea is named after the Dutch navigator **Willem Barents**. In the 16th century he looked for a sea route to Asia through the icy sea in the north. On his last voyage his ship got stuck in the ice, and the crew had to spend the winter there.

A branch of the warm **North Atlantic Current** flows into the Barents Sea. That is why its southern part usually stays **free of ice** even in winter, while the north freezes over. The Russian port of **Murmansk** can therefore be reached all year round. The Barents Sea is very rich in fish, especially **cod**. So it is important for the fishing of Norway and Russia.

gewusst: Murmansk on the Barents Sea is one of the largest cities north of the Arctic Circle.

teile.einleitung: Greece lies in the south-east of Europe, on the Mediterranean. It has many islands, plenty of sun and a very long history. In ancient Greece, ideas arose that still shape Europe today, for example the Olympic Games.
wichtigste: The capital of Greece is Athens.
Since 2002 people in Greece have paid with euro coins and euro notes.
The flag is blue and white and has nine stripes.
In 1896 the first modern Olympic Games took place in Athens.
People speak Greek, a language with its own letters.
Olive trees are very common, and olive oil is pressed from their fruit.

abschnitte.text: Greece lies in the **south-east of Europe**. It consists of a mountainous mainland and very many **islands**. The capital is **Athens**. The **flag** is blue and white: it has **nine** horizontal stripes, five blue and four white, and a white cross on a blue square at the top left. Greece belongs to the EU and pays with the **euro**. Since 2002 there have been euro coins and euro notes there.

More than 2000 years ago, Greece was a centre of **science**, art and thought. An early form of **democracy** arose in Athens. On the hill of the **Acropolis**, the remains of ancient temples still stand today. In ancient **Olympia**, sporting contests took place in honour of the gods. This was remembered when the first **modern Olympic Games** took place in Athens in **1896**.

In Greece people speak **Greek**. The language has its own **alphabet** with letters such as alpha, beta and omega. Our word “alphabet” comes from the first two letters. Many words we use come from Greek, for example “telephone”, “mathematics” or “democracy”.

Very many **olive trees** grow in Greece. **Olive oil** is pressed from the olives and is often used in Greek cooking. A Greek salad contains **feta**. This is a white, salty cheese made from **sheep's milk**, often with a little goat's milk. Tomatoes, cucumbers, onions and olives are added.

gewusst: The word “alphabet” comes from alpha and beta, the first Greek letters.
The nine stripes of the flag are often explained by the nine syllables of the Greek motto “Freedom or death”.

teile.einleitung: The City of London is the oldest part of London and one of the most important financial centres in the world. Although it is very small and only a few people live there, hundreds of thousands work here every day.
wichtigste: The City of London is only about 2.9 square kilometres in area.
Because of its size it is called the “Square Mile”.
The Bank of England has its seat there in Threadneedle Street.
In 1986 the financial market was greatly changed in the “Big Bang”.
London is the largest trading centre in the world for foreign currencies.
At the head of the City stands the Lord Mayor, who is newly elected every year.
Fewer than 10,000 people live in the City.

abschnitte.text: The **City of London** is only about **2.9 square kilometres** in area, roughly one square mile. That is why it is also called the **Square Mile**. The Roman city of Londinium already lay here. Today fewer than 10,000 people live in the City. But in the daytime hundreds of thousands of **commuters** come to work. At night and at weekends it is rather quiet by contrast.

In Threadneedle Street stands the **Bank of England**, the central bank of the United Kingdom. It was founded in **1694** and has the nickname “Old Lady of Threadneedle Street”. Also in the City is **Lloyd’s of London**, a famous insurance market. It began in the 17th century in a **coffee house** where ship insurance was traded.

On 27 October 1986, the London financial market was greatly **deregulated** under Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher. This means that many rules were relaxed. It is called the **Big Bang**. Afterwards many foreign banks moved to London, and stock trading increasingly went electronic. Later, in the old dockland areas, the district of **Canary Wharf** arose as London’s second financial centre.

In London more is traded in **foreign currencies** than anywhere else in the world. With **Brexit**, financial firms in London lost so-called **passporting**. This right had allowed them to do business in all EU states with a licence from London. Some firms therefore moved parts of their business into the EU. The City is run by the City of London Corporation. At its head stands the **Lord Mayor**, who must not be confused with the Mayor of the whole of London.

gewusst: The Lord Mayor of the City is newly elected every year and rides in a golden coach in a big procession.
The insurance market Lloyd’s began in a coffee house.

teile.einleitung: The term Gaeltacht refers to the areas in Ireland where Irish is still an everyday language. There families, schools and shops use Irish in daily life. Most of these areas lie on the west coast.
wichtigste: Gaeltacht is the name of an area in Ireland where Irish is spoken in daily life.
The Gaeltacht lies mainly on the west coast, for example in Donegal and Galway.
Irish is a Celtic language.
Irish is, alongside English, an official language of Ireland.
In the rest of Ireland people mostly speak English in daily life.

abschnitte.text: The word **Gaeltacht** refers to the regions of Ireland where **Irish** is still the language of everyday life. The largest areas lie on the **west coast**, for example in the counties of **Donegal**, **Galway** and **Kerry**. They also include islands such as the **Aran Islands**. In these regions Irish is spoken in families, in schools and in church.

Irish is one of the **Celtic languages** and is related to Scottish Gaelic. Over the centuries English pushed the Irish language back more and more. Today, according to the constitution, Irish is the first **official language** of Ireland and English the second. All children in Ireland learn Irish at school. In daily life, though, most people outside the Gaeltacht speak English.

The state supports the Gaeltacht so that the language does not disappear. There are Irish-language radio and television stations. In summer many young people from all over Ireland travel to the Gaeltacht to practise Irish in language courses. Like **Romansh** in the Grisons, Irish is a language that only a few still speak daily and that is therefore looked after with special care.

gewusst: Many place signs in the Gaeltacht are written only in Irish.
Irish is also an official language of the European Union.

teile.einleitung: The Rock of Gibraltar rises steeply out of the sea at the very south of the Iberian Peninsula. It lies on the strait between Europe and Africa and belongs to the United Kingdom.
wichtigste: Gibraltar lies in the south of Spain, but belongs to the United Kingdom.
The Rock is about 426 metres high and consists of limestone.
Barbary macaques live on the Rock, the only free-living monkeys in Europe.
The Strait of Gibraltar connects the Atlantic and the Mediterranean.
Opposite lies Morocco, only about 14 kilometres away at the narrowest point.
The ancient Greeks called the rocks here the Pillars of Hercules.

abschnitte.titel: A piece of the United Kingdom
abschnitte.text: **Gibraltar** lies at the southern tip of Spain, but belongs to the **United Kingdom**. It is a British **overseas territory**. That is why **English** is the official language there, and people pay with the Gibraltar pound. Britain has owned Gibraltar since the early 18th century. Spain would like the territory back, and talks about this continue to this day.

The Rock of Gibraltar is about **426 metres** high and rises steeply out of the sea. It consists of **limestone**. In this rock **caves** form easily, for example the stalactite cave **St Michael’s Cave**. In addition, soldiers once dug many kilometres of **tunnels** into the Rock. On clear days you can see as far as Africa from the top.

**Barbary macaques** live on the Rock. They are the only free-living **monkeys in Europe**. Originally Barbary macaques come from North Africa. The animals are used to people and sometimes climb on cars or snatch food. Feeding them is forbidden, because it harms the monkeys.

abschnitte.titel: Between two seas and two continents
abschnitte.text: The **Strait of Gibraltar** is a narrow stretch of sea. It connects the **Atlantic** with the **Mediterranean**. Opposite, in Africa, lies **Morocco**. At the narrowest point Europe and Africa are only about **14 kilometres** apart. The ancient Greeks called the rocks on both sides of the strait the **Pillars of Hercules**, and they were seen as the end of the world as it was then known.

gewusst: The road to Gibraltar airport crosses the runway, so it is closed whenever a plane lands or takes off.
Very many ships pass through the Strait of Gibraltar every day, and it is one of the most important sea routes in the world.

teile.einleitung: Gjirokastra is an old town in the south of Albania. It lies on a mountainside and is known for its houses made of grey stone. That is why it is also called the “City of Stone”.
wichtigste: Gjirokastra lies in the south of Albania.
The houses are built of grey stone and roofed with stone slabs.
That is why Gjirokastra is also called the “City of Stone”.
The old town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
A large castle towers above the town.

abschnitte.text: **Gjirokastra** lies in a valley in the **south of Albania**, on the slopes of a mountain. The old houses are built of **grey stone**. The roofs are also covered with flat **stone slabs**. That is why Gjirokastra is called the “City of Stone”. Many houses are built tall and narrow like small towers, with thick walls and small windows in the lower part.

High above the town stands a large **castle**. Most of the typical stone houses were built when the region belonged to the **Ottoman Empire** for a long time. The old town is well preserved and was therefore added to the **UNESCO World Heritage** list, together with the town of Berat. The famous Albanian writer **Ismail Kadare** was also born in Gjirokastra.

A big **folk music festival** takes place in Gjirokastra regularly. Groups from all over Albania show songs, dances and traditional costumes there. The polyphonic folk singing of southern Albania is especially well known. Today many tourists visit the steep, cobbled lanes of the old town.

gewusst: In Gjirokastra even the roofs are made of stone.
Albania's polyphonic folk singing is protected by UNESCO as intangible cultural heritage.

teile.einleitung: Luxembourg is small, but it is one of the most important financial centres in Europe. The country is especially well known for investment funds and as the home of several European financial institutions.
wichtigste: Luxembourg is the largest fund centre in Europe and number two in the world after the USA.
The European Investment Bank has its seat in Luxembourg.
The European Stability Mechanism (ESM) is also based in Luxembourg.
In 2007 the EIB issued the world’s first green bond.
Since 2015 Luxembourg has exchanged account data automatically with other EU states.
Almost half of the workers are cross-border commuters from the neighbouring countries.

abschnitte.text: An **investment fund** collects money from many investors and invests it together, for example in shares. In Luxembourg, funds with assets of several thousand billion euros are managed. That makes Luxembourg the **largest fund centre in Europe** and number two in the world after the USA. Important for this are the EU rules for **UCITS** (in German, OGAW). A UCITS fund approved in one EU country may be sold in all member states with this “EU passport”.

The **European Investment Bank** (EIB) has its seat in Luxembourg. It grants long-term loans for projects in the interest of the EU, for example for transport or the environment. The ECB, by contrast, is in Frankfurt, and the Bank for International Settlements in **Basel**. The **European Stability Mechanism** (ESM) is also based in Luxembourg. It was founded in 2012 as a rescue fund for the eurozone and gives loans to countries in financial trouble in return for reform conditions.

A **bond** is a security with which a state or a bank borrows money. In 2007 the EIB issued the “Climate Awareness Bond”, which is regarded as the world’s first **green bond**. The money is used for climate and environmental projects. The bond was listed on the **Luxembourg Stock Exchange**. The exchange now runs its own platform for sustainable bonds.

For a long time Luxembourg was known for strict **banking secrecy**. Under international pressure it took part in the **automatic exchange of information** from **2015**. Since then banks report the account data of customers from other EU states to their tax authorities. In this way banking secrecy towards foreign tax authorities was largely given up. **Switzerland** also adopted this standard from 2017.

Almost half of the workers in Luxembourg are **cross-border commuters**. Every day over 200,000 people travel to work from France, Belgium and Germany. Because they work there but are not counted as residents, the **GDP per head** is especially high. From **1921** Luxembourg formed an economic and monetary union with **Belgium**. The Belgian franc was also used in Luxembourg until the euro arrived in 2002.

gewusst: The world’s first green bond came in 2007 from the European Investment Bank in Luxembourg.
In Switzerland too there are many cross-border commuters, for example in Geneva, Basel and Ticino.

teile.einleitung: The Durmitor is a mountain range in the north of Montenegro. It is a national park with high limestone peaks, deep gorges and clear glacial lakes.
wichtigste: The Durmitor lies in the north of **Montenegro**.
It is a **national park** and part of the UNESCO World Heritage.
In the mountains there are many **glacial lakes**, for example the **Black Lake**.
On the edge of the national park lies the deep **Tara Gorge**.
The town of **Žabljak** is the starting point for hikes.

abschnitte.text: The Durmitor belongs to the Dinaric Alps and consists mainly of **limestone**. It has many peaks over 2,000 metres. The highest is **Bobotov Kuk** at a good 2,500 metres. In winter there is a lot of snow, so the Durmitor is also a ski area. At the foot of the mountains lies the town of **Žabljak**, one of the highest-lying towns in the Balkans.

In the ice age there were large glaciers in the Durmitor. When they melted, hollows were left that filled with water. This is how many **glacial lakes** formed. In Montenegro they are also called “mountain eyes”. The best known is the **Black Lake** near Žabljak, surrounded by dark coniferous forest.

Since 1952 the Durmitor has been a **national park**, and since 1980 it has been part of the **UNESCO World Heritage**. The area also includes part of the **Tara Gorge**, one of the deepest gorges in Europe. In the forests live, among others, bears, wolves and chamois. In summer many people come for hiking and for boat trips on the Tara.

gewusst: Across the Tara Gorge runs a large arch bridge, the Đurđevića Tara Bridge.
Montenegro means “black mountain” in translation.

teile.einleitung: Lake Thun is a large pre-Alpine lake in the Bernese Oberland. The Aare flows through it, and around the lake stand castles, villages and high mountains such as the pyramid-shaped Niesen. With its blue water and the view of the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau, it is one of the most beautiful lakes in Switzerland.
wichtigste: Lake Thun lies in the canton of Bern at about 558 metres above sea level.
It is about 48 square kilometres in area and up to 217 metres deep.
The Aare flows first through Lake Brienz and then through Lake Thun.
Between the two lakes lies the city of Interlaken.
On the south shore rises the pyramid-shaped Niesen.
On the shore stand well-known castles such as Oberhofen and Spiez.
The International Ski and Snowboard Federation FIS has its seat in Oberhofen.

abschnitte.text: Lake Thun is about 17 kilometres long and lies between **Thun** in the north-west and **Interlaken** in the south-east. The **Aare** comes from Lake Brienz, flows into Lake Thun and leaves it again at Thun. Since 1714 the Kander has also been led into Lake Thun. Before that it flowed past Thun and often caused floods there.

On the south shore stands the **Niesen**, a 2,362-metre mountain with an almost perfect pyramid shape. A funicular leads up it, and beside it lies the longest staircase in the world with over 11,000 steps. On the north shore lies the Niederhorn, and across the lake you can see the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau in good weather. This backdrop makes the lake popular with visitors from all over the world.

Several **castles** stand on Lake Thun. Oberhofen Castle has a small tower that stands directly in the water. Spiez Castle lies on a rock above a bay with vineyards. In Thun the castle with its four corner towers sits high above the old town.

On the lake, BLS passenger ships run between Thun, Spiez and Interlaken. A special ship is the **paddle steamer** Blüemlisalp from 1906. It is driven by a steam engine that turns large paddle wheels. Many visitors also travel on it to the St Beatus Caves on the north shore.

The **St Beatus Caves** are dripstone caves high above the north shore. According to legend, the monk Beatus lived there in the early Middle Ages and is said to have driven a dragon out of the cave. Today you can visit part of the caves. Inside there are underground streams and many **dripstones**.

begriffe.erklaerung: A lake on the edge of the Alps, usually carved out by glaciers.
A ship with a steam engine that is driven by large paddle wheels.
A column or cone of limestone that grows in caves from dripping water.
The building of a tunnel in 1714 that led the Kander into Lake Thun.

gewusst: Beside the Niesen funicular lies a service staircase with 11,674 steps, which counts as the longest staircase in the world.
Because the Kander was diverted, a large delta of gravel has formed where it enters Lake Thun.
After the ice age, Lake Thun and Lake Brienz were once a single large lake.

teile.einleitung: Lake Murten is a small lake on the Swiss Central Plateau between the cantons of Fribourg and Vaud. On its shore lies the medieval little town of Murten with its well-preserved town wall. Here, in 1476, one of the most famous battles in Swiss history took place.
wichtigste: Lake Murten is about 23 square kilometres in area and up to 45 metres deep.
It is one of the Jura lakes, together with Lake Neuchâtel and Lake Biel.
On the east shore lies the little town of Murten with a town wall you can walk on.
In 1476 the Confederates defeated Charles the Bold of Burgundy at Murten.
The Broye Canal links Lake Murten with Lake Neuchâtel.
On the north shore rises the Mont Vully with vineyards.
In Lake Murten lives the wels catfish, one of the largest freshwater fish in Europe.

abschnitte.text: Lake Murten lies at about 429 metres above sea level in the **Seeland**. It is about 8 kilometres long and at most 45 metres deep. The Broye flows into the lake from the south and leaves it again as the **Broye Canal** towards Lake Neuchâtel. The language border runs through the area, which is why the lake is called Lac de Morat in French.

Murten was founded in the Middle Ages by the Dukes of Zähringen. The old town has arcades and an almost completely preserved **town wall** that you can walk on. From the top you look over the roofs to the lake. In Murten people speak German and French.

On 22 June 1476, **Charles the Bold**, Duke of Burgundy, attacked Murten with his army. The **Confederates** came to the aid of the besieged town and defeated the Burgundians crushingly. Many Burgundian soldiers fled into the lake and drowned. The battle belongs to the Burgundian Wars, which Charles the Bold finally lost.

On the north shore rises **Mont Vully**, a hill with vineyards. In the Iron Age a fortified Celtic settlement, a so-called **oppidum**, stood on it. There archaeologists found a layer of burning from the time when the Helvetii set out in 58 BC. Today vines grow on its slopes, from which Vully wine is made.

In Lake Murten lives the **wels catfish**, a predatory fish with long barbels that can grow to over 2 metres long. There are also pike, perch and whitefish. In the past, a red alga, the Burgundian blood alga, sometimes turned the water reddish. A legend said that this was the blood of the Burgundians from 1476.

begriffe.erklaerung: A large Celtic settlement fortified with walls.
The name for the members of the old Swiss alliance.
The flat landscape around Lake Biel, Lake Neuchâtel and Lake Murten.
A large freshwater fish with a broad mouth and long barbels.

gewusst: At the national exhibition Expo.02, a giant rusty cube, the Monolith, stood in the middle of Lake Murten.
After the battle in 1476 an ossuary was built with the bones of the fallen; today an obelisk commemorates it.
The town wall of Murten is so well preserved that you can still walk on it almost all the way round the old town today.

teile.einleitung: The Balkan Peninsula is a large peninsula in south-eastern Europe. It is surrounded by several seas, and on it lie many countries with a long and eventful history.
wichtigste: The Balkan Peninsula lies in south-eastern Europe.
It is named after the Balkan Mountains in Bulgaria.
In the east it is bounded by the Black Sea.
In the west lies the Adriatic, in the south the Mediterranean with the Aegean.
The rivers Danube and Sava are often given as the northern boundary.

abschnitte.text: The peninsula is named after the **Balkan Mountains**, which run across **Bulgaria**. The word Balkan comes from Turkish and means roughly “mountain range”. The whole peninsula is very mountainous. Besides the Balkan Mountains there are, for example, the Dinaric Alps on the Adriatic and the Pindus Mountains in Greece.

In the east the Balkan Peninsula borders the **Black Sea**. In the west lie the **Adriatic** and the Ionian Sea, in the south the Mediterranean with the **Aegean**. In the north there is no coast. The rivers **Danube** and **Sava** are often given as the **northern boundary**. But the boundary is not defined in the same way everywhere.

On the Balkan Peninsula lie, wholly or partly, countries such as **Greece**, **Albania**, **Bulgaria**, North Macedonia, Montenegro, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Serbia and Croatia. The European part of **Turkey** with Istanbul also belongs to it. Many peoples with different languages and religions live in the region. Many people from these countries also live in **Switzerland** today.

gewusst: The Olympic Games began in ancient Greece, on the Balkan Peninsula.
On its way to the Black Sea, the Danube flows along the northern boundary of the peninsula.

teile.einleitung: Denmark is a small kingdom in the north of Europe. It consists of the peninsula of Jutland and many islands, and the capital is Copenhagen.
wichtigste: On land, Denmark borders only **Germany**.
Part of the country lies on the peninsula of **Jutland**, and there are also many islands.
The landscape is **very flat**; the highest point is only about 170 metres high.
Since 2024 **Frederik X** has been King of Denmark (as of 2026).
**Greenland** and the Faroe Islands also belong to the kingdom.
People pay with the **Danish krone**, and a lot of electricity comes from **wind power**.

abschnitte.text: Denmark lies between the North Sea and the Baltic Sea. Most of the mainland is the peninsula of **Jutland**. In the south it borders **Germany**, the only neighbouring country on land. There are also many islands, the largest being Zealand and Funen. On Zealand lies the capital **Copenhagen**. The **Øresund Bridge** links Denmark with Sweden.

Denmark is **very flat**. The highest natural point is only about 170 metres high, so much lower than the Uetliberg near Zurich. Large parts of the country are used for farming. Because the wind blows almost all the time, Denmark gets a very large part of its electricity from **wind power**. Many wind turbines also stand in the sea.

Denmark is a **monarchy** with a parliament. Since January 2024 **Frederik X** has been king (as of 2026). He followed his mother Margrethe II, who had stepped down. The huge island of **Greenland** and the Faroe Islands in the Atlantic also belong to the kingdom. Both manage many matters themselves.

The Danish flag is called the **Dannebrog**. It shows a white cross on a red background and is regarded as one of the oldest national flags in the world. Denmark is a member of the EU but has not introduced the euro. People pay with the **Danish krone**. Switzerland too has kept its own currency, the franc.

gewusst: LEGO bricks were invented in Denmark, and the company has its seat in Billund.
No place in Denmark is more than about 50 kilometres from the sea.

teile.einleitung: France is the western neighbour of Switzerland and one of the largest countries in Europe. It is known for Paris, good food, high mountains and long coasts. French is also one of the four national languages of Switzerland.
wichtigste: The capital of France is Paris.
Mont Blanc, at about 4,800 metres, is the highest mountain in France and in the Alps.
France celebrates its national day on 14 July.
The Gallic rooster is a well-known symbol of the country.
Switzerland and France share Lake Geneva.
In France people pay with the euro.

abschnitte.text: In area, France is the **largest country in the European Union**. It borders the Atlantic, the English Channel and the Mediterranean. In the east lie the **Alps** and the **Jura**, in the south the **Pyrenees**. The capital **Paris** lies on the Seine and is famous for the Eiffel Tower. France also includes territories far away, for example islands in the Caribbean and in the Indian Ocean.

The flag, the **tricolour**, is blue, white and red. The motto is “Liberté, Égalité, Fraternité”, that is, liberty, equality, fraternity. An old symbol is the **Gallic rooster**, which you often see on the shirts of sports teams. On **14 July** France celebrates its national day with parades and fireworks. It recalls the storming of the Bastille in 1789, the beginning of the **French Revolution**.

abschnitte.titel: Mountains and lakes on the border
abschnitte.text: **Mont Blanc** is about 4,800 metres high and the highest mountain in the Alps. It lies on the border with Italy, not far from Switzerland. The two countries share **Lake Geneva**: the south shore belongs to France, the north shore to Switzerland. In French it is called “Lac Léman”. The Doubs and the Jura also form a stretch of the shared border.

Typical of France is the **baguette**, a long, narrow white loaf with a crispy crust. Many people buy it fresh every day at the baker’s. France is also known for many kinds of **cheese**, for wine and for pastries such as croissants. In France people pay with the **euro**. The national language is French, which is also spoken in **French-speaking Switzerland**.

gewusst: Paris is one of the most visited cities in the world.
Switzerland celebrates its national day on 1 August, and France a good two weeks earlier on 14 July.

teile.einleitung: A fjord is a long, narrow bay of the sea that reaches far inland. Especially many famous fjords are found in Norway, where they lie between high, steep mountains.
wichtigste: A fjord is a long, narrow arm of the sea between mountains.
Fjords were shaped by glaciers in the Ice Age.
Because a fjord is connected to the sea, its water is salty.
The longest fjord in Norway is the Sognefjord at about 200 kilometres.
The Geirangerfjord has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2005.
At its mouth a fjord is often less deep, because a sill lies there.

abschnitte.text: A **fjord** is a long, narrow **arm of the sea** that reaches far inland. Often it lies between high mountains. Because it is connected to the open sea, its water is **salt water**. The shores often drop almost vertically into the water as **steep rock walls**. Sometimes **waterfalls** plunge down over the rocks.

Fjords were shaped long ago by **glaciers**. In the **Ice Age**, huge streams of ice carved out deep valleys. When the ice melted, the sea level rose, and **sea water** flowed into these valleys. Further inland the glacier dug deepest, and at the end it lost strength. At the mouth a **sill** of rock and moraine debris therefore often remained, which is why a fjord is less deep there than further in.

The west coast of **Norway** is full of fjords. The longest is the **Sognefjord** at about **200 kilometres**. It is also very deep, in some places over a thousand metres. Very well known is the **Geirangerfjord**. In **2005** it was added, together with the Nærøyfjord, to the **UNESCO World Heritage** list.

At the Geirangerfjord, several waterfalls plunge side by side down a high rock wall. They are called the **Seven Sisters**. Many tourists visit the fjord by **ship** to see the waterfalls and the steep shores up close. On some slopes there are old farms that used to be hard to reach. Today the fjords are among the best-known sights in Norway.

Fjords are not only found in Norway. You also find them in **Greenland**, **Iceland**, **Scotland**, **Canada**, **Chile** and **New Zealand**. Everywhere there, large glaciers lay close to the sea in the Ice Age. **Switzerland** has no fjords, because it has no sea. But many Swiss lakes, for example in the Alpine valleys, were also carved out by glaciers.

gewusst: The word “fjord” comes from Norwegian and is used in many languages.
At its deepest point the Sognefjord is over a thousand metres deep, much deeper than the sea in front of its mouth.

teile.einleitung: Bratislava is the capital of Slovakia and lies on the Danube. The city has a special location: it borders two other states at once.
wichtigste: Bratislava is the capital of Slovakia.
The city lies on the Danube.
In German it used to be called Pressburg.
Bratislava borders Austria and Hungary.
The castle with four corner towers looks like an upturned table.
The UFO Bridge has a round restaurant at the top of its pylon.

abschnitte.text: **Bratislava** lies in the south-west of Slovakia on the **Danube**. The city borders directly on **Austria** and on **Hungary**. This is unique among capitals. It is only about 60 kilometres to Vienna, so the two are regarded as the capitals lying closest together in Europe. Bratislava has been the capital of a state of its own since 1993, when Czechoslovakia split peacefully into two countries.

In German the city used to be called **Pressburg**, in Hungarian Pozsony. For a long time it belonged to the Kingdom of **Hungary**. After 1563, the Hungarian kings and queens were crowned in **St Martin’s Cathedral** for about 250 years. That is why Bratislava is also called the coronation city. In the old town, small crowns in the street paving still recall this time.

High above the Danube stands **Bratislava Castle**. It is a large rectangular building with **four corner towers**. From a distance it looks like an **upturned table**, which is why it is often described that way. The castle was rebuilt several times and rebuilt again after a fire in the 20th century. Today it houses exhibitions on history, among other things.

A modern landmark is the **UFO Bridge** over the Danube, which opened in 1972. On its tall pylon sits a round **restaurant** that looks like a flying saucer. From there you have a wide view over the city. In the old town there are also funny bronze statues, for example a worker peeping out of a manhole.

gewusst: Bratislava is the only capital in the world that borders two other states.
The bronze figure Čumil peeps out of a manhole in the old town and is a popular photo spot.

teile.einleitung: The “Blue Banana” is a term from geography. It describes a curved strip in Europe in which especially many people live and work and a great deal of the economy is concentrated.
wichtigste: The Blue Banana is a densely populated economic area in Europe.
It stretches from north-west England to northern Italy.
The French geographer Roger Brunet coined the image in 1989.
The Rhine is an important transport axis in this area.
Basel with its Rhine port and the Ruhr area lie within it.
Milan forms its southern end.
Paris lies outside the Blue Banana.

abschnitte.text: The **Blue Banana** is an arc-shaped belt across Europe. Here many large cities, industrial areas and important transport routes lie close together. This is called an **economic area**. On the map it looks like a curved strip, hence the name banana. The blue colour probably recalls the European flag.

The Blue Banana begins in **north-west England** around Manchester and reaches over London, the **Benelux countries** and the Rhine region to **Milan**. On the way lie cities such as Brussels, Amsterdam, Cologne and Frankfurt. The **Ruhr area**, one of the largest urban areas in Europe, also belongs to it. In the past, coal and steel shaped the region there. Milan is the industrial and financial centre of northern Italy and forms the southern end.

The **Rhine** is one of the busiest waterways in the world. On its banks lie many factories and cities. Switzerland also lies in the Blue Banana. **Basel** has the Swiss Rhine ports: from there ships sail to the North Sea. So, despite having no sea coast, Switzerland is linked to the great seaports.

In **1989** the French geographer **Roger Brunet** and his research group studied the cities of Europe. The commission came from the French regional planning authority **DATAR**. A newspaper article then made the name Blue Banana known. In France the study caused a stir: **Paris** lies outside the strip to the west. This was understood as a warning sign that France could be cut off from the economic core of Europe.

gewusst: The Blue Banana is not an official area with borders but an image for describing Europe’s economy.
From Basel, ships can sail along the Rhine to the North Sea.

teile.einleitung: Brussels is the capital of Belgium. Important parts of the European Union and NATO work here, which is why Brussels is often also called the capital of Europe.
wichtigste: Brussels is the capital of Belgium.
The official languages are French and Dutch.
The European Commission has its headquarters in the Berlaymont building.
NATO also has its headquarters in Brussels.
The Atomium was built in 1958 for a world fair.
Every two years a huge carpet of flowers is laid on the Grand-Place.
Brussels is regarded as the city of comics.

abschnitte.text: **Brussels** is the capital of **Belgium**. The king also has his palace here. In the city, **French** and **Dutch** are official languages. That is why street signs are mostly bilingual. In everyday life you hear French most, but also many other languages, because people from all over the world live in Brussels.

In Brussels, important parts of the **European Union** work. The **European Commission** has its headquarters in the star-shaped **Berlaymont building** in the European Quarter. The Council of the EU also meets in Brussels. In addition, the military alliance **NATO** has its headquarters here. That is why Brussels is an important place of international politics, like Geneva in Switzerland with its many international organisations.

The **Atomium** was built in 1958 for a **world fair**. It consists of huge shiny spheres and shows a tiny building block of iron, enlarged many billions of times. The **Grand-Place** is the magnificent main square with old **guildhouses** and the town hall. In August, every two years, a **carpet of flowers** made of many thousands of blooms is laid out there. Right next to the Atomium, the park **Mini-Europe** shows well-known buildings of Europe as small models.

Brussels is regarded as the **city of comics**. Well-known characters such as Tintin and Snowy come from Belgium. On many house walls, large pictures of comic characters are painted. Also very famous is the **Manneken Pis**, a bronze fountain figure of a small boy only about 60 centimetres tall. He owns more than 900 **costumes**, which he wears in turn. Brussels is also known for waffles, chocolate and chips.

gewusst: The Atomium has nine spheres, like part of an iron crystal, only many billions of times larger.
The Manneken Pis has a wardrobe of his own with more than 900 costumes from all over the world.

teile.einleitung: A tidal power station produces electricity from high and low tide. The sea water flows through turbines into a bay and back out again. A well-known example has stood in France since 1966, at the mouth of the Rance.
wichtigste: A tidal power station uses high and low tide to generate electricity.
The flowing water drives turbines.
