The power station on the Rance in Brittany opened in 1966.
It was the largest tidal power station in the world until 2011.
Tidal power stations are only worthwhile where the tidal range is very large.

abschnitte.text: A **tidal power station** uses **high and low tide**. Usually a bay or river mouth is closed off with a **dam**. At high tide, water flows through openings in the dam into the bay, and at low tide it flows out again. As it does so, it drives **turbines** that produce electricity. Because high and low tide come very regularly, it is easy to predict when how much electricity will be produced.

abschnitte.titel: The power station on the Rance
abschnitte.text: In **Brittany**, near **Saint-Malo**, stands the tidal power station on the **Rance**. It opened in **1966** and was the largest tidal power station in the world until **2011**, when one in South Korea became bigger. The place was chosen because the **tidal range** is very large there: the difference between low and high tide can be more than 12 metres. A road also runs across the dam.

Tidal power stations supply **renewable energy** and give off no CO₂ when they are running. But there are only a few places in the world with a large enough tidal range. Building one is expensive, and a dam changes the **nature** in the bay, for example for fish and birds. Switzerland has no sea, but here **hydroelectric power stations** on rivers and reservoirs produce a large share of the electricity.

gewusst: The power station on the Rance has been running for over 50 years.
The greater the tidal range, the more electricity a tidal power station can produce.

teile.einleitung: Lake Lucerne is a branching lake in Central Switzerland, surrounded by steep mountains. It is named after the four forest cantons of Uri, Schwyz, Unterwalden and Lucerne. On its shore lies the Rütli, the famous meadow from the founding story of Switzerland.
wichtigste: Lake Lucerne is about 114 square kilometres in area and up to 214 metres deep.
It is named after the four forest cantons of Uri, Schwyz, Unterwalden and Lucerne.
On Lake Uri lies the Rütli, where the Rütli Oath is said to have taken place.
Lucerne joined the alliance of the Confederates in 1332 as the fourth member.
The Reuss flows into the lake at Flüelen and leaves it at Lucerne.
Several historic paddle steamers still sail on the lake today.
The Rigi, Pilatus and Bürgenstock rise around the lake.

abschnitte.text: Lake Lucerne lies at about 434 metres above sea level and borders the cantons of **Lucerne**, **Uri**, **Schwyz**, Nidwalden and Obwalden. It has many arms, such as Lake Uri, Lake Küssnacht and Lake Alpnach. That is why it looks on the map like a cross with many branches. The **Reuss** flows into the lake at Flüelen and leaves it in the city of Lucerne.

On the shore of Lake Uri lies the **Rütli**, a meadow above the lake. There, according to tradition, representatives of Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden met for the **Rütli Oath**. The Federal Charter, on which the national holiday is based, dates from 1291. Lucerne joined the alliance in 1332 as the fourth member.

On Lake Uri also lies the **Tell’s Platform**, a rock ledge on the shore with a chapel. According to legend, William Tell leapt here from the boat of the bailiff Gessler during a storm and escaped. He is then said to have met Gessler in the Hollow Lane near Küssnacht. Friedrich Schiller made the story famous with his play William Tell.

The shipping company of Lake Lucerne runs five historic **paddle steamers**, for example the Uri from 1901. The ships are driven by steam engines that turn large paddle wheels. This gives the lake one of the largest paddle steamer fleets in Europe. You can travel by ship from Lucerne all the way to Flüelen.

Around the lake stand well-known viewpoint mountains. Up the **Rigi** runs the first mountain railway in Europe, a cog railway, since 1871. Up Pilatus runs the steepest cog railway in the world. At the Bürgenstock there is the Hammetschwand Lift, an outdoor lift on a rock face.

begriffe.erklaerung: The places Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden, and later Lucerne, that lie on the lake.
A legendary oath with which the first Confederates promised each other help.
A ship with a steam engine and large paddle wheels at the sides.
A warm, often stormy wind falling from the Alps, which can make the lake dangerous.

gewusst: The Rütli belongs to the Swiss Society for the Common Good, which bought it in 1859 with donations from schoolchildren.
In a foehn storm, Lake Uri can become so wild that ships are not allowed to sail.
The Chapel Bridge in Lucerne crosses the Reuss exactly where it leaves the lake.

teile.einleitung: Many great rivers flow through Europe. They have always been important for trade, shipping and cities, and some of the greatest rise in Switzerland.
wichtigste: The longest river in Europe is the Volga, the second longest the Danube.
The Danube is about 2,850 kilometres long.
The Po, at about 650 kilometres, is the longest river in Italy.
The Oder and the Neisse form the greater part of the border between Germany and Poland.
The Main-Danube Canal has connected the Rhine and the Danube since 1992.
The Rhine and the Rhône rise in the Swiss Alps.

abschnitte.text: The longest river in Europe is the **Volga** in Russia. It flows into the Caspian Sea. The second longest is the **Danube** at about **2,850 kilometres**. It rises in the Black Forest in Germany and flows through many countries to the **Black Sea**. Cities such as Vienna, Budapest and Belgrade lie on the Danube.

Switzerland is often called the **water tower of Europe**. The **Rhine** rises in the Grisons and flows all the way to the **North Sea**. The **Rhône** comes from the Rhône Glacier in Valais, flows through Lake Geneva and on to the **Mediterranean**. The **Inn** flows from the Engadine into the Danube, and the **Ticino** flows into the **Po**. In this way water from Switzerland reaches several seas.

The **Oder** rises in the Czech Republic and flows through Poland. On its lower course it forms, together with the **Lusatian Neisse**, the greater part of the border between Germany and Poland. The **Meuse**, in Dutch the Maas, flows through France, Belgium and the Netherlands and, together with the Rhine, ends in the North Sea. The **Garonne** rises in the Pyrenees and flows through Toulouse and the wine city of **Bordeaux**. After that it flows into the Gironde.

The **Po**, at about **650 kilometres**, is the longest river in Italy. It flows through the fertile **Po Plain** and ends in the **Adriatic**. The **Don** flows through the south of Russia. At Rostov-on-Don it flows into the **Sea of Azov**. Both rivers are important for the agriculture of their surroundings.

Many rivers are important **waterways** for ships. Since **1992** the **Main-Danube Canal** has connected the Main near Bamberg with the Danube near Kelheim. Because the Main flows into the Rhine, the river systems of the **Rhine** and the **Danube** are thereby connected. Ships can thus travel from the North Sea to the Black Sea. Basel too, thanks to the Rhine, has a port with a connection to the sea.

gewusst: Depending on which side it lands on, a raindrop in the Swiss Alps can end up in the North Sea, the Mediterranean or the Black Sea.
The Danube flows through more countries than any other river in the world.

teile.einleitung: Brittany is a peninsula and region in the north-west of France. It has its own Celtic language, a long coast and ancient stone monuments.
wichtigste: Brittany lies in the north-west of France between the English Channel and the Atlantic.
The capital of the region is Rennes.
Breton is a Celtic language.
At Carnac stand about 3,000 menhirs in long rows.
On the Rance, a tidal power station has stood since 1966.
Finistère means “end of the earth”.
The galette is a pancake made from buckwheat flour.

abschnitte.text: **Brittany** juts out into the **Atlantic** like a nose. In the north lies the English Channel. The coast is long and rocky and has many bays, islands and lighthouses. The capital of the region is **Rennes**, which is also the largest city. The westernmost part is called **Finistère**, from the Latin “finis terrae”, which means **end of the earth**.

In Brittany, besides French, people partly also speak **Breton**. This language belongs to the **Celtic languages**. It is closely related to Welsh and Cornish. It came to Brittany long ago with immigrants from Britain. Today there are schools in which children learn in Breton, and many place signs are bilingual.

At **Carnac** stand about **3,000** upright stones in long rows. Such stones are called **menhirs**. They were set up in the **Neolithic**, many thousands of years ago. What exactly they were for is still not known for certain. The rows of stones are among the best-known stone monuments in the world.

On the coast of Brittany the difference between **low tide** and **high tide** is very large. The **tidal power station** at the mouth of the Rance, which went into operation in 1966, makes use of this. It was the first large tidal power station in the world. Brittany is also known for its food: the savoury **galette** is a thin pancake made from **buckwheat flour**, often with ham, cheese and egg. Sweet crêpes and cider belong to it as well.

gewusst: The flag of Brittany is striped black and white and is called “Gwenn ha Du” in Breton, meaning white and black.
The tidal power station on the Rance has been running since 1966.

teile.einleitung: Lake Zurich is a long pre-Alpine lake between the city of Zurich and the Glarus Alps. It was carved out by a glacier in the ice age and today supplies hundreds of thousands of people with drinking water. Densely populated communities lie on its shores, and in Meilen the study of pile dwellings began.
wichtigste: Lake Zurich is about 40 kilometres long, about 88 square kilometres in area and up to 136 metres deep.
It borders the cantons of Zurich, St Gallen and Schwyz.
The Linth flows into the lake, and the Limmat leaves it in the city of Zurich.
The causeway at Rapperswil separates Lake Zurich from the Upper Lake.
The lake was formed when a glacier carved out a basin in the ice age.
In the winter of 1853/54, remains of pile dwellings were discovered in Meilen.
In Roman times Zurich was called Turicum.

abschnitte.text: Lake Zurich lies at about 406 metres above sea level and stretches from **Zurich** in the north-west to the Linth plain in the south-east. It has the shape of a long, slightly curved banana. The shores have nicknames in Zurich: the sunny north-east shore is called the “Goldküste” (Gold Coast) and the shadier south-west shore the “Pfnüselküste” (Sniffle Coast). The **Linth** brings water from the Glarus Alps and Lake Walen, and the **Limmat** flows out of the lake in Zurich.

In the last ice age, the **Linth Glacier** reached beyond Zurich. It carved out the deep basin in which the lake lies today. When the ice melted about 15,000 years ago, a **moraine** was left behind, a ridge of rubble. This ridge dammed the water, and so Lake Zurich was formed, like many other lakes on the Central Plateau.

Between **Rapperswil** and Hurden, a causeway crosses the lake, carrying road and railway. The part east of it is called the Upper Lake. Beside the causeway runs a long wooden footbridge for pedestrians, which recalls an old pilgrims’ path to Einsiedeln. In the lake lie the islands of **Ufenau** and Lützelau; the Ufenau belongs to the monastery of Einsiedeln.

In the dry winter of 1853/54, the water level fell sharply. In **Meilen**, wooden piles, shards and tools from prehistoric times came to light. The Zurich scholar **Ferdinand Keller** described the finds from 1854 and made the pile dwellings world famous. Since then we have known that villages stood on many Swiss lake shores in the Neolithic and the Bronze Age.

abschnitte.titel: Life on and by the lake
abschnitte.text: Many **mute swans**, coots and great crested grebes live on Lake Zurich. The city of Zurich gets a large part of its drinking water from the lake. In summer many people swim in the lakeside baths, and passenger ships sail as far as Rapperswil. Two historic paddle steamers, the Stadt Zürich and the Stadt Rapperswil, are still in service.

begriffe.erklaerung: A ridge of stones and rubble that a glacier leaves behind.
A large river of ice that moves slowly down a valley.
Houses on wooden piles on the shores of lakes or in moors from prehistoric times.
The Latin name of Zurich in Roman times.

gewusst: In very cold winters Lake Zurich has frozen over completely, most recently in 1963, when thousands of people walked on the ice.
Since 2011, the pile dwellings around the Alps have been part of the UNESCO World Heritage.
The wooden footbridge between Rapperswil and Hurden is over 800 metres long.

teile.einleitung: Durrës is a port city in Albania on the Adriatic. It has the country’s most important port and is one of the oldest cities in Albania.
wichtigste: Durrës has the most important **port** in Albania.
The city lies on the **Adriatic**, not far from the capital **Tirana**.
It was founded in ancient times by **Greeks**.
The Romans called it **Dyrrachium**.
In the city stands a large **Roman amphitheatre**.

abschnitte.text: Durrës was founded over 2,500 years ago by **Greeks**. It was then called **Epidamnos**. Later the city belonged to the Roman Empire and was called **Dyrrachium**. Here began the **Via Egnatia**, an important Roman road that led across the Balkans as far as Constantinople. From this time dates the large **amphitheatre**, which once had room for thousands of spectators.

Today Durrës has the most important **port** in Albania. Ferries from Italy arrive here, for example from Bari. Many goods for the whole country are also transferred here. The capital **Tirana** lies only about 35 kilometres away and is linked by a motorway.
South of the city stretches a long **sandy beach**. In summer many holidaymakers come from Albania and abroad. Along the coast stand numerous hotels. Durrës is among the largest cities in Albania.

gewusst: The amphitheatre of Durrës was rediscovered only in the 20th century, because houses had been built over it.

teile.einleitung: The Little Mermaid is a small bronze figure at the harbour of Copenhagen. It is among the best-known sights in Denmark.
wichtigste: The figure sits in **Copenhagen**, the capital of Denmark.
It shows the heroine of a fairy tale by **Hans Christian Andersen**.
It is made of **bronze** and sits on a rock on the shore.
The figure is only about 1.25 metres tall.
It was set up in 1913.

abschnitte.text: The Danish writer **Hans Christian Andersen** wrote the fairy tale “The Little Mermaid” in the 19th century. It tells of a mermaid who gives up her life in the sea because she loves a prince. The fairy tale has a sad ending. It has been translated into many languages and later filmed too, for example as an animated film.

The figure was set up in 1913. The brewer Carl Jacobsen had ordered it, and the sculptor Edvard Eriksen made it of **bronze**. It sits on a rock on the Langelinie promenade and looks out over the water. At about 1.25 metres it is much smaller than many visitors expect.

Every year very many tourists come to photograph the Little Mermaid. Unfortunately the figure has been damaged or sprayed with paint several times. But each time it was repaired. In 2010 it even travelled for a few months to the World Expo in Shanghai.

gewusst: Although she is so small, the Little Mermaid is among the best-known statues in the world.
Her head has already had to be replaced after damage.

teile.einleitung: Demography is concerned with how a population is made up and how it changes. Italy is a particularly interesting example, because its population is getting older and smaller.
wichtigste: In 2024, according to Eurostat, Italy had the highest **median age** in the EU.
In 2024, according to ISTAT, just under 370,000 children were born in Italy.
The birth rate in 2024 was about 1.18 children per woman.
For years more people have died in Italy than have been born.
The **old-age dependency ratio** compares the over-64s with people of working age.
Many young, well-educated people move abroad.

abschnitte.text: The **median age** divides the population into two equal halves: one is younger, the other older. The **birth rate** says how many children a woman has on average. For a population to stay the same size without immigration, about 2.1 children would be needed. The **natural balance** is the number of births minus the number of deaths. If it is negative, more people die than are born.

According to the Italian statistics authority **ISTAT**, just under 370,000 children were born in 2024. That was the lowest figure since the unification of Italy. The birth rate was about 1.18 and is among the lowest in Europe. At the same time people live to a very great age. According to Eurostat, Italy had in 2024 the highest median age of all EU countries.

The **old-age dependency ratio** compares the number of over-64s with the people between 15 and 64. In Italy it is rising sharply. This means: fewer and fewer working people pay, with their contributions, the pensions of more and more older people. This puts a strain on the state budget. Switzerland also knows this question, for example in the financing of the **AVS** (old-age insurance).

Many small villages, above all in the south and in the mountains, are losing inhabitants. Some municipalities sell empty houses for a symbolic **euro** if the buyers renovate them. At the same time many young, well-educated people move abroad. In Italian this is called **“fuga dei cervelli”**, the flight of brains, in English the brain drain.

**Blue Zones** are areas in which especially many people live to a very great age. One of them lies in the mountains of **Sardinia**. There remarkably many centenarians live, including many men. Researchers suspect that exercise, simple food and close families play a part.

gewusst: In Italy more people over 65 live than children and young people under 15.
The houses for one euro have attracted buyers from all over the world to small Italian villages.

teile.einleitung: Belarus, formerly often called White Russia, is a country in Eastern Europe without a sea coast. It is flat and has many forests, lakes and marshes.
wichtigste: Belarus is a landlocked country without a sea coast.
The official languages are Belarusian and Russian.
The landscape is flat with many forests, lakes and marshes.
In the primeval forest of Białowieża lives the European bison.
Belarus was badly affected by the Chernobyl disaster in 1986.
The currency is the Belarusian rouble.

abschnitte.text: **Belarus** lies in **Eastern Europe** between Russia, Ukraine, Poland, Lithuania and Latvia. It is a **landlocked country**, so like Switzerland it has no sea coast. The capital is **Minsk**. Until 1991 Belarus belonged to the Soviet Union. The **official languages** are **Belarusian** and **Russian**, and in everyday life many people speak Russian.

Belarus is very **flat**. The highest point, **Dzyarzhynskaya Hara**, is only about **345 metres** high. The country has many **forests**, **lakes** and **marshes**. In the south lies **Polesia**, a huge area of marsh and forest. The river **Bug** forms part of the border with Poland and flows past the old **Brest Fortress**.

On the border with Poland lies the primeval forest of **Białowieża**, one of the last large lowland primeval forests in Europe. Here lives the **European bison**, the European wisent. It had almost died out in the wild and was reintroduced. The forest is part of the **UNESCO World Heritage**.

In 1986 a reactor exploded in the **Chernobyl** nuclear power plant in what is now Ukraine. The wind carried radioactive material far away. **Belarus** received an especially large share of the **radioactive fallout**. Whole villages in the south were abandoned, and some areas are still closed off today.

People pay with the **Belarusian rouble**. An important natural resource is **potash**, which is mined near the town of **Salihorsk**. It is made into fertiliser for farming. Belarus also makes lorries and tractors and grows many potatoes and cereals.

gewusst: The European bison is the heaviest land mammal in Europe.
In Belarus there are over ten thousand lakes.

teile.einleitung: Estonia is a small country on the Baltic Sea and the northernmost of the three Baltic States. It has a beautiful medieval capital and is regarded as a particularly digital country.
wichtigste: The capital is Tallinn, which used to be called Reval.
Tallinn was an important trading city of the Hanseatic League.
Estonia has about 1.4 million inhabitants (as of 2024).
Lake Peipus forms part of the border with Russia.
The largest island is Saaremaa.
Almost all dealings with the authorities can be done online.

abschnitte.text: The capital **Tallinn** used to be called **Reval**. In the Middle Ages it was an important trading city of the **Hanseatic League**, an alliance of merchant towns around the Baltic Sea and North Sea. City walls, towers and narrow lanes date from this time. The well-preserved old town is part of the **UNESCO World Heritage**. Many tourists come by ship, for example from Helsinki.

Estonia is flat and to a large extent covered with **forest**. In the east lies **Lake Peipus**, one of the largest lakes in Europe. The border between Estonia and Russia runs right through it. Off the west coast lie over a thousand islands. The largest is **Saaremaa** in the Baltic Sea.

In Estonia live only about **1.4 million** people (as of 2024), fewer than in the canton of Zurich. The official language is **Estonian**. It is closely related to Finnish and does not belong to the Indo-European languages like German. Many people also speak Russian or English. Well known are the large **song festivals**, at which thousands sing together.

In 1918 Estonia became an independent state for the first time. In the Second World War it came under the rule of the **Soviet Union**. In 1991 Estonia became independent again. The peaceful path there, with many shared songs, is called the **Singing Revolution**. Since 2004 Estonia has been a member of the EU and NATO, and since 2011 people have paid with the euro.

Estonia is today especially known for its **digital administration**. Almost all dealings with the authorities can be done on the internet. Every person has a digital ID with which they can log in and sign online. In elections you can even vote over the internet. The software **Skype** was also co-developed in Estonia.

gewusst: In Estonia you have been able to vote over the internet in elections since 2005.
The border with Russia runs right through the huge Lake Peipus.

teile.einleitung: Lake Superior is the largest of the five Great Lakes of North America. It lies on the border between the USA and Canada and, measured by area, is the largest freshwater lake in the world. It is so huge that from one shore you cannot see the other.
wichtigste: Lake Superior lies between the USA and Canada.
It is about 82,000 square kilometres in area, so about twice as large as Switzerland.
By area it is the largest freshwater lake in the world.
It is up to about 400 metres deep.
It is the northernmost and westernmost of the five Great Lakes.
Its water flows through the St Marys River into Lake Huron.
Heavy storms can rage on the lake.

abschnitte.text: Lake Superior lies in the north of the USA and the south of Canada. On its shore lie the Canadian province of **Ontario** and the US states of **Minnesota**, Wisconsin and Michigan. It belongs to the **Great Lakes**, together with Lake Michigan, Lake Huron, Lake Erie and Lake Ontario. Its water flows through these lakes and the St Lawrence River to the Atlantic.

The lake is about 560 kilometres long and up to 260 kilometres wide. At about 82,000 square kilometres it is the largest **freshwater lake** on Earth. Only the Caspian Sea is larger, but it contains salt water. Lake Superior holds about a tenth of all the fresh water that lies on the Earth's surface in lakes and rivers.

The shores are often rocky and covered with dense coniferous forests. The water is very clear and cold even in summer. In winter parts of the lake freeze over. In the lake lies the island of **Isle Royale**, a national park where moose and wolves live.

Large cargo ships carry mainly iron ore and grain on the lake. Important ports are **Duluth** in Minnesota and Thunder Bay in Ontario. In autumn storms, waves several metres high can form. In 1975 the big freighter **Edmund Fitzgerald** sank in a storm with its whole crew.

The name comes from the French “Lac Supérieur”, which means “upper lake”, because it lies above the other lakes. The Ojibwe, an Indigenous people, call it Gichigami, which means great water. French traders and missionaries came to the lake in the 17th century. Later, copper and iron ore were mined around the lake.

begriffe.erklaerung: Five large, linked lakes on the border between the USA and Canada.
Water with very little salt, as in rivers and most lakes.
An Indigenous people who have lived around Lake Superior for a long time.
Rock from which iron is obtained.

gewusst: Because the water is so cold, shipwrecks on the bottom of Lake Superior often stay very well preserved.
Lake Superior is almost 150 times as large as Lake Neuchâtel.

teile.einleitung: Banlieue is the French word for the suburbs around a large city. The banlieues of Paris with their large housing estates are especially well known.
wichtigste: Banlieue refers to the belt of suburbs around a large city.
Between 1950 and 1975, large housing estates were built, the “grands ensembles”.
HLM stands for “habitation à loyer modéré”, flats with low rent.
Seine-Saint-Denis is regarded as the poorest département of mainland France.
In 2005, riots across the country began in Clichy-sous-Bois.
The Grand Paris Express is meant to link the suburbs better.

abschnitte.text: The French word **banlieue** refers to the **belt of suburbs** around a large city. Around Paris, far more people live in the banlieues than in the city itself. The ring motorway **Boulevard périphérique** physically separates the city of Paris from the suburbs. There are rich and poor suburbs. In everyday speech, however, many people think of large housing estates on the edge of the city when they hear the word banlieue.

After the Second World War, France lacked many homes. Especially between **1950 and 1975**, huge estates with tall blocks of flats were therefore built, the **grands ensembles**. Many flats are **HLM**, which stands for **habitation à loyer modéré**, that is, a flat with a moderate rent. At first the modern flats counted as progress. Later many better-off families moved away.

In some banlieues there is a lot of **unemployment** and poverty. The département of **Seine-Saint-Denis** north of Paris is regarded as the poorest département of mainland France. In October **2005**, riots began in **Clichy-sous-Bois** that spread across the whole of France. The causes and the right solutions are still debated in France today.

Many lines of the Paris metro run like a star to the centre. Anyone wanting to go from one suburb to another often has to travel through the city. The big project **Grand Paris Express** is meant to link the suburbs directly with each other with new **ring lines**. In Saint-Denis there is also the **Stade de France**, the largest stadium in France.

Life in the banlieues is often a subject of films and music. Well known is the film **“La Haine”** by **Mathieu Kassovitz** from **1995**. It tells of one day in the life of young men from a Paris banlieue. Many well-known French rappers and footballers also grew up in suburbs.

gewusst: The film “La Haine” was shot in black and white.
In Switzerland too, large housing estates were built on the edge of cities in the 1960s and 1970s, for example in Geneva and Aarau.

teile.einleitung: The bora is a cold, very violent wind on the Adriatic coast, above all in Croatia and near Trieste. It plunges from the mountains down to the sea and can reach hurricane force.
wichtigste: The bora is a cold downslope wind on the Adriatic coast.
It blows most often in winter.
The gusts can reach over 200 km/h.
On the Velebit in Croatia it is especially strong.
In Trieste there are ropes or chains on steep streets to hold on to.
People distinguish the bright “bora chiara” and the dark “bora scura”.
The name is related to Boreas, the Greek god of the north wind.

abschnitte.text: A **downslope wind** is a wind that flows from a mountain range down into the valley or to the sea. With the **bora**, very cold air collects inland behind the coastal mountains. This air then flows down over the passes to the coast in violent **gusts**. It happens most often in **winter**, because the air in the hinterland is then especially cold.

abschnitte.titel: Why not warm like the foehn?
abschnitte.text: Air gets warmer as it sinks. With the **foehn** in the Alps, this leads to a warm wind. The bora also warms as it flows down. But its **starting air** is so cold that the warming is not enough. So it still arrives on the coast as an icy wind. Quite different is the **sirocco**, a warm, damp south wind.

The bora blows especially strongly on the **Velebit**, a coastal mountain range about 145 kilometres long in Croatia, for example near Senj and Karlobag. At the **Maslenica Bridge**, a gust of **248 km/h** was measured on 21 December 1998, officially the highest bora gust in Croatia. In the port city of **Trieste**, gusts often reach over 120 km/h. There, on some steep pavements, ropes or chains are stretched so that people can hold on.

In Trieste two kinds are distinguished. The **bora chiara**, the bright bora, blows in high pressure under a cloudless sky. The **bora scura**, the dark bora, comes with low pressure, clouds and often rain or snow. A similar downslope wind also blows near **Novorossiysk** on the Black Sea in Russia. The name bora goes back to the Greek **Boreas**, the god of the north wind.

gewusst: In the cold spell of February 2012, the bora is said to have hurled fish out of the sea onto the land on the island of Pag.
In a strong bora, motorways and bridges sometimes have to be closed in Croatia.

teile.einleitung: The Atlantic Ocean is the second-largest ocean on Earth. It lies between Europe and Africa on one side and the Americas on the other, and strongly shapes the weather in Europe.
wichtigste: The Atlantic is the second-largest ocean on Earth.
The Gulf Stream brings mild weather to Europe.
The Bay of Biscay lies between France and Spain.
Brittany juts far out into the Atlantic.
At Nazaré in Portugal there are huge waves.
Whales live in the Atlantic.

abschnitte.text: The **Atlantic Ocean** separates Europe and Africa from North and South America. Only the Pacific is larger. Through the middle of the Atlantic runs a long underwater mountain range, the **Mid-Atlantic Ridge**. There, Earth’s plates are slowly moving apart. The **North Sea** also belongs to the Atlantic, and so the water of the Rhine from **Switzerland** ends up in this ocean.

The **Gulf Stream** is a warm **ocean current**. It brings warm water from the Gulf of Mexico across the Atlantic to the north. Its continuation, the North Atlantic Current, makes the weather in western Europe milder than in other regions equally far north. Without it, the winters in Europe would be much colder.

Between France and Spain lies the large bay of the **Bay of Biscay**. There are often storms and high waves. In France the **Brittany** peninsula juts far into the Atlantic. In Portugal the city of **Porto** lies at the mouth of the river **Douro**. At **Nazaré**, professional surfers ride huge waves that are created by a deep underwater canyon.

Many **whales** live in the Atlantic. They are mammals and breathe air through a **blowhole** on their head. There are also dolphins, sharks, tuna and large shoals of herring and cod. **Fishing** is important for many coastal countries.

In the Atlantic lie many islands, for example **Iceland**, the Canary Islands, the Azores and **Madeira**. Madeira belongs to Portugal. The footballer **Cristiano Ronaldo** was born there. Iceland lies exactly on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge and therefore has many volcanoes.

gewusst: The Atlantic becomes a few centimetres wider every year, because the Earth’s plates are moving apart.
The name Atlantic goes back to the Titan Atlas from Greek legend.

teile.einleitung: Athens is the capital of Greece and one of the oldest cities in Europe. Democracy arose in ancient Athens, and the famous Acropolis sits above the city.
wichtigste: Athens is named after the goddess Athena.
On the Acropolis stands the Parthenon from the time of Pericles.
The Acropolis has been a UNESCO World Heritage site since 1987.
Democracy arose in ancient Athens.
The port city of Piraeus borders Athens directly.
In 2004 the Summer Olympic Games took place in Athens.

abschnitte.text: Athens is named after the goddess **Athena**, the goddess of wisdom. Her symbol was the owl. On the rock of the **Acropolis**, the **Parthenon**, a temple for Athena, was built in the 5th century BC under the statesman **Pericles**. The Acropolis has been a UNESCO World Heritage site since **1987**.

In ancient Athens **democracy** arose, rule by the people. Free citizens were allowed to vote on laws in an assembly. Women, slaves and foreigners, however, were excluded. Even so, democracy is regarded as the greatest legacy of Athens. Today’s democracies such as **Switzerland** also draw on this idea.

In 1896 the first **modern Olympic Games** took place in Athens. The venue was the **Panathenaic Stadium**, which is built entirely of **marble**. Most recently, Athens hosted the Summer Olympics in **2004**. For these Games, new roads, railways and sports venues were built.

In the centre lies **Syntagma Square**, where the Greek **parliament** stands. When the **metro** was built, experts found many old objects in the ground. Some of them are now on display in the metro stations, for example at Syntagma station. So passengers can see history on the way to the train.

Directly next to Athens lies the port city of **Piraeus**. It is the largest port in Greece. From here ferries sail to many Greek islands. In **2016** the Chinese group **COSCO** took over the majority of the port company.

gewusst: Even in ancient times a long wall linked Athens with the port of Piraeus.
Athens has been the capital of modern Greece since 1834.

teile.einleitung: Dublin is the capital of Ireland. The city lies on the east coast of the island and is known for its history, its music and its colourful front doors.
wichtigste: Dublin lies on the **Irish Sea**.
The river **Liffey** flows through the middle of the city.
On the street signs, besides English, there is also **Irish**.
In the 9th century, **Vikings** founded a settlement here.
In **Trinity College** you can see the old **Book of Kells**.
In the large Phoenix Park live free-roaming deer.

abschnitte.text: Dublin lies on the east coast of Ireland on the **Irish Sea**. The river **Liffey** flows through the middle of the city and divides it into a northern and a southern part. Many bridges cross the river. The well-known **Ha'penny Bridge** gets its name from a bridge toll: in the past, crossing cost half a penny. On the street signs the names are in English and in **Irish**, the old language of the country.

In the 9th century **Vikings** came with their ships and founded a settlement here. The name Dublin comes from the Irish “Dubh Linn” and means **“black pool”**. This meant a dark pool where a small river entered the Liffey. Later Dublin became the most important city in Ireland.

**Trinity College** is the oldest university in Ireland. It was founded in 1592 and lies in the middle of the city. The **Book of Kells** is kept there. It is a very old manuscript of the four Gospels, which monks decorated over 1,200 years ago with colourful pictures and interlaced patterns. Every year very many visitors come to see it.

**Phoenix Park** is one of the largest city parks in Europe. In it lives a herd of free-roaming **deer**. Many old houses in Dublin date from the 18th century and look very similar. But their **front doors** are painted in strong colours, for example red, blue, green or yellow. They are a popular photo subject.

gewusst: In Phoenix Park also stands the residence of the President of Ireland.
The harp is the emblem of Ireland and even appears on the Irish euro coins.

teile.einleitung: The Canal Ring is a ring of canals around the old town of Amsterdam. It was planned in the 17th century, when the trading city was growing fast. Since 2010 it has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
wichtigste: The Canal Ring was created in the 17th century as a planned expansion of the city.
Since 2010 it has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
From the inside outwards come the Herengracht, the Keizersgracht and the Prinsengracht.
The Singel was originally the city moat and forms the innermost ring.
Most of the houses stand on wooden piles.
The name Amsterdam comes from the river Amstel.

abschnitte.text: In the **17th century** Amsterdam was one of the richest **trading cities** in the world and grew quickly. The city therefore planned a large expansion: new **canals** for transport and drainage, and building land for rich merchants. The canals curve around the old town as **half rings**. In **2010** UNESCO added the Canal Ring to the World Heritage list as an outstanding example of a planned city expansion.

abschnitte.titel: The rings from the inside outwards
abschnitte.text: The innermost ring is the **Singel**. Until the end of the 16th century it surrounded the medieval city as a **defensive moat**. Then come the three main canals: the **Herengracht**, the **Keizersgracht** and the **Prinsengracht**. The outer edge of the World Heritage area is formed by the **Singelgracht**, formerly the fortress moat of the expanded city.

The ground in Amsterdam is made of soft **peat** and clay. That is why long **wooden piles** were driven deep into the ground, down to a firm layer of sand. Most of the historic houses stand on these piles. The houses are narrow and have steep, tight staircases. That is why a **beam with a hook** sticks out from many gables. With it, people hoisted goods and furniture up through the windows on a rope.

Amsterdam grew up at a **dam** on the river **Amstel**. The present name comes from “Amstelredamme”. At **Prinsengracht 263** stands the **Anne Frank House**. There Anne Frank hid with her family from the Nazis in the Second World War, in the rear annexe. Today it is a museum that very many people visit every year.

gewusst: Many canal houses lean slightly forward so that goods do not bump against the front when they are hauled up.
Amsterdam has more than 1000 bridges.

teile.einleitung: Andalusia is a large region in the far south of Spain. It is known for sun, old Moorish buildings, flamenco and huge olive groves.
wichtigste: Andalusia is an autonomous community in the south of Spain.
The capital is Seville.
The most important river is the Guadalquivir.
In Granada stands the Alhambra, in Córdoba the Mezquita.
Flamenco comes from Andalusia.
Andalusia produces a great deal of olive oil.

abschnitte.text: Andalusia lies in the south of the Iberian Peninsula and borders the **Mediterranean** and the **Atlantic**. In the far south, the **Strait of Gibraltar** separates Europe from Africa. The region is divided into eight provinces, including Seville, Granada, Córdoba, Málaga and Jaén. In the **Sierra Nevada** mountains lies Mulhacén, the highest mountain of mainland Spain. In summer it often gets very hot in Andalusia.

The **Guadalquivir** is the main river of Andalusia. It flows through Córdoba and Seville and enters the Atlantic. It is navigable for ships as far as Seville, which is why Seville used to be an important port for trade with America. At its mouth lies the **Doñana** National Park, a large wetland with many birds.

The name Andalusia comes from the Arabic **al-Andalus**. This is what the **Moors**, Muslims from North Africa, called their territory in Spain. They ruled here for many centuries. In **Granada** they built the magnificent fortress complex of the **Alhambra**, which has been a UNESCO World Heritage site since 1984. In **Córdoba** stands the **Mezquita**, a former mosque with a forest of columns and red and white arches. Today it is a cathedral.

**Flamenco** is a style of music and dance from Andalusia. It combines singing, guitar playing, clapping and dancing. Since 2010 it has belonged to the **intangible cultural heritage** of UNESCO, that is, to the important traditions of humanity. In Seville a big folk festival takes place every spring, the Feria.

In Andalusia grow huge **olive groves**, especially in the province of **Jaén**. **Olive oil** is pressed from the olives. Spain is the largest olive oil producer in the world, and a large part of it comes from Andalusia. Oranges, vegetables and wine are also grown. Many holidaymakers come to the coast, for example to the Costa del Sol near Málaga.

gewusst: From the southern tip of Andalusia you can see as far as Africa in clear weather.
The Alhambra is among the most visited sights in Spain.

t1ollgbq.t: The border between Europe and Asia

teile.einleitung: Europe and Asia lie on the same large landmass. Where exactly one continent ends and the other begins was decided by people. That is why there are different border lines.
wichtigste: Europe and Asia together form one landmass, which is called Eurasia.
The usual border follows the Urals, the Ural River and the Caspian Sea.
Russia, Turkey and Kazakhstan have territory on both continents.
Around three quarters of the area of Russia lie in Asia.
Since the 18th century the Urals have been regarded as the border.
Cyprus, a member of the EU, lies entirely in Asia geographically.

abschnitte.text: Europe and Asia are not separated by an ocean. They form one connected **landmass**, which is often called **Eurasia**. The border between them is therefore not a natural coastline, but was set by people. That is why there are different suggestions for where it runs. The line used today leads from the **Ural Mountains** along the **Ural River** to the **Caspian Sea**.

The ancient Greeks regarded the river **Don**, called Tanais in Greek, as the border. This is how geographers such as **Strabo** and **Ptolemy** described it. Only around **1730** did the officer Philip Johan von **Strahlenberg** and the Russian scholar Vasily **Tatishchev** suggest the **Urals** as the border. This idea caught on. Since the 18th century the Urals have been used in this way.

Between the Caspian Sea and the Black Sea the border is unclear. Some draw it along the **crest of the Caucasus**. Others take the **Kuma-Manych Depression** to the north of it. Then the whole Caucasus lies in Asia. A country like **Georgia** is counted partly as part of Europe, depending on where the border is drawn. Georgia also sees itself politically as a European country and is a **candidate for EU membership**.

Some states lie on both continents. **Russia** has around three quarters of its area in Asia, east of the Urals, mainly **Siberia**. Most people, however, live in the European part. In **Turkey**, Eastern Thrace with the European part of **Istanbul** lies in Europe, while the larger part, Anatolia, lies in Asia. **Kazakhstan** also has a small part in Europe, west of the Ural River. The island of **Cyprus**, on the other hand, lies entirely in Asia geographically, but belongs to the EU.

gewusst: Istanbul is a city on two continents, separated by the Bosphorus strait.
The EU country Cyprus lies in Asia geographically.

teile.einleitung: The eurozone is the area of the EU countries that have the euro as their official currency. Since Bulgaria joined on 1 January 2026, it has 21 members (as of 2026).
wichtigste: The eurozone has 21 members (as of 2026).
In 1999 eleven countries started with the euro as money in accounts.
Since 1 January 2002 there have been euro coins and banknotes.
Croatia joined in 2023 as the 20th country, Bulgaria in 2026 as the 21st.
Denmark has an opt-out and does not have to introduce the euro.
Montenegro and Kosovo use the euro unilaterally without EU membership.

abschnitte.text: On **1 January 1999**, **eleven EU countries** introduced the euro, among them Germany, France and Italy. At first it existed only as **book money**, that is, in accounts and for transfers. Greece followed in 2001. On **1 January 2002** the coins and banknotes came into circulation. Since then people in these countries have had the euro in their purses.

In time more countries joined. **Croatia** introduced the euro on 1 January 2023 and became the **20th member**, replacing the kuna. On 1 January 2026 **Bulgaria** followed as the **21st member**. Bulgaria gave up its **lev**, which had previously been tied firmly to the euro. Anyone who wants to introduce the euro must meet certain conditions, for example on government debt and prices.

Not all EU countries have the euro. **Denmark** secured the right in a treaty not to have to introduce it, and keeps the **Danish krone**. **Sweden**, **Poland** and the **Czech Republic** also have their own national currencies (as of 2025): Sweden the krona, Poland the zloty and the Czech Republic the koruna. They are in the EU, but not in the eurozone. In countries such as Finland, Ireland and Austria, on the other hand, people pay with euros.

Some countries outside the EU also use the euro. **Monaco**, **San Marino**, **Vatican City** and **Andorra** have agreements with the EU for this. **Montenegro** and **Kosovo**, by contrast, adopted the euro **unilaterally**, without an agreement of their own. **Switzerland** has its own franc, although it is almost entirely surrounded by euro countries.

On all euro coins the **value side** is the same. Each country designs the back itself, for example with landmarks or well-known people. The banknotes, by contrast, look the same everywhere. The note with the highest value is the **500-euro note**. It has no longer been newly issued since 2019, but remains valid. The **European Central Bank** in Frankfurt am Main looks after the euro.

gewusst: Before there was euro cash, the euro was already used for three years only in accounts.
Montenegro uses the euro even though it belongs neither to the EU nor to the eurozone.

teile.einleitung: The Althing is the parliament of Iceland. It was founded in the year 930 and is regarded as one of the oldest parliaments in the world.
wichtigste: The Althing is the Icelandic parliament.
It was founded in the year 930.
In the past people met in the open air at Þingvellir.
Today the Althing meets in Reykjavík.
It is regarded as one of the oldest parliaments in the world.

abschnitte.titel: An assembly in the open air
abschnitte.text: In the year **930**, the free men of Iceland met for the first time at the **Althing**. The name means roughly “assembly of all”. Every summer they came together on a plain called **Þingvellir**, which means “plain of the assembly”. There laws were passed and disputes settled. A **law speaker** recited the laws from memory, because for a long time little was written down.

For many centuries Iceland belonged to Norway and later to Denmark. The Althing therefore lost much of its power and was even dissolved around 1800. In the 19th century it was set up again, now in the capital **Reykjavík**. Today it is a modern **parliament** whose members are elected by the people. Since 1944 Iceland has been an independent republic.

**Þingvellir** is now a **national park** and part of the UNESCO World Heritage. There you can see how the **North American** and the **Eurasian Plate** are slowly drifting apart. Between them lie deep cracks in the rock. The old assembly is a little reminiscent of the **Landsgemeinde**, which still exists in Switzerland today in Glarus and Appenzell Innerrhoden.

gewusst: At Þingvellir you can walk between two continental plates.
The laws of the old Althing were learned by heart for a long time and recited aloud.

teile.einleitung: The Faroe Islands are a group of islands in the middle of the North Atlantic. They belong to the Kingdom of Denmark, but run most things themselves. The landscape is green, windy and almost without trees.
wichtigste: The Faroe Islands lie in the North Atlantic between Iceland, Norway and Scotland.
They consist of 18 larger islands, all but one of them inhabited.
The capital is called Tórshavn.
In 2025 about 55,000 people lived in the Faroe Islands.
The islands belong to Denmark, but not to the EU.
The most important way of making a living is fishing.

abschnitte.text: The **Faroe Islands** lie in the **North Atlantic**, between Iceland, Norway and Scotland. They consist of **18 larger islands**, all but one of which are inhabited. The weather is often windy, foggy and rainy, but not very cold, because warm sea water flows past. Many islands are now connected by **tunnels** and bridges, and some tunnels even run under the sea.

The name “Faroe” is usually interpreted as **“sheep islands”**. And indeed very many sheep live there. There is almost no **natural forest**: strong wind, a cool climate and grazing sheep let hardly any trees grow. The steep slopes are covered with grass and moss. Many seabirds breed on the cliffs, for example **puffins**.

The capital **Tórshavn** is one of the smallest capitals in the world. Typical are colourful houses with **grass roofs**. In 2025 about 55,000 people lived on all the islands together, roughly as many as in the city of Biel/Bienne. In everyday life people speak **Faroese**, a North Germanic language related to Icelandic. At school the children also learn Danish.

The Faroe Islands belong to the **Kingdom of Denmark**, but have their own parliament and run most things themselves. Although Denmark is a member of the EU, the Faroe Islands are **not part of the EU**. In this way they can decide on their fishing themselves. **Fishing** is the most important branch of the economy. Fish and fish products, including from **salmon farming**, make up the largest part of the exports.

gewusst: In the Faroe Islands there are almost no trees, but very many sheep.
The Faroe Islands have their own national football team, which has even played against Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: Lake Walen is a long, narrow lake between the cantons of St Gallen and Glarus. On its north side, the seven peaks of the Churfirsten rise almost vertically from the water. On the shore lies Quinten, a village that can be reached only by boat or on foot.
wichtigste: Lake Walen is about 24 square kilometres in area and up to about 150 metres deep.
It lies in the cantons of St Gallen and Glarus.
On the north side stand the Churfirsten with their seven peaks.
The village of Quinten can be reached only by boat or on foot.
The Linth flows through Lake Walen towards Lake Zurich.
Railway and motorway run along the south shore.
Because of the mild climate, vines and even figs grow in Quinten.

abschnitte.text: Lake Walen lies at about 419 metres above sea level between **Weesen** in the west and **Walenstadt** in the east. It is about 15 kilometres long and only about 2 kilometres wide. Most of it belongs to the canton of St Gallen, a smaller part to the canton of Glarus. Since the building of the **Escher Canal** in 1811, the Linth flows into Lake Walen and leaves it through the Linth Canal towards Lake Zurich.

On the north side of the lake stand the **Churfirsten**, a mountain range with seven peaks. They fall away towards the lake in steep rock faces, while on the other side they have gentle grassy slopes towards the Toggenburg. The highest peak is the Hinterrugg at about 2,300 metres. Beneath the rock faces, the Seerenbach Falls tumble down in several steps; they are among the highest waterfalls in Switzerland.

**Quinten** lies on the north shore between rock and water and has no road. You can reach it only by boat or on a hiking trail. Because the rock faces store the warmth of the sun and keep out cold winds, the climate is very mild. That is why vines, figs and kiwis grow here, and Quinten is sometimes called the Riviera of eastern Switzerland.

On the south shore there is little room between mountain and lake. Even so, the railway line to Chur and the **A3 motorway** run along it, often through tunnels and galleries. In the past the lake was an important waterway for trade between Zurich and the Grisons. Today passenger ships run between the villages.

The name Walen probably comes from the old word **Walen**, with which the Alemanni referred to people who spoke a Romance language. In the early Middle Ages a language border ran roughly along the lake. The place name Walenstadt has the same origin. The names Quinten, Terzen and Quarten may go back to old words for numbers.

begriffe.erklaerung: A mountain range with seven peaks on the north shore of Lake Walen.
An artificial canal that leads the Linth from Lake Walen into Lake Zurich.
A special climate in a small area that differs from the climate of its surroundings.
An old word of the Alemanni for people who spoke a Romance language.

gewusst: In Quinten there are no cars; the residents bring their shopping to the village by boat.
The Linth Canal was built under the leadership of Hans Conrad Escher, who received the honorary name “von der Linth” for it.

teile.einleitung: The Douro is a large river on the Iberian Peninsula. It rises in Spain, flows through Portugal and enters the Atlantic at Porto.
wichtigste: The Douro rises in **Spain**, where it is called the Duero.
It enters the Atlantic at the city of **Porto**.
**Port wine** is made from the grapes of the Douro Valley.
The wine landscape of the **Alto Douro** has been a UNESCO World Heritage site since 2001.
In the past, wooden boats called **rabelos** carried the wine barrels downstream.

abschnitte.text: The river rises in the north of **Spain**, where it is called the **Duero**. It flows west through the plateau of Castile. For a stretch it forms the border between Spain and Portugal. Then it flows through the north of **Portugal** and enters the Atlantic at **Porto**. It is among the longest rivers of the Iberian Peninsula.

In the valley of the Douro, vines grow on steep slopes. The winegrowers have built many **terraces** there, which are step-like fields on the slope. The grapes are used mainly to make **port wine**, a sweet, strong wine. It is named after the city of Porto. Since 2001 the wine landscape of the **Alto Douro** has been part of the UNESCO World Heritage.

In the past there were no good roads through the narrow valley. So the wine barrels were carried downstream on flat wooden boats. These boats are called **rabelos**. They brought the wine to Vila Nova de Gaia, opposite Porto, where it was stored in large cellars. Today rabelos are seen mainly as decoration and for trips on the river.

gewusst: On many wine terraces on the Douro, the hard slate ground used to be broken up by hand so that vines could be planted.
The well-known port wine cellars lie not in Porto itself but on the other side of the river in Vila Nova de Gaia.

teile.einleitung: Lake Neuchâtel is the largest lake that lies entirely in Switzerland. It stretches along the foot of the Jura for about 38 kilometres. On its shores, people lived in pile-dwelling settlements thousands of years ago.
wichtigste: Lake Neuchâtel is about 218 square kilometres in area and up to 152 metres deep.
It borders the cantons of Neuchâtel, Vaud, Fribourg and Bern.
Canals link it with Lake Biel and Lake Murten.
On the south shore lies the Grande Cariçaie, the largest shore landscape in Switzerland.
The sites of Cortaillod and La Tène gave their names to whole periods of prehistory.
The first cormorants in Switzerland bred at the Fanel.
Larger towns on the lake are Neuchâtel and Yverdon-les-Bains.

abschnitte.text: Lake Neuchâtel lies at about 429 metres above sea level between the **Jura** and the Central Plateau. It is about 38 kilometres long and up to 8 kilometres wide. It is therefore the largest lake lying entirely in Switzerland. Lake Geneva and Lake Constance are larger, but belong partly to France or Germany.

abschnitte.titel: Canals and the Jura Water Correction
abschnitte.text: The **Zihl Canal** links the lake with Lake Biel, the Broye Canal with Lake Murten. In the 19th century, the **Jura Water Correction** lowered the water level of the three lakes by about 2.5 metres. As a result floods became rarer and much swampland became farmland. Many remains of old pile dwellings also came to light.

On the shores in the Neolithic and the Bronze Age stood **pile-dwelling settlements**. A Neolithic culture is named after the village of **Cortaillod**. At **La Tène** at the north-eastern end, many Celtic weapons and pieces of jewellery were found in the 19th century, which is why the later Iron Age is called the La Tène period. In the Laténium museum in Hauterive you can admire the finds.

On the south shore lies the **Grande Cariçaie**, a long belt of reeds, swamp and floodplain forest. Hundreds of species of plants and animals live here. In the Fanel nature reserve at the eastern end, the first cormorant breeding in Switzerland took place; today there are about 3,000 to 3,500 breeding pairs nationwide. Great crested grebes can also be watched well on the lake, and in the depths lives the wels catfish.

On the north-western shore lies the city of **Neuchâtel** with its castle and the university. At the southern end lies Yverdon-les-Bains, known for its thermal springs. Other places are Estavayer-le-Lac, Grandson and Concise. In summer you can sail, swim and travel across the lake on passenger boats.

begriffe.erklaerung: Houses that stood on wooden piles on the lakeshore or in the moor.
A large building work with canals that lowered the water levels of the Jura lakes and protects the land from floods.
The later Iron Age of the Celts, named after a find site on Lake Neuchâtel.
A black waterbird that catches fish by diving.

gewusst: At Grandson on Lake Neuchâtel, Charles the Bold lost a battle against the Confederates in 1476 and left his rich treasure behind.
The Grande Cariçaie on the south shore is about 40 kilometres long.
When the bise blows, high waves like those on a small sea can form on Lake Neuchâtel.

teile.einleitung: In the Aegean Sea, the sea between Greece and Turkey, lie very many islands. Most of them belong to Greece. Each island has its own history, from volcanoes to orders of knights to famous finds from ancient times.
wichtigste: Most of the Aegean Islands belong to Greece.
The Dodecanese were under Italian rule from 1912 to 1947.
The caldera of Santorini was formed by a volcanic eruption in the Bronze Age.
On Rhodes, the Knights of St John ruled from 1309 to 1522.
Hippocrates was born on Kos.
Imbros and Tenedos have belonged to Turkey since 1923.

abschnitte.text: **Santorini** has a special shape: the island is a ring around a huge hollow filled with sea water. This hollow is called a **caldera**. It was formed by a huge **volcanic eruption** in the **Bronze Age**, in the 2nd millennium BC. Back then the empty **magma chamber** collapsed, and the sea filled the crater. Today white houses stand high up on the rim of the caldera.

The **Dodecanese** are a group of islands in the south-east of the Aegean. The largest island is **Rhodes**. There the **Knights of St John** ruled from 1309 to 1522. Its fortified old town is a **UNESCO World Heritage** site. In 1912 **Italy** occupied the Dodecanese in the war against the Ottoman Empire. Only the peace treaty of **1947** awarded the islands to Greece. On **Kos** was born the doctor **Hippocrates**, who is regarded as the **father of medicine**.

Only in the south of the island of **Chios** is **mastic** harvested, a resin from a shrub. The mastic villages were therefore prosperous for a long time. The island of **Ikaria** counts as a **Blue Zone**: remarkably many people there live to over 90. Researchers suspect that diet, exercise and close community help. On **Samothrace**, the winged **Victory of Samothrace** was found in **1863**; today it stands in the **Louvre** in Paris.

Almost all the Aegean Islands are Greek. **Imbros**, today **Gökçeada**, and **Tenedos**, today **Bozcaada**, lie off the Dardanelles. In **1923** they went to **Turkey** with the **Treaty of Lausanne**. This treaty was signed in Switzerland. The island of **Lesbos** lies only a few kilometres off the Turkish coast. From **2015**, hundreds of thousands of refugees reached Europe there in boats, and the Moria camp burned down in 2020.

gewusst: The Victory of Samothrace stands in the Louvre at the top of a large staircase and is among its most famous works of art.
The Treaty of Lausanne, which helped to decide the borders in the Aegean, was signed in Switzerland in 1923.

teile.einleitung: Lake Constance lies between Switzerland, Germany and Austria. It is one of the largest lakes in central Europe and the Rhine flows through it.
wichtigste: Lake Constance is about 536 square kilometres in area.
At its deepest point it is about 251 metres deep.
It consists of the large Upper Lake and the smaller Lower Lake.
The Seerhein links the two parts in the middle of Konstanz.
Konstanz is the largest town on Lake Constance.
The borders on the Upper Lake have never been fixed by treaty.
On the Swiss side, the cantons of Thurgau and St Gallen lie on the lake.

abschnitte.text: Three countries meet at **Lake Constance**: **Switzerland**, **Germany** and **Austria**. On the Swiss side, the cantons of **Thurgau** and **St Gallen** border the lake, with places such as Kreuzlingen, Romanshorn, Arbon and Rorschach. In Austria, Bregenz lies on the shore; in Germany, among others, Lindau, Friedrichshafen and Konstanz. At about **536 square kilometres**, Lake Constance is somewhat smaller than Lake Geneva.

The lake has two main parts: the large **Upper Lake** and the shallower **Lower Lake**. They are linked by the **Seerhein**, a stretch of river only about 4 kilometres long through the middle of Konstanz. The deepest point, at **251 metres**, lies in the Upper Lake between Fischbach and Uttwil. The **Rhine** flows into the lake from the Alpine Rhine Valley and leaves it again at Stein am Rhein.

**Konstanz** is the largest town on Lake Constance. It borders directly on Kreuzlingen in Thurgau, and the border runs right through the houses. High above the shore stands **Meersburg Castle**. It is regarded as the oldest castle in Germany that is still lived in. Also very well known is the flower island of **Mainau** with its large gardens.

Something special is the **border** on the Upper Lake: Germany, Austria and Switzerland have never agreed on it by treaty. In everyday life this still works well, because shared rules apply to **shipping** and **fishing**. The lake is also an important **drinking water reservoir**: millions of people in southern Germany drink water from Lake Constance.

gewusst: In the very cold winter of 1963, Lake Constance almost completely froze over; this is called a “Seegfrörni” (a freeze of the whole lake).
Between Konstanz and Kreuzlingen, the national border runs right through residential districts.

teile.einleitung: The “Third Italy” is a term from economic geography. It describes regions in the north-east and centre of Italy that became successful with many small family firms.
wichtigste: The term “Terza Italia” was coined by the sociologist **Arnaldo Bagnasco** in 1977.
The Third Italy typically includes **Emilia-Romagna**, **Tuscany** and **Veneto**.
The First Italy is the old **industrial triangle** of Milan, Turin and Genoa.
Typical are **small and medium-sized family firms**.
Firms in the same industry cluster together in **industrial districts**.
Their model of success is called **flexible specialisation**.

abschnitte.text: After the Second World War, Italy was often divided economically into two parts: the rich, industrial north and the poorer south. The **First Italy** was the **industrial triangle** between Milan, Turin and Genoa with large factories. The second Italy was the south, the **Mezzogiorno**. In 1977 the sociologist **Arnaldo Bagnasco** described a third area that developed differently. He called it **“Terza Italia”**, the Third Italy.

In the Third Italy the economy is shaped not by huge corporations but by **small and medium-sized family firms**. Many of them make only one part of a product. Firms in the same industry often lie close together. Such clusters are called **industrial districts**. The firms work together but also compete with each other.

The town of **Prato** in Tuscany is known for its **textile industry**. **Sassuolo** in Emilia-Romagna is world famous for **ceramic tiles**. Also in Emilia-Romagna lies the so-called **Motor Valley**. There sports car makers such as Ferrari and Lamborghini have their seats. In Veneto there are districts for glasses, shoes or furniture.

The model of success of the Third Italy is called **flexible specialisation**. The small firms can quickly adapt to new wishes of customers. They do not make huge quantities of the same product but often smaller series in high quality. Well-trained specialists and trust between the firms help. Switzerland also has such clusters, for example the watch industry in the Jura Arc.

gewusst: Many tiles in bathrooms all over the world come from the area around Sassuolo.
In Prato, old fabrics have been turned into new wool for centuries.

teile.einleitung: The Aegean Sea, or Aegean for short, is a part of the Mediterranean. It lies between Greece and Turkey and is full of islands. Even in ancient times it was an important route for sailors and traders.
wichtigste: The Aegean lies between the Greek mainland and Asia Minor, that is, Turkey.
It is a part of the Mediterranean.
According to a legend, it is named after King Aegeus.
Thousands of islands lie in the Aegean, for example the Cyclades and the Sporades.
Thessaloniki in Greece and Izmir in Turkey lie on its coasts.
Lesbos is the third-largest island of Greece.

abschnitte.text: The Aegean lies in the eastern Mediterranean. In the west and north it borders **Greece**, in the east **Turkey**. In the south the island of Crete roughly forms its boundary. In the north-east, the strait of the **Dardanelles** leads into the Sea of Marmara and on to the Black Sea.

According to a Greek legend, the name goes back to **King Aegeus** of Athens. His son **Theseus** sailed to Crete to fight a monster. On his return a white sail was to show that he was alive. But Theseus forgot to change the black sail. Aegeus believed his son was dead and threw himself into the sea.

The Aegean is one of the seas with the most islands in the world. Well-known groups are the **Cyclades** in the middle and the **Northern Sporades** with Skiathos and Skopelos, north-east of the large island of Euboea. “Sporades” means “scattered islands”. In the north-east lies **Lesbos**, only a few kilometres off the Turkish coast. It is the third-largest island of Greece.

In the north-west lies **Thessaloniki** on the Thermaic Gulf. It is the second-largest city in Greece. On the Turkish coast lies **Izmir**, which used to be called Smyrna. Izmir is the third-largest city in Turkey and lies on a long bay of the Aegean.

abschnitte.titel: A sea with a long history
abschnitte.text: Thousands of years ago, people were already sailing from island to island. Ancient cultures and cities grew up on the coasts. Today the Aegean is important mainly for **fishing**, **shipping** and **tourism**. Many people go on holiday there to the beach.

gewusst: The Aegean has so many islands that from many places you can always see another island.
The ancient city of Troy lay close to the entrance of the Dardanelles.

teile.einleitung: The Eysturoy Tunnel in the Faroe Islands is a road tunnel under the sea. It is known worldwide because its branches meet in a roundabout under the seabed.
wichtigste: The Eysturoy Tunnel lies in the Faroe Islands in the North Atlantic.
It was opened in 2020.
The tunnel connects three places with one another.
Its branches meet under the seabed in a roundabout.
The roundabout is designed with light and art.

abschnitte.text: The **Faroe Islands** are a group of islands in the North Atlantic between Scotland, Norway and Iceland. They belong to the Kingdom of **Denmark**, but run many things themselves. Between the islands lie arms of the sea and deep fjords. In the past people therefore often needed **ferries** or long detours. Today several **undersea tunnels** connect the islands.

The **Eysturoy Tunnel** was opened in **2020**. It runs under an arm of the sea and connects the main island with the island of **Eysturoy**. The special thing: the tunnel has several branches that connect **three places** with one another. These branches meet deep under the seabed in a **roundabout**. The roundabout is designed with coloured **light** and a work of art, so that the drive underground does not seem dull.

Thanks to the tunnel, the journeys between the capital **Tórshavn** and the places on Eysturoy have become much shorter. Trips that used to take almost an hour are now much quicker. For the people in the Faroe Islands this matters a great deal in everyday life, for example on the way to work or to school. For tourists the illuminated roundabout is a sight worth seeing.

gewusst: The Eysturoy Tunnel is regarded as the first tunnel in the world with a roundabout under the sea.
Fewer people live in the Faroe Islands than in the city of Lucerne, yet they have several undersea tunnels.

teile.einleitung: Bosnia and Herzegovina is a country in the Balkans in south-eastern Europe. It consists of two large parts and has a particularly varied history. The capital is Sarajevo.
wichtigste: The capital of Bosnia and Herzegovina is Sarajevo.
The country consists of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the Republika Srpska.
In addition there is the special district of Brčko.
This order comes from the Dayton peace agreement of 1995.
The currency is called the Convertible Mark.
The three largest ethnic groups are Bosniaks, Serbs and Croats.
The country has only a very short stretch of sea coast at Neum.

abschnitte.text: Bosnia and Herzegovina lies on the **Balkan Peninsula**. It borders Croatia, Serbia and Montenegro. The country is very mountainous and has many forests and rivers. It reaches the sea only at the town of **Neum**, on a stretch of coast of about 20 kilometres. The name is made up of two historical regions: **Bosnia** in the north and **Herzegovina** in the south.

After the **Bosnian War** of 1992 to 1995, a new order was laid down in the **Dayton Agreement**. Since then the country has consisted of two **entities**, that is, large parts of the country with their own government: the **Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina** and the **Republika Srpska**. In addition there is the special district of **Brčko**. At the head of the state stands a presidency with three members, one from each of the three large ethnic groups.

In Bosnia and Herzegovina live mainly **Bosniaks**, **Serbs** and **Croats**. Many Bosniaks are Muslims, many Serbs Orthodox Christians and many Croats Catholics. That is why in some towns mosques, churches and synagogues stand close together. Sarajevo is therefore sometimes called the Jerusalem of Europe. Many people with roots in Bosnia and Herzegovina also live in Switzerland.

A well-known landmark is the old bridge **Stari Most** in Mostar. It dates from the time of the Ottomans, was destroyed in the war in 1993 and rebuilt by 2004. Today it is part of the **UNESCO World Heritage**. In **Sarajevo** the Winter Olympic Games took place in 1984. The currency of the country is the **Convertible Mark**, which was introduced in 1998. Its value was at first tied to the Deutschmark, today to the euro.

gewusst: From the old bridge in Mostar, brave divers have for a long time jumped over 20 metres down into the river Neretva.
Bosnia and Herzegovina has one of the shortest sea coasts of any country with access to the sea.

teile.einleitung: Brač is a large island in Dalmatia, on the Croatian Adriatic coast. It is famous for the beach Zlatni Rat and for its pale limestone.
wichtigste: Brač lies in the Adriatic off the city of Split.
It is among the largest islands in the Adriatic.
Near Bol lies the famous beach Zlatni Rat, the “Golden Horn”.
White limestone has been quarried on Brač since ancient times.
The stone was already used for Diocletian’s Palace in Split.
The main town is Supetar, and ferries run there from Split.

abschnitte.text: **Brač** lies opposite the city of **Split** in the Adriatic. It is one of the largest islands on the Croatian coast. The main town **Supetar** is easy to reach by ferry from Split. On the island there are olive groves, vineyards and small stone villages. The highest mountain, Vidova Gora, at 778 metres is the highest peak of all the Adriatic islands.

Near the town of Bol lies the beach **Zlatni Rat**, in English the **Golden Horn**. It consists of fine pebbles and juts out into the sea like a point. Depending on the **wind** and **current**, the shape of its tip changes slightly. The beach is among the best-known beaches in Croatia and is also popular with windsurfers.

Since **ancient times**, Brač has been known for its pale **limestone**. The Romans used it to build **Diocletian’s Palace** in Split. Many houses and churches in Dalmatia are also made of this stone. It is still quarried today. In the town of Pučišća there is even a school where young people learn the craft of the stonemason.

gewusst: The beach Zlatni Rat changes its tip a little depending on the wind.
Vidova Gora on Brač is the highest mountain of all the islands in the Adriatic.

teile.einleitung: The English Channel is an arm of the sea between England and France. It links the North Sea with the Atlantic. So many ships sail on it that hardly anywhere else in the world has more.
wichtigste: The English Channel separates the south coast of England from the north coast of France.
At its narrowest point, the Strait of Dover, it is only about 33 kilometres wide.
In French it is called “La Manche”, which means “the sleeve”.
The white cliffs of Dover gleam white.
It is among the busiest waterways in the world.
Louis Blériot flew over it in 1909, and Matthew Webb swam across it in 1875.

abschnitte.text: The Channel lies between **England** and **France**. In the west it is wide, and towards the east it gets narrower and narrower. The narrowest point is called the **Strait of Dover**, in French the **Pas de Calais**. There it is only about 33 kilometres wide. The French name “La Manche” means “the sleeve”, and the German name Ärmelkanal (“sleeve canal”) comes from it too.

At **Dover** stand high cliffs of **chalk**, which is why they gleam white. Opposite lies the French port of **Calais**. Many ferries sail between the two towns. In the Channel lie the **Channel Islands**, for example **Jersey**. They lie close to France but are linked with the British Crown.

Every day hundreds of ships sail through the Channel. Large cargo ships bring goods to the ports on the North Sea. Then there are ferries that cross from side to side. To prevent collisions, fixed **shipping lanes** apply, like on a motorway. Since 1994, trains have also run through the **Channel Tunnel** under the sea.

In 1875 the Englishman **Matthew Webb** became the first person to swim from Dover to Calais without aids. It took him almost 22 hours, because the current carried him far off course. On 25 July 1909 the Frenchman **Louis Blériot** flew an aeroplane from Calais to Dover. His flight took about 37 minutes.

gewusst: In clear weather you can see the white cliffs of Dover from Calais.
A French département is also named after the Strait of Dover, in French Pas de Calais.

teile.einleitung: Afsluitdijk is the Dutch name of the Enclosure Dam. The dam, about 32 kilometres long, has separated the former Zuiderzee from the North Sea since 1932.
wichtigste: Afsluitdijk means “Enclosure Dam” in English.
The dam is about 32 kilometres long.
It links the provinces of North Holland and Friesland.
In 1932 the last gap was closed.
Behind the dam the freshwater lake IJsselmeer was formed.
A motorway runs along the dam.

abschnitte.text: **Afsluiten** means “to close off” in Dutch, and **dijk** means “dyke” or “dam”. The Afsluitdijk is therefore the Enclosure Dam. It belongs to the **Zuiderzee Works**, one of the largest water engineering projects in the Netherlands. A large part of the Netherlands lies very low, and some areas even lie below sea level. That is why dykes there are vital.

In the past the salty **Zuiderzee** reached far inland. In storm surges, villages and fields were flooded, especially badly in 1916. Parliament then decided to close off the bay. The engineer **Cornelis Lely** had planned the work. Building began in 1927, and in 1932 the dam was closed.

Behind the dam there was now a closed lake. Because the river **IJssel** kept bringing fresh water, the water gradually became fresh. This is how the **IJsselmeer** was formed. Today it serves as a large **water reservoir** for drinking water and farming. Parts of the former bay became new land, the polders.

On the Afsluitdijk the **A7 motorway** runs between North Holland and Friesland. Beside it there is a cycle path. On one side lies the open **Wadden Sea**, on the other the calm IJsselmeer. Locks in the dam let ships through and let surplus water out into the sea at low tide.

gewusst: On the Afsluitdijk you can drive for kilometres with nothing but water on both sides.
The Wadden Sea beside the dam is part of the UNESCO World Heritage.

teile.einleitung: The Enclosure Dam is a dam about 32 kilometres long in the Netherlands. Since 1932 it has separated the former Zuiderzee from the Wadden Sea and links the provinces of North Holland and Friesland.
wichtigste: The Enclosure Dam links North Holland and Friesland.
It is about 32 kilometres long and about 90 metres wide.
Building began in 1927, and the last gap was closed in 1932.
The engineer and minister Cornelis Lely is regarded as its mastermind.
The salty Zuiderzee became the freshwater lake IJsselmeer.
The A7 motorway runs over the dam.

abschnitte.text: The **Zuiderzee** used to be a large, salty bay of the sea in the middle of the Netherlands. In storm surges the water flooded the land again and again. As early as the end of the 19th century, the engineer **Cornelis Lely** drew up a plan to close off the bay. The breakthrough came with the **storm surge of 1916**, which flooded wide areas. Because food was also scarce in the First World War, the **Zuiderzee Act** was passed in 1918.

From 1927, thousands of workers built the dam. They tipped mainly **boulder clay**, sand and stones into the sea. On 28 May 1932 the last gap was closed, and the official opening followed in 1933. The dam runs from **Den Oever** in North Holland to Friesland. There it ends at the little hamlet of **Zurich**, which has the same name as the Swiss city.

Behind the dam there was now a closed basin. The river **IJssel** kept bringing fresh water into it. So the salt water gradually became the freshwater lake **IJsselmeer**. Today it is an important **drinking water reservoir**. Part of the former sea was drained and turned into **polders**, that is, new land below sea level.
