There are two lock complexes in the dam, the **Stevin Locks** and the **Lorentz Locks**. They let ships through. They also let surplus water out: at **low tide** the Wadden Sea lies lower than the IJsselmeer. Then the gates open, and the water flows into the sea under its own gradient.

Over the Enclosure Dam runs the **A7 motorway**. At the **Vlieter monument** stands a statue of Cornelis Lely. In 1975 a further dam was added, the **Houtribdijk** between Enkhuizen and Lelystad. It separates the **Markermeer** from the rest of the IJsselmeer. A new polder, the Markerwaard, was actually planned there, but it was never drained.

gewusst: At the end of the Enclosure Dam in Friesland lies a hamlet called Zurich.
The town of Lelystad is named after Cornelis Lely, the mastermind of the dam.

teile.einleitung: In Europe there are some very small countries, which are called microstates or mini-states. Some of them are smaller than a Swiss municipality, and yet they are states in their own right with their own governments.
wichtigste: Very small countries such as Monaco, Andorra or San Marino are called microstates.
Vatican City in Rome is the smallest state in the world.
Monaco, at about 2 square kilometres, is the second-smallest state in the world.
San Marino is completely surrounded by Italy.
Malta consists of several islands in the Mediterranean.
Liechtenstein is about 160 square kilometres, much smaller than the canton of Zurich.
Luxembourg, at about 2,600 square kilometres, is the largest of these microstates.

abschnitte.text: **Vatican City** lies in the middle of **Rome** and is the smallest state in the world. The **Pope**, the head of the Catholic Church, lives there. He is guarded by the **Swiss Guard**, whose soldiers come from Switzerland. **Monaco**, at about 2 square kilometres, is the **second-smallest** state in the world. It lies on the Mediterranean, the official language is **French**, and some people still speak the old language Monegasque.

**San Marino** lies on a mountain near the Adriatic and is surrounded on all sides by **Italy**. People there speak **Italian**. San Marino is regarded as one of the oldest republics in the world. **Andorra** lies high in the **Pyrenees** between France and Spain. The official language is Catalan, and many visitors come to ski.

**Liechtenstein** lies between Switzerland and Austria on the **Rhine**. It is only about **160 square kilometres**, and the canton of Zurich is more than ten times as big. The main town is called **Vaduz**, and a prince stands at its head. Liechtenstein is closely linked with Switzerland: people pay with the **Swiss franc**, and there has been a customs treaty since 1923. The official language is German.

**Malta** consists of several **islands in the Mediterranean**, south of Sicily. The official languages are Maltese and English, and Malta has been part of the EU since 2004. **Luxembourg**, at about **2,600 square kilometres**, is the largest of these microstates. It is a **Grand Duchy** between Belgium, France and Germany. Luxembourg was one of the founding countries of today’s EU.

gewusst: The Swiss Guard has been guarding the Pope for over 500 years.
The whole of Vatican City is smaller than half a square kilometre.

teile.einleitung: Dubrovnik is a city in the south of Croatia on the Adriatic. Its old town is completely surrounded by a mighty wall and is part of the UNESCO World Heritage.
wichtigste: Dubrovnik lies in **Croatia** on the Adriatic.
The whole old town is surrounded by a thick **city wall** about 2 kilometres long.
The wide main street of the old town is called the **Stradun**.
In the past the city was called **Ragusa** and was a small republic of its own.
The nickname of the city is the **Pearl of the Adriatic**.
In front of the city lies the island of **Lokrum**, which is known for its peacocks.

abschnitte.text: The old town of Dubrovnik is surrounded all the way round by a thick **city wall**. It is about 2 kilometres long and has several towers and fortresses. The wall was built and strengthened over many centuries to protect the city from attackers. Today you can walk on the wall right around the old town. From the top you can see the red roofs and the blue sea.

In the past Dubrovnik was called **Ragusa**. For many centuries the city was a small **republic** of its own with a strong merchant fleet. It traded all over the Mediterranean and stayed independent for a long time, although powerful neighbours surrounded it. In 1808 the republic was dissolved by Napoleon’s troops. Afterwards the city belonged to various states, today to Croatia.

The wide main street of the old town is called the **Stradun**. Its paving of pale limestone has become quite smooth from the many footsteps. On the left and right stand old stone houses with shops and cafés. Because of its beauty, the city is called the **“Pearl of the Adriatic”**. Since 1979 the old town has been part of the **UNESCO World Heritage**.

Above the city rises the local mountain **Srđ**. Anyone who does not want to hike up can ride comfortably **by cable car**. At the top there is a wonderful view over the old town and the islands. Right in front of Dubrovnik lies the small island of **Lokrum**. It is known for its **peacocks**, which roam freely there.

gewusst: In the old town of Dubrovnik, scenes for well-known films and television series were shot.
The old town of Dubrovnik is car-free; you explore it on foot.

teile.einleitung: The Côte d'Azur is the Mediterranean coast in the south-east of France. With its blue sea, plenty of sun and famous cities such as Nice and Cannes, it is one of the best-known holiday regions in Europe.
wichtigste: Côte d'Azur means “Blue Coast” in English.
It lies in the south-east of France on the Mediterranean.
The largest city is Nice.
In Cannes a famous film festival takes place every year in May.
The main prize in Cannes is called the Palme d'Or (Golden Palm).
The Maritime Alps reach close to the sea.
Until 1860 Nice belonged to the Kingdom of Sardinia.

abschnitte.text: “Côte” means **coast** and “azur” is a bright **sky blue**. The name **Côte d'Azur** suits the blue sea and the sky. The coast lies in the south-east of France on the **Mediterranean** and reaches to the border with Italy. The small principality of **Monaco** also lies on this coast. Many beaches there consist of round, smooth **pebbles** instead of fine sand.

The Côte d'Azur has a great many **sunny days**. The summers are hot and dry, the winters mild. Behind the coast rise the **Maritime Alps**, the southernmost part of the Alps. They reach almost to the sea. So in spring you can walk by the sea and ski in the mountains on the same day.

**Nice** is the largest city on the Côte d'Azur and has a large airport. Well known is the **Promenade des Anglais**, a long path right by the sea. The name means “walkway of the English”, because many rich English people used to spend the winter here. Until **1860** Nice belonged to the **Kingdom of Sardinia**. In the same year Savoy also came to France.

In **Cannes**, one of the most famous **film festivals** in the world takes place every year in May. Film stars from all over the world walk across the red carpet there. The main prize for the best film is the **Palme d'Or**, the Golden Palm. Switzerland also has a well-known film festival: in **Locarno** in Ticino the **Golden Leopard** is awarded.

gewusst: The name “Côte d'Azur” comes from a book by the French writer Stéphen Liégeard from 1887.
Monaco, one of the smallest countries in the world, lies right on the Côte d'Azur.

teile.einleitung: Finnish is the language of most people in Finland. It sounds strange to German speakers, because it belongs to a completely different language family from German, French or Italian.
wichtigste: Finnish belongs to the Uralic language family, not to the Indo-European languages.
It is most closely related to Estonian.
Finnish is also distantly related to Hungarian.
In Finland, Finnish and Swedish are official languages.
Finnish has no articles and no grammatical gender.

abschnitte.text: Most languages of Europe, for example German, French, Italian and Romansh, belong to the **Indo-European languages**. **Finnish**, by contrast, belongs to the **Uralic language family**. It is most closely related to **Estonian**, so Finns and Estonians can partly understand each other. Finnish is also distantly related to **Hungarian**. But this relationship is so old that you hardly notice it in everyday life.

Finnish has **no articles** such as “the” or “a”. There is also **no grammatical gender**: the word “hän” means both “he” and “she”. Instead, many **endings** are attached to words where English uses small words such as in, from or with. This often produces very long words. The stress always falls on the **first syllable**.

In **Finland**, **Finnish** and **Swedish** are the two official languages, similar to how Switzerland has several national languages. The great majority speak Finnish as their mother tongue. An important work is the **Kalevala**, a collection of old songs and legends that was written down in the 19th century. One Finnish word is known to almost everyone: **sauna**.

gewusst: The word “sauna” comes from Finnish and is used today in many languages.
In Finnish there is only a single word for “he” and “she”: “hän”.

teile.einleitung: The euro is the common money of many countries of the European Union. Anyone going on holiday to Germany, France, Italy or Austria pays there in euros and cents.
wichtigste: The euro is the money of many EU countries; this area is called the eurozone.
One euro has 100 cents.
There are 8 coins: 1, 2, 5, 10, 20 and 50 cents as well as 1 and 2 euros.
The smallest banknote is the 5-euro note.
Each country designs one side of the coins itself.
The European Central Bank stands in Frankfurt am Main.

abschnitte.text: In the past every country in Europe had its own money, for example the Deutschmark or the French franc. Since 2002 there has been the **euro** as coins and notes in many EU countries. The area in which people pay with euros is called the **eurozone**. The sign for the euro is **€**. One euro is divided into **100 cents**.

There are **8 euro coins**: 1, 2, 5, 10, 20 and 50 cents as well as 1 and 2 euros. The coin with the highest value is the **2-euro coin**. One side of every coin is the same everywhere and shows the value. On the other side each country shows its **own picture**, for example a king, a building or an animal. Even so you may use all the coins in the whole eurozone.

From 5 euros upwards there are **banknotes**. The smallest note is the **5-euro note**, followed by 10, 20, 50, 100 and 200 euros. There are also 500-euro notes, but they are no longer being newly printed. The notes look the same in all countries. They show windows, gates and bridges from different periods of European architecture.

The **European Central Bank**, **ECB** for short, looks after the euro. It stands in **Frankfurt am Main** in Germany. The ECB is meant to make sure that the euro stays stable and prices do not rise too fast. In Switzerland, this work for the franc is done by the **Swiss National Bank**. So Switzerland has its own money and not the euro.

In Switzerland people pay with the **Swiss franc**. Because many neighbouring countries have the euro, most Swiss people nevertheless know it well. In border towns, at stations or in tourist areas you can sometimes pay with euros too. But the change is then often given in francs. Anyone going on holiday therefore often changes money.

gewusst: On a euro coin you can tell from the picture which country it comes from.
The buildings on the euro notes do not really exist like that; they stand for architectural styles from different periods.

teile.einleitung: The flag of Kosovo is blue and shows the golden outline of the country with six white stars above it. It was introduced in 2008, when Kosovo declared its independence.
wichtigste: The flag is blue with the golden outline of the country.
Above the outline stand six white stars.
The stars are mostly interpreted as a sign of the ethnic groups of the country.
The flag was introduced in 2008 with the declaration of independence.
The colours recall the European flag.

abschnitte.text: The flag of Kosovo has a **blue** background. In the middle you can see the **golden outline** of the country. Above it stand, in an arc, **six white stars**. The stars are mostly interpreted as standing for the **ethnic groups** of the country, such as Albanians and Serbs. Blue and gold recall the **European flag**.

The flag was introduced in February **2008**, when Kosovo declared its **independence** from Serbia. It was deliberately meant not to favour any ethnic group. That is why it shows neither an old coat of arms nor the colours of a neighbouring country. Many states, including **Switzerland**, have recognised Kosovo as an independent state. Other states, including Serbia, do not.

Only very few countries show their own **outline** on their flag. Another example is **Cyprus**, whose flag shows the shape of the island. In Switzerland many people live with roots in Kosovo. That is why you see the flag here, for example, at football matches or festivals.

gewusst: Besides Kosovo, Cyprus also shows the outline of its own country on its flag.
The flag of Kosovo is one of the youngest flags in Europe.

teile.einleitung: The Dolomites are a mountain group in the Alps in the north of Italy. With their pale, steep towers of rock, they are among the most beautiful mountains in the world.
wichtigste: The Dolomites lie in **Italy** and belong to the **Alps**.
Parts of them lie in **South Tyrol**, where many people speak German.
They are named after the French researcher **Déodat de Dolomieu**.
They arose from **coral reefs** in a primeval sea.
The highest mountain is the **Marmolada**.
Since 2009 the Dolomites have been a UNESCO World Natural Heritage site.

abschnitte.text: The Dolomites lie in the north-east of **Italy**. They are spread across the regions of **South Tyrol**, Trentino and Veneto. In South Tyrol many people speak German, and in some valleys also **Ladin**, an old Rhaeto-Romance language. It is related to Romansh in the Grisons. The highest mountain is the **Marmolada** at about 3,340 metres, and there is even a glacier on it.

About 250 million years ago a warm sea lay here. In it grew huge **coral reefs**. From the remains of the reefs a pale rock formed. Later it was pushed up into mountains by the movement of the Earth’s plates. That is why you can still find fossilised sea creatures in the Dolomites today.

The French researcher **Déodat de Dolomieu** studied the rock of these mountains at the end of the 18th century. He found that it was different from ordinary limestone. The rock was named **dolomite** after him, and later the mountains were given this name too.

At sunset the pale rocks often turn **red and pink**. The locals call this glow **Enrosadira** in Ladin. Especially well known are the **Three Peaks**, three mighty towers of rock side by side. Since 2009 the Dolomites have been a **UNESCO World Natural Heritage** site. In summer many people hike and climb there, and in winter people ski.

gewusst: The Dolomites are also home to the legend of the rose garden of the dwarf king Laurin, which is meant to explain the red glow of the rocks.
The mineral dolomite was named after a person, and the mountains after the mineral.

teile.einleitung: The European Union, or EU for short, is an association of 27 countries in Europe (as of 2026). They work closely together in many areas, for example trade, protecting the environment and travel.
wichtigste: The EU has 27 member countries (as of 2026).
In 1957 six countries founded the European Economic Community, which became the EU.
The European Parliament is elected every five years by the people in the EU countries.
The Parliament has its official seat in Strasbourg.
The United Kingdom left the EU on 31 January 2020.
Croatia was the last country to join, in 2013 (as of 2026).
The European anthem is Beethoven’s “Ode to Joy”.

abschnitte.text: After the Second World War, many countries in Europe wanted to work together so that there would be no more war. In **1957**, **six countries** founded the **European Economic Community**, **EEC** for short: Belgium, Germany, France, Italy, Luxembourg and the Netherlands. In time more and more countries joined. The EEC eventually became the **European Union**. In 2012 the EU received the **Nobel Peace Prize**.

Today the EU has **27 member countries** (as of 2026), among them Germany, France, Italy and Austria. **Croatia** joined in 2013 as the 28th country, and no new country has joined since. The **United Kingdom** left on **31 January 2020**. This departure is called **Brexit**. Several countries, above all in the Balkans, would still like to join the EU.

The EU has several important institutions. The **European Parliament** is elected every five years by the adults in the EU countries. Its official seat is in **Strasbourg** in France. The **European Commission** in **Brussels** proposes new laws. In the **Council of the EU** sit ministers from all the member countries, and they decide together with the Parliament.

The EU uses the blue **European flag** with twelve golden stars. The **European anthem** is a melody from the 9th Symphony by **Ludwig van Beethoven**, the “Ode to Joy”. The motto of the EU is “United in diversity”. Many EU countries also share a common currency, the **euro**. 9 May is Europe Day.

**Switzerland** is not a member of the EU, but lies right in the middle of EU countries. Almost all its neighbouring countries belong to the EU, only **Liechtenstein** does not. Switzerland has concluded many treaties with the EU, which are called the **Bilateral Agreements**. They regulate, for example, trade and travel. How closely Switzerland should work with the EU is discussed in Switzerland again and again.

gewusst: The EU received the Nobel Peace Prize in 2012.
The European anthem is mostly played without words so that it suits all languages.

teile.einleitung: The Basques are a people in the north of Spain and the south-west of France. They have their own very old language, which is related to no other language.
wichtigste: The Basques call their language Euskara.
Euskara is related to no other known language.
Vitoria-Gasteiz is the seat of the government and parliament of the Spanish Basque Country.
In 1937 the town of Gernika was bombed.
The organisation ETA announced its dissolution in 2018.
The Spanish Basque Country collects most of its taxes itself.

abschnitte.text: The Basques call their language **Euskara**, in English Basque. It is related to no other known language. Experts call this an **isolated language**. Basque was probably spoken before other European languages came to the area. Today many children in the Basque Country learn Euskara at school, alongside Spanish or French.

The Basque area lies on the **Bay of Biscay** on both sides of the **Pyrenees**. The larger part belongs to Spain, a smaller part to France. In Spain the Basque Country is an **autonomous community**. Government and parliament have their seat in **Vitoria-Gasteiz**. The largest city is **Bilbao** with the well-known Guggenheim Museum.

The Spanish Basque Country has a financial peculiarity: it **collects most of its taxes itself**. It pays part of this to the Spanish state for shared tasks. This old right is a sign of its great independence. It is a little reminiscent of **Switzerland**, where the cantons also levy their own taxes.

In the **Spanish Civil War**, the Basque town of **Gernika** was bombed by German and Italian aircraft on 26 April **1937**. The painter **Pablo Picasso** made his famous painting “Guernica” about it. Later the underground organisation **ETA** fought with violence for a Basque state of its own. In **2018** it announced its **dissolution**. Many Basques work peacefully for more independence, while others feel just as Spanish.

gewusst: The Basques are known for strength sports such as stone lifting and wood chopping as competitions.
The game of pelota, in which a ball is hit against a wall, is very popular in the Basque Country.

teile.einleitung: The Garonne is a large river in the south-west of France. It rises in the Pyrenees and flows past Toulouse and Bordeaux to the Atlantic. On its way it shapes cities, vineyards and trade routes.
wichtigste: The Garonne rises in the Val d’Aran in the Spanish Pyrenees.
Toulouse on the Garonne is called the “Ville rose” because of its brick buildings.
Bordeaux on the Garonne is world famous for its wine.
The Garonne and the Dordogne together form the funnel-shaped estuary Gironde.
The Canal du Midi connects the Garonne at Toulouse with the Mediterranean.
At high tide a wave called the mascaret runs upstream.

abschnitte.text: The **Garonne** rises in the **Val d’Aran**, a valley in the Spanish **Pyrenees**. Only after that does it flow into France. It is about 500 kilometres long and one of the great rivers of the country. On its way to the north-west it crosses fertile plains with fruit, vegetables and grain. Finally it reaches the **Atlantic**.

The largest city on the Garonne is **Toulouse**. Because of its reddish **brick buildings** it is called the “Ville rose”, the pink city. Toulouse is a European centre of **aviation and space**: many aircraft are built here and satellites developed. At Toulouse also begins the **Canal du Midi**, which was built in the 17th century and leads to the Mediterranean. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Further downstream lies the port city of **Bordeaux**. It is the centre of one of the best-known **wine-growing regions** in the world. The beautiful old town, with its pale stone houses by the river, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. For centuries wine has been shipped from here to many countries.

North of Bordeaux the Garonne joins the **Dordogne**. Together they form the **Gironde**, one of the largest estuaries in Europe. At high tide the sea pushes water into the Gironde. This creates a wave that runs upstream. It is called the **mascaret**, and some surfers even ride it.

gewusst: You can surf on the Garonne when the tidal wave, the mascaret, rolls upstream.
Together with a side canal along the Garonne, the Canal du Midi connects the Atlantic with the Mediterranean.

teile.einleitung: The Finnish Lakeland is a huge landscape of lakes, islands and forests in the south and centre of Finland. It is a legacy of the Ice Age and one of the regions richest in lakes in the world.
wichtigste: Finland has about 188,000 lakes larger than 500 square metres.
Most of the lakes were formed by glaciers of the Ice Age.
In the south the Salpausselkä end moraine ridge bounds the lakeland.
The land has been slowly rising since the Ice Age.
Lake Saimaa is connected to the sea by the Saimaa Canal.
Inland waters cover about a tenth of the area of Finland.

abschnitte.text: Finland is called the “land of a thousand lakes”, but has many more. About **188,000 lakes** larger than 500 square metres are counted. Lakes and rivers together cover about **34,000 square kilometres**, out of a land area of about 338,000 square kilometres. That is roughly **one tenth** of the country. Many lakes are linked by rivers and narrow channels, so that you can travel long distances by boat.

The lakeland lies on the **Baltic Shield**, an ancient plate of rock made of granite and gneiss that is over a billion years old. In the **Ice Age** mighty glaciers scoured hollows into the hard rock and left debris behind. After the ice melted, the hollows filled with water. In the south the **Salpausselkä** bounds the lakeland. This end moraine ridge formed when the edge of the ice stood still for a long time and deposited debris.

Typical of the region are **eskers**, long narrow ridges of sand and gravel. They formed from gravel that meltwater rivers deposited in tunnels under the glacier. A well-known example is the ridge **Punkaharju** in the Saimaa area. In addition, the land is still slowly rising today. The heavy ice had pressed the Earth’s crust downwards, and since the ice melted it has been springing back. This is called **isostatic uplift**.

The largest lake system is **Saimaa** in the east. Its water drains away through the river **Vuoksi**, which used to form famous rapids at Imatra. The Vuoksi flows into Russia and ends in **Lake Ladoga**. The **Saimaa Canal** was opened in 1856 and runs from Lappeenranta to Vyborg on the sea. Its southern part has been in Russia since 1944, and Finland has leased it since 1963.

In **Savonlinna**, the medieval castle **Olavinlinna** stands on an island. Since 1912 **opera festivals** have taken place there every summer. Many Finns have a **summer house** by the lakes, often with its own sauna. In winter the lakes freeze over, and you can ski or skate on them. In Switzerland many lakes were also formed by glaciers, but not in such great numbers.

gewusst: In Lake Saimaa lives the Saimaa ringed seal, a rare seal that occurs only in this freshwater lake.
Because the land is rising, lake shores and outflows in Finland are still changing very slowly today.

teile.einleitung: The Albanian Alps are a wild high mountain range in the north of Albania. Because of their rugged peaks they are also called the “Accursed Mountains”.
wichtigste: The Albanian Alps lie in the north of Albania.
They belong to the Prokletije mountains.
The Prokletije is the southernmost part of the Dinaric Alps.
They lie on the border with Montenegro and Kosovo.
The mountain villages of Theth and Valbona are well known.

abschnitte.text: The Albanian Alps are part of the **Prokletije**. The name means roughly “the bewitched” or “the accursed”. The range is the southernmost part of the **Dinaric Alps**, which stretch along the Adriatic across the Balkans. It lies on the border between Albania, **Montenegro** and **Kosovo**. The peaks consist mainly of pale **limestone** and are very steep.

In the valleys lie small **mountain villages**. The best known are **Theth** and **Valbona**. For a long time they were hard to reach, in winter often not at all. Today more and more hikers come. A popular trail leads over a pass from Valbona to Theth.

The Albanian Alps are among the wildest mountains in Europe. There are deep gorges, clear mountain streams and dense forests. In the remote areas, rare animals such as **brown bears** and **wolves** still live. Parts of the range are protected as a **national park**.

gewusst: Some mountain villages in the Albanian Alps used to be cut off from the outside world for months in winter.
Despite their name, the Albanian Alps do not belong to the Alps but to the Dinaric Alps.

teile.einleitung: Christiansborg is a large palace in the centre of Copenhagen. The Danish parliament, the government and the Supreme Court sit here. The palace thus stands for all three branches of power in Denmark.
wichtigste: Christiansborg Palace stands in Copenhagen, the capital of Denmark.
It lies on the small island of Slotsholmen.
The Danish parliament, the Folketing, meets in the palace.
The government and the Supreme Court also have their seat there.
The present palace is already the third building with this name.
Beneath the palace you can see remains of a medieval castle.

abschnitte.text: **Christiansborg** lies on the small island of **Slotsholmen** in the middle of **Copenhagen**. Canals surround the island. As early as the 12th century, Bishop Absalon had a castle built here. Its remains can be visited today beneath the palace. Later several palaces stood on this site.

abschnitte.titel: Three branches of power under one roof
abschnitte.text: In the palace the Danish parliament, the **Folketing**, meets. The official seat of the head of government and the **Supreme Court** are also here. So the three **branches of power** are under one roof: making laws, governing and administering justice. The royal family uses some state rooms for receptions and celebrations. In Switzerland the parliament and the Federal Council meet in the **Federal Palace** in Bern.

The first Christiansborg Palace burned down in 1794, the second in 1884. The present palace is therefore the **third building** with this name. It was built at the beginning of the 20th century. Its **tower** is one of the tallest in Copenhagen. From the top you have a wide view over the city.

gewusst: Christiansborg is one of the few buildings in the world in which parliament, government and Supreme Court sit together.
Beneath the palace lie the ruins of a castle from the 12th century.

teile.einleitung: The Adriatic Sea, or Adriatic for short, is an arm of the Mediterranean. It lies between Italy on the Apennine Peninsula and the countries of the Balkan Peninsula.
wichtigste: The Adriatic is a part of the Mediterranean.
It lies between the Apennine Peninsula and the Balkan Peninsula.
Italy lies on the west coast, Croatia, Montenegro and Albania on the east coast.
Croatia has over a thousand islands in the Adriatic.
The Po is the largest river that flows into the Adriatic.
The largest peninsula on the Adriatic is Istria.

abschnitte.text: The Adriatic is a long, narrow arm of the **Mediterranean** east of Italy. To the west lies **Italy**, and to the east lie **Slovenia**, **Croatia**, Bosnia and Herzegovina, **Montenegro** and **Albania**. Slovenia has only about 47 kilometres of coast, and Bosnia and Herzegovina only a very short stretch. In the south, the **Strait of Otranto** links the Adriatic with the Ionian Sea.

The Italian coast is mostly flat and has long **sandy beaches**, for example at the seaside resort of **Rimini**. The east coast, by contrast, is rocky and deeply indented. Off **Croatia** lie over a thousand islands. In the north the peninsula of **Istria** juts into the sea. Most of it belongs to Croatia, smaller parts to Slovenia and Italy.

Many well-known cities lie on the Adriatic. In the far north-east of Italy, near the border with Slovenia, lies the port city of **Trieste**. **Venice** is built on islands in a lagoon. Further south lie Ancona and Bari. On the eastern side, Split and Dubrovnik in Croatia are well known.

abschnitte.titel: The Po and the town of Adria
abschnitte.text: The **Po** is the longest river in Italy. It flows through the Po plain and enters the Adriatic south of Venice. The sea got its name from the town of **Adria**. In ancient times it was an important port. Today it lies about 20 kilometres from the sea, because the **Po** and the **Adige** have deposited so much sand and mud that the coast has moved eastwards.

The Adriatic is a popular holiday destination, also for many families from **Switzerland**. From Switzerland you can reach the Italian Adriatic coast in a few hours by car or train. In the north the sea is quite shallow and warm in summer. Further south the Adriatic becomes much deeper.

gewusst: The town after which the Adriatic is named no longer lies on the sea at all today.
Bosnia and Herzegovina has only a very short stretch of coast on the Adriatic, at the town of Neum.

teile.einleitung: The Algarve is the southernmost region of Portugal. It is known for plenty of sun, golden-yellow cliffs, grottoes and beautiful beaches, and is a popular holiday destination.
wichtigste: The Algarve lies at the very south of Portugal.
Its main town is Faro, with an international airport.
The coast is famous for cliffs, grottoes and beaches.
Cabo de São Vicente is the south-western tip of the European mainland.
Many oranges grow in the Algarve.
Grilled sardines are a popular dish.

abschnitte.text: The **Algarve** is a region in the south of **Portugal**. Its coast faces south onto the **Atlantic**. The name comes from Arabic and means “the west”. For centuries the Moors from North Africa ruled this area. In the north, hills and mountains such as the **Serra de Monchique** separate the Algarve from the rest of the country.

The coast of the Algarve is famous for its **golden-yellow cliffs**. Wind and waves have shaped arches, pillars and **grottoes** out of them. In small boats you can go into some of the caves. In between lie beautiful **sandy beaches**. In the east near Faro there is also a large lagoon landscape, the **Ria Formosa**.

**Faro** is the main town and administrative seat of the Algarve. Through its international **airport**, millions of holidaymakers arrive every year, many of them from Switzerland. Other well-known places are **Lagos**, **Portimão** and **Albufeira**. Many people come for the many sunny days, the warm summers and the beaches.

At the very south-west lies **Cabo de São Vicente**, in English **Cape St Vincent**, near the town of **Sagres**. It is the south-westernmost tip of the European mainland. The cliffs fall steeply into the sea, and on top stands a large **lighthouse**. Beyond it there is only the wide Atlantic.

In the mild climate, many **orange trees** grow. The oranges of the Algarve are known for their sweet taste. Almonds, figs and carob also thrive here. By the sea people like to eat fish, especially grilled **sardines**. In **Portimão** there is even a sardine festival of its own.

gewusst: The name Algarve comes from Arabic and means “the west”.
At Cabo de São Vicente, the European mainland ends in the south-west.

teile.einleitung: The Dnieper is a large river in Eastern Europe. It flows through Russia, Belarus and Ukraine into the Black Sea.
wichtigste: The Dnieper is about 2,200 kilometres long.
It rises in **Russia** and flows through **Belarus** and **Ukraine**.
It flows roughly from north to south and enters the **Black Sea**.
The capital **Kyiv** lies on the Dnieper.
The Dnieper is the longest river in Ukraine.
In many places dams were built to generate electricity.

abschnitte.text: The Dnieper rises west of Moscow in **Russia**. Then it flows through **Belarus** and on into **Ukraine**. It flows roughly from north to south. At the town of Kherson it enters the **Black Sea**. At about 2,200 kilometres it is among the longest rivers in Europe and the longest river in Ukraine.

The Ukrainian capital **Kyiv** lies on both banks of the Dnieper. On a hill above the river stand old churches and monasteries. Further south lies the large city of **Dnipro**, which is named after the river. Zaporizhzhia and Kherson also lie on the Dnieper. As early as the Middle Ages the river was an important trade route.

Many rivers flow into the Dnieper. One of the most important is the **Pripyat**. It comes from large marshlands in Belarus and in the north of Ukraine. A tributary is a river that flows into a larger river. Together they collect the water from a huge area.

In the 20th century several large **dams** were built on the Dnieper. Behind them long reservoirs formed. In the power stations the water drives turbines and so generates electricity. The water of the reservoirs is also used for fields and factories. The dams have greatly changed the landscape along the river.

gewusst: In Ukrainian the river is called Dnipro, just like the city.
The Dnieper divides Ukraine roughly into a western and an eastern part.

teile.einleitung: The Baltic States are Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania. The three countries lie on the Baltic Sea and became independent of the Soviet Union in 1990 and 1991.
wichtigste: The Baltic States are Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania.
They lie on the Baltic Sea.
The capitals are Tallinn, Riga and Vilnius.
All three pay with the euro; Estonia introduced it first.
In 1989 about two million people formed a human chain.
In 1990 and 1991 they became independent of the Soviet Union.

abschnitte.titel: Three countries on the Baltic Sea
abschnitte.text: The three **Baltic States** lie in north-eastern Europe on the **Baltic Sea**. Furthest north lies **Estonia** with the capital **Tallinn**. In the middle lies **Latvia** with the capital **Riga**. In the south lies **Lithuania** with the capital **Vilnius**. The landscape is flat, with many forests, lakes and long sandy beaches.

Each country has its own language. **Latvian** and **Lithuanian** belong to the **Baltic languages**, which are spoken only here today. **Estonian**, by contrast, is related to Finnish. In all three countries there is also a larger group of people whose mother tongue is Russian.

For a long time the three countries belonged to the **Soviet Union**. On 23 August **1989**, about **two million people** formed a **human chain** across all three countries, from Tallinn through Riga to Vilnius. It is called the **Baltic Way**. In this way people showed peacefully that they wanted to be free. In 1990 and 1991 the states became **independent**.

Since **2004** the Baltic States have been members of the **European Union** and of **NATO**. Today people pay with the **euro** in all three countries. **Estonia** introduced it first, in 2011. Latvia followed in 2014 and Lithuania in 2015. Estonia in particular is known for the fact that many visits to the authorities can be done digitally over the internet.

gewusst: The Baltic Way was about 600 kilometres long.
The old towns of Tallinn, Riga and Vilnius are all part of the UNESCO World Heritage.

teile.einleitung: Barcelona is the second-largest city in Spain and the capital of Catalonia. The city on the Mediterranean is famous for the buildings of Antoni Gaudí, the Rambla and FC Barcelona.
wichtigste: Barcelona lies on the Mediterranean.
It is the capital of the autonomous community of Catalonia.
Barcelona is the second-largest city in Spain.
Catalan and Spanish are spoken.
In Gaudí’s Park Güell sits a colourful mosaic lizard.
In 1992 the Summer Olympic Games took place here.

abschnitte.text: **Barcelona** lies in the north-east of Spain on the **Mediterranean**. After Madrid it is the **second-largest city** in Spain and the capital of the autonomous community of **Catalonia**. Besides Spanish, people speak **Catalan** here. The city has beaches and a large port, and lies between the sea and hills.

The architect **Antoni Gaudí** strongly shaped the look of Barcelona. His buildings have flowing shapes and colourful decoration. Best known is the church of the **Sagrada Família**, which has been under construction since 1882. In **Park Güell**, also designed by Gaudí, a colourful **lizard made of mosaic** sits on a staircase. Several of Gaudí’s works are UNESCO World Heritage sites.

The famous promenade is called **La Rambla**. It leads from the old town to the harbour. Under the trees, many people stroll past flower stalls, cafés and street performers every day. Right next to it lies the large market hall **La Boqueria** with fruit, fish and many other foods.

**FC Barcelona** is among the best-known football clubs in the world. Its large stadium is called **Camp Nou**. In 1992 the **Summer Olympic Games** took place in Barcelona. For the Games the city was greatly renewed, and many beaches by the sea were redesigned.

gewusst: Even over a hundred years after building began, the Sagrada Família is still not quite finished.
FC Barcelona was co-founded in 1899 by the Swiss Joan Gamper.

teile.einleitung: Åland is a group of islands in the Baltic Sea between Finland and Sweden. It belongs to Finland, but the people there speak Swedish. Åland manages many things itself.
wichtigste: Åland lies in the Baltic Sea between Finland and Sweden.
The island group is an autonomous region of Finland.
The only official language is Swedish.
Åland includes over 6,700 islands and skerries.
The main town is called Mariehamn.

abschnitte.text: Åland consists of over 6,700 islands and **skerries**. Skerries are small, flat rocky islands that the ice smoothed in the ice age. On most of the islands nobody lives. The largest island is also called Åland, and the main town **Mariehamn** lies there.

Åland belongs to **Finland** but is **autonomous**. This means the islands have their own parliament and decide many matters themselves. The only official language is **Swedish**, although elsewhere in Finland mainly Finnish is spoken. Åland also has its own flag and its own stamps.

After a dispute between Finland and Sweden, the **League of Nations** decided in 1921 that Åland belongs to Finland. At the same time, the rights of the Swedish-speaking population were protected. Åland is **demilitarised**: there are no soldiers and no fortresses there.

gewusst: On Åland, children at school do not have to learn Finnish but Swedish.
Young men from Åland do not have to do military service.

teile.einleitung: Flamenco is a passionate art from Spain. It includes singing, guitar playing, dance and rhythmic clapping.
wichtigste: Flamenco is music and dance at the same time.
It comes from Andalusia in the south of Spain.
The most important instrument is the guitar.
Spectators and musicians clap in time.
Dancers stamp in shoes that have small nails.
Since 2010 flamenco has been part of the UNESCO cultural heritage.

abschnitte.text: **Flamenco** is a Spanish art made of **singing**, **guitar playing** and **dance**. It is often very passionate and full of feeling. Some songs sound cheerful, others sad and serious. The singing is called **cante** in Spanish, the guitar playing **toque** and the dance **baile**. Spectators often shout “olé” when they like something especially well.

Flamenco comes from **Andalusia** in the south of Spain. There, many different peoples lived together over the centuries. In particular the Spanish **Gitanos**, a group of the Roma, shaped flamenco strongly. Influences from Arabic and Jewish music are also mentioned. To this day there are many **flamenco festivals** in Andalusia, for example in Seville.

The most important instrument is the **flamenco guitar**. It accompanies the singing and the dance. Many dancers hold **castanets** in their hands: two small wooden shells that you click together. Spectators and musicians **clap** their hands in rhythm, which is called **palmas**. The clapping is a firm part of the music.

Flamenco dancers stamp hard on the floor with their **shoes**. For this the shoes have small **nails** at the toe and heel, so that it sounds loud. This footwork is called **zapateado**. Typical **flamenco dresses** have many **ruffles** and are often spotted. When the dancer turns, the ruffles fly through the air with a swing.

In **2010** **UNESCO** added flamenco to the list of the intangible **cultural heritage of humanity**. In this way the art is to be protected and passed on. Today flamenco is danced and learned all over the world. In Switzerland too there are flamenco schools and performances. Many musicians mix flamenco with jazz or pop music.

gewusst: Flamenco shoes have small nails so that every step sounds loud.
In flamenco, the clapping of hands is an instrument of its own.

teile.einleitung: Bucharest is the capital and largest city of Romania. Because of its splendid buildings and wide boulevards, it got the nickname “Little Paris”.
wichtigste: Bucharest is the capital of Romania.
It is the largest city in the country.
Because of its buildings in the French style, it is called “Little Paris”.
Bucharest has a triumphal arch of its own.
The Palace of the Parliament is among the largest buildings in the world.
The river Dâmbovița flows through the city.

abschnitte.text: **Bucharest** lies in the south of **Romania**, in a wide plain not far from the Danube. The river **Dâmbovița** flows through the city. Bucharest is the largest city in the country and its political and economic centre. In Romania people speak **Romanian**, a language that descends from Latin, like French or Italian.

Around 1900, many buildings in the **French style** with wide **boulevards** were built in Bucharest. That is why the city got the nickname **Little Paris**. It even has a **triumphal arch** of its own, similar to the one in Paris. A well-known building from this period is the **Romanian Athenaeum**, a round concert hall with a dome.

A huge building is the **Palace of the Parliament**. It was built in the 1980s under the dictator **Nicolae Ceaușescu**. For it, the government had a large part of the old town demolished. The palace is among the largest buildings in the world. After the **revolution of 1989** the dictatorship ended, and today the Romanian parliament meets in the building.

abschnitte.titel: A village in the middle of the city
abschnitte.text: In Bucharest’s **Village Museum** stand old farmhouses, mills and churches from all over Romania. They were rebuilt there in the open air. This way you can see how people used to live in the countryside. A similar open-air museum exists in Switzerland at **Ballenberg** in the Bernese Oberland.

gewusst: The Palace of the Parliament in Bucharest is so large that it counts among the heaviest buildings in the world.
Bucharest has a triumphal arch that recalls the Arc de Triomphe in Paris.

teile.einleitung: Dalmatia is a region on the coast of Croatia. It is known for its many islands, its old towns of pale stone and the clear water of the Adriatic.
wichtigste: Dalmatia lies on the Adriatic coast in the south of Croatia.
The largest city is Split.
After Zagreb, Split is the second-largest city in Croatia.
Other well-known cities are Zadar, Šibenik and Dubrovnik.
Off the coast lie many islands such as Brač, Hvar and Korčula.
The dog breed Dalmatian is named after the region.

abschnitte.text: **Dalmatia** is a long, narrow strip of coast on the **Adriatic**. Behind the coast rise bare limestone mountains. In front of the mainland lie very many **islands**, for example **Brač**, **Hvar** and **Korčula**. The climate is Mediterranean: hot, dry summers and mild winters. Typical are olive trees, figs and grapevines.

**Split** is the largest city in Dalmatia and, after **Zagreb**, the second-largest city in Croatia. In the middle of the old town stands **Diocletian’s Palace**. The Roman emperor Diocletian had it built around the year 300. Later people built their houses into the palace walls. Today the palace is part of the **UNESCO World Heritage**. Many **ferries** sail from Split to the islands.

Along the coast old towns follow one after another, such as **Zadar**, **Šibenik**, **Trogir** and, in the far south, **Dubrovnik** with its mighty city wall. Many of these towns belonged for a long time to the Republic of **Venice**. You can see this from their churches, squares and lion figures. Inland lies the **Krka** National Park with waterfalls.

The dog breed **Dalmatian** with its black spots is named after this region. Also well known are the winds of Dalmatia: the cold **bora** plunges down from the mountains in winter. The warm, damp **jugo** comes from the south and often brings high waves and rain.

gewusst: In the old town of Split, people still live today in houses built into the walls of a Roman imperial palace.
The dogs with the black spots are named after the region of Dalmatia.

teile.einleitung: Big Ben is one of the most famous landmarks of London. Strictly speaking, though, Big Ben is not a tower but the largest bell in the clock tower at the British Parliament.
wichtigste: Big Ben is the name of the great bell in the clock tower.
Often the whole tower is also called Big Ben.
Since 2012 the tower has officially been called the Elizabeth Tower.
It belongs to the Palace of Westminster, where the British Parliament meets.
Big Ben strikes on every full hour.
The bell rang for the first time in the year 1859.

abschnitte.text: Many people think Big Ben is the tower. In reality **Big Ben** is the largest bell in it. It weighs more than 13 tonnes. Where exactly the name comes from is not quite certain. It is often supposed to go back to Sir Benjamin Hall, who was in charge of the building work at the time. In everyday speech most people nevertheless say Big Ben when they mean the whole tower.

The clock tower stands in **London** at the **Palace of Westminster**, right on the Thames. The British **Parliament** meets in this building. The tower is almost 100 metres high. For a long time it was simply called the Clock Tower. In **2012** it was renamed **Elizabeth Tower** in honour of Queen Elizabeth II, because she had been on the throne for 60 years.

On all four sides of the tower is a huge **clock face**. The clock is regarded as very accurate. On every full hour Big Ben **strikes** with a deep note that can be heard far around. Smaller bells play a melody every quarter of an hour. In Great Britain the striking of the hours has been broadcast on the radio for a long time.

Big Ben rang for the first time in **1859**. Soon afterwards the bell developed a **crack**. It was turned a little and a lighter hammer was used, and since then it has sounded somewhat different. From **2017 to 2022** the tower was thoroughly renovated. During this time the bell was mostly silent and rang only on special occasions.

gewusst: Big Ben has had a crack for over 150 years and still keeps ringing.
The tower was named in 2012 after Queen Elizabeth II.

teile.einleitung: The Baščaršija is the old bazaar in the old town of Sarajevo, the capital of Bosnia and Herzegovina. With its narrow lanes and workshops it is the heart of the city.
wichtigste: The Baščaršija is the old bazaar of Sarajevo.
It arose in the 15th century under the Ottomans.
Craftsmen still work in the lanes today.
On the main square stands the wooden fountain Sebilj.
Nearby stands the Gazi Husrev-beg Mosque.

abschnitte.text: The **Baščaršija** arose in the **15th century**, when Sarajevo belonged to the **Ottoman Empire**. The name comes from Turkish and means roughly “main market”. Here lay the centre of trade and crafts at that time. Nearby stands the large **Gazi Husrev-beg Mosque** from the 16th century, one of the most important mosques in the country.

The Baščaršija consists of many **narrow lanes** with small shops. In the past each craft had its own lane. To this day you can hear the **coppersmiths** hammering in one lane, making coffee pots and plates. Beside them are cafés where you drink Bosnian coffee, and small restaurants serving **ćevapi**, grilled minced-meat rolls.

On the main square stands the **Sebilj**, a pretty wooden **fountain** with a small roof. It is the best-known landmark of the Baščaršija. Many **pigeons** often sit around the fountain. A legend says that whoever drinks from it will return to Sarajevo.

gewusst: In Sarajevo, mosques, churches and a synagogue stand very close together.

teile.einleitung: The elk is the largest deer in the world. It lives in the cool forests of the north of Europe, Asia and America and is a true symbol of Scandinavia.
wichtigste: The elk is the largest species of deer in the world.
A bull elk can be over 2 metres tall at the shoulder.
Many bulls carry broad, palmate antlers.
Elks eat only plants: leaves, twigs, bark and water plants.
Elks are very good swimmers.
In Sweden, road signs warn of elks on the road.

abschnitte.text: The elk is the largest deer there is. A fully grown bull can be over **2 metres** tall at the shoulder and weigh several hundred kilograms. Elks have very long legs, a short tail and a broad, overhanging nose. Under the neck there often hangs a flap of skin called a **bell** or dewlap. With their long legs they get through deep snow and boggy ground well.

Only the male animals, the **bull elks**, carry antlers. In many they are broad and flat like a shovel, which is why they are called **palmate antlers**. Every winter the bull sheds his antlers, and in spring a new pair grows. The female animals are called **cows**, the young **calves**. The calves are born in spring and stay with their mother for about a year.

Elks are pure **plant eaters**. In summer they eat leaves, herbs and, with pleasure, **water plants**, which they look for on the shore or even in the water. In winter they nibble twigs, buds and the **bark** of trees. They need large amounts for this, because their body is heavy. That is why they often move slowly through wide forests and moors.

Elks can **swim** surprisingly well. They cross wide rivers and lakes and can cover long distances in doing so. The water also helps them against heat in summer and against annoying mosquitoes. Their dense coat keeps them warm even when it is very cold. So elks are well adapted to life in the north.

In **Sweden**, Norway and Finland many elks live. Because they often cross roads, special **warning signs** with an elk on them stand there. A collision with such a large animal is dangerous for drivers. That is why people there drive especially carefully at dusk. For tourists, the elk sign is a popular photo subject.

gewusst: The famous “Elchtest” (elk test) is a driving test for cars: it checks whether a car can swerve safely around a sudden obstacle.
In North America the animal is called a “moose” in English.
An elk can dip its head under water to eat water plants.

teile.einleitung: Lake Garda is the largest lake in Italy. It lies on the southern edge of the Alps and is a popular holiday destination, including for many families from Switzerland. In the north it is narrow and surrounded by mountains, in the south wide and flat.
wichtigste: Lake Garda, at about 370 km², is the largest lake in Italy.
It borders the regions of Lombardy, Veneto and Trentino.
The Mincio flows out of the lake at Peschiera and later ends in the Po.
On the Sirmione peninsula stands a moated castle from the 13th century.
In the north strong winds blow regularly, which surfers and sailors love.
On the east shore rises Monte Baldo.

abschnitte.text: **Lake Garda** is about **370 km²** and so the largest lake in Italy. It is almost twice as big as Lake Maggiore. The lake lies entirely in Italy and borders three regions: the west shore belongs to **Lombardy**, the east shore to **Veneto** and the northern tip to **Trentino**. It was formed by a great glacier in the Ice Age.

From the north the **Sarca** flows into the lake. In the south the **Mincio** leaves it near the town of **Peschiera**. It flows past Mantua and finally ends in the **Po**, the longest river in Italy. The northern part of the lake is narrow like a fjord and surrounded by steep mountains. The southern part is wide and framed by gentle hills.

On the south shore the narrow **Sirmione** peninsula juts into the lake. There stands the **Scaliger Castle** from the 13th century, surrounded by water. On the east shore rises the long mountain ridge of **Monte Baldo**, which is over 2,200 metres high. From **Malcesine** a cable car leads up. At the top you have a wide view over the whole lake.

In the north reliable winds blow almost daily: in the morning the **Pelèr** from the north, in the afternoon the **Ora** from the south. That is why the area around Riva and Torbole is very popular with **surfers** and **sailors**. Thanks to the mild climate, olive trees and even lemons grow by the lake. By the way, Lake Garda lies entirely in Italy, whereas the northern part of **Lake Maggiore** with Locarno belongs to the canton of **Ticino**.

gewusst: Olive trees and lemons grow at Lake Garda, even though it lies on the edge of the Alps.
The town of Limone sul Garda used to be known for its lemon gardens.

teile.einleitung: The Belgian waffle is a crisp pastry with a pattern of small squares. In Belgium there are two famous kinds: the Brussels and the Liège waffle.
wichtigste: Waffles are baked in a waffle iron.
A waffle has a pattern of small squares.
The Brussels waffle is rectangular, light and has deep holes.
The Liège waffle is roundish and has crunchy pieces of sugar.
For the batter you need flour, eggs and milk, among other things.
Waffles are often eaten with icing sugar, strawberries and whipped cream.

abschnitte.text: Waffles are baked in a **waffle iron**. It consists of two hot plates with a pattern. You pour the batter in, close the iron and wait until the waffle is golden brown. This creates the typical pattern of **small squares**. Many waffle irons for home bake waffles in the shape of **hearts**.

For a simple waffle batter you need **flour**, **eggs** and **milk**, among other things. Sugar, butter and a pinch of salt are usually added. For Belgian waffles the batter is often made with **yeast**, to make it airy. It then has to rest and rise for a while.

The **Brussels waffle** is **rectangular**, light and crisp and has **deep holes**. The **Liège waffle** became known in the city of **Liège**. It is **roundish**, denser and sweeter. In its dough are coarse **pieces of sugar**, which caramelise during baking and become crunchy. Liège waffles are often eaten simply out of the hand.

On a waffle people often sprinkle white **icing sugar**. **Strawberries** with **whipped cream** or melted chocolate are also popular. Some like to pour **maple syrup** over it, a sweet syrup from the sap of the maple tree from **Canada**. In Belgium, waffles are often bought warm from street stalls.

gewusst: Waffle irons have existed since the Middle Ages.
The German word “Waffel” is related to the word “Wabe” (honeycomb), because of the pattern.

teile.einleitung: Estonia is a small country on the Baltic Sea. It is regarded as one of the most digital countries in the world, because almost all dealings with the authorities can be done over the internet.
wichtigste: Since 2001, authorities and companies have exchanged their data over the platform **X-Road**.
Since the local elections of 2005, people in Estonia can vote bindingly over the internet.
At the end of 2014 Estonia introduced **e-Residency**, a digital identity also for foreigners.
The internet telephone service **Skype** was largely developed in 2003 by Estonian programmers.
In 2007 cyber attacks paralysed many websites in Estonia.
Under the **once-only principle**, the state may ask for the same data only once.

abschnitte.text: Estonia became independent of the Soviet Union in 1991. The country had little money but wanted to become modern. In 1996 the programme **Tiger Leap** began, in Estonian “Tiigrihüpe”. It equipped schools with computers and an internet connection. So many children learned early how to use computers.

Since 2001 there has been the platform **X-Road**. It is decentralised, meaning the data stay with the individual offices and are only exchanged securely when they are needed. In addition the **once-only principle** applies: the state may ask citizens for data only once. Anyone who moves house therefore does not have to report the new address to each office separately. With an electronic identity card you can identify yourself and sign documents digitally.

In the local elections of 2005, people in Estonia could vote bindingly over the internet for the first time. Estonia was thus one of the first countries in the world to do so. Today a large share of voters cast their vote online in elections. In Switzerland too, electronic voting, **e-voting**, is being tested in some cantons. But there particular attention is paid to security.

The internet telephone service **Skype** was developed in 2003 to a large extent by programmers from Estonia. This made the country known in the tech world. At the end of 2014 Estonia introduced **e-Residency**. With it, people from other countries can also receive a digital identity of Estonia and, for example, set up a company online. But this does not make them Estonian citizens.

In 2007 a wave of **cyber attacks** hit the country. Websites of banks, media and authorities were hardly reachable for days. Afterwards Estonia greatly expanded its cyber defence. In 2008 a **NATO Cooperative Cyber Defence Centre of Excellence** was founded in Tallinn. Since 2017, Estonia has stored backup copies of important state data in a **data embassy** in Luxembourg.

gewusst: The Estonian data embassy in Luxembourg is a server room that is especially protected, like an embassy.
The electronic identity card has existed in Estonia since 2002.

teile.einleitung: Lake Sihl is an artificial lake in the canton of Schwyz, right next to the monastery town of Einsiedeln. It was created in the 1930s to generate electricity. By area it is the largest reservoir in Switzerland.
wichtigste: Lake Sihl is a reservoir and was flooded in 1937.
It lies in the canton of Schwyz next to Einsiedeln at about 890 metres above sea level.
At about 11 square kilometres, it is the largest reservoir in Switzerland by area.
Its water drives the Etzelwerk power station in Altendorf on Lake Zurich.
Farms and houses in the valley had to be given up for the lake.
In winter the lake often freezes over.

abschnitte.text: Lake Sihl lies in the **high valley** of Einsiedeln in the canton of Schwyz. The Sihl, a river that later flows through Zurich, is dammed up here. The lake is about 8 kilometres long but only about 23 metres deep at most. Two long bridges, the viaducts of Willerzell and Euthal, cross the lake.

There were plans early on to use the water of the Sihl to make electricity. In the 1930s a **dam** was built, and in 1937 the lake began to be flooded. Meadows, moors and farms disappeared under the water. Many families had to move away, which caused a lot of argument and sadness at the time.

The water of Lake Sihl flows through a tunnel through the Etzel mountain. It then plunges down pressure pipes to the **Etzelwerk** in Altendorf on Lake Zurich. There it drives turbines that generate electricity. A large part of this electricity is meant for the trains of the **SBB**.

Right next to the lake lies **Einsiedeln** with its famous Benedictine monastery. The monastery is an important place of pilgrimage with the Black Madonna. Many pilgrims come here every year. An outing often combines a visit to the monastery with a walk by the lake.

In summer you can swim, sail and fish in Lake Sihl. Because the high valley is cold, the lake often freezes over in winter, and then you can go ice skating. Around the lake lie valuable **moorlands**, which are now protected. Rare plants and birds live there.

begriffe.erklaerung: A lake that forms when a river is dammed up with a wall or an embankment.
A strong wall that holds back the water of a river.
A plant that turns turbines with flowing water and so generates electricity.
A long bridge over a valley or a lake.

gewusst: When the water level is very low, remains of old walls and paths from the time before the flooding sometimes appear in Lake Sihl.
The water of Lake Sihl does not end up in the Sihl but is led over the Etzel into Lake Zurich.

teile.einleitung: The Dardanelles are a strait in Turkey. They link the Sea of Marmara with the Aegean and separate Europe from Asia.
wichtigste: The Dardanelles are about 60 kilometres long.
In ancient times they were called the **Hellespont**.
On the Asian shore lies the town of **Çanakkale**, on the European the **Gallipoli** peninsula.
In 1915 the Battle of Gallipoli took place here in the First World War.
The Çanakkale Bridge of 2022 has the longest span of any suspension bridge.
Together with the Bosphorus and the Sea of Marmara they form the **Turkish Straits**.

abschnitte.text: A **strait** is a narrow waterway between two pieces of land. The Dardanelles are about 60 kilometres long and in some places only a little over a kilometre wide. On one side lies Europe with the Gallipoli peninsula, on the other Asia with the town of Çanakkale. Together with the Sea of Marmara and the Bosphorus at Istanbul, they form the **Turkish Straits**. They are the only sea route from the Black Sea into the Mediterranean.

The ancient Greeks called the strait the **Hellespont**, which means “sea of Helle”, after a figure from a legend. Near the Asian shore lay the ancient city of Troy. A well-known legend tells of Leander, who swam across the Hellespont every night. In 1810 the English poet **Lord Byron** swam across the strait to show that it was possible.

In the First World War, Great Britain and France wanted in 1915 to conquer the Dardanelles in order to open a sea route to Russia. The Ottoman Empire defended the strait. The **Battle of Gallipoli** lasted many months and cost very many lives on both sides. In the end the attackers withdrew. In Australia, New Zealand and Turkey, this battle is still remembered today.

For a long time there were only ferries across the Dardanelles. In 2022 the **Çanakkale Bridge** was opened. It is a suspension bridge: the roadway hangs from thick steel cables between two tall towers. Its span, that is, the distance between the towers, is over 2,000 metres and so the longest in the world. Until then a bridge in Japan held the record.

gewusst: The span of the Çanakkale Bridge is 2,023 metres, to match the 100th anniversary of the Turkish Republic in 2023.
Today many people swim every year from Europe to Asia through the Dardanelles in a competition.

teile.einleitung: Bornholm is a Danish island in the middle of the Baltic Sea. It lies far to the east of the rest of Denmark, between Sweden and Poland, and is known for its rocky coasts and round churches.
wichtigste: Bornholm belongs to Denmark and lies in the Baltic Sea.
The island lies between the south coast of Sweden and Poland.
It is about 150 kilometres to Copenhagen.
The main town is called Rønne.
The four medieval round churches are well known.
The castle ruin of Hammershus is among the largest in northern Europe.

abschnitte.text: **Bornholm** lies much closer to Sweden than to the rest of Denmark. It is about 150 kilometres to **Copenhagen**. Many travellers come by ferry via the Swedish port of Ystad. The main town and most important port is **Rønne**. Unlike the mostly flat Denmark, Bornholm has steep **granite rocks** and cliffs in the north.

Famous are the four **round churches** from the Middle Ages. They are built perfectly round and have thick white walls. In the past they served not only as churches but also as places of refuge in times of danger. In the north of the island stands the castle ruin of **Hammershus** high above the sea. It is among the largest castle ruins in northern Europe.

For a long time many people on Bornholm lived from **fishing**. Well known is the smoked **herring**, which is produced in smokehouses with tall chimneys. Today the island is a popular holiday destination with sandy beaches in the south. Because it is often sunny there, Bornholm is sometimes called the Sun Island.

gewusst: At the end of the Second World War, Bornholm was occupied by Soviet troops for about a year; they did not leave until 1946.
The round churches of Bornholm are almost 900 years old.

teile.einleitung: Florence is a famous city in Italy and the capital of Tuscany. The Renaissance began here, and to this day the city is full of works of art, palaces and churches.
wichtigste: In Italian the city is called Firenze.
Florence is the capital of Tuscany and lies on the River Arno.
On the Ponte Vecchio stand small shops, mostly of goldsmiths.
The cathedral has a huge red dome.
Michelangelo’s David and the Uffizi make Florence a city of art.
From 1865 to 1871 Florence was the capital of Italy.

abschnitte.text: The Italians call their city **Firenze**, and in English it is called **Florence**. It is the capital of the region of **Tuscany**, which is known for its gentle hills. Right through the city flows the **Arno**, which several bridges cross. The old town is part of the **UNESCO World Heritage**. Every year millions of tourists come to Florence.

The oldest bridge is called the **Ponte Vecchio**, which means “old bridge”. On it stand many small **shops**, and today it is mainly **goldsmiths** who sell their jewellery there. The landmark of the city is the **cathedral** with its mighty **dome** of red bricks. It was built in the 15th century to plans by the master builder **Filippo Brunelleschi**. If you climb many steps, you have a wide view from the top.

Florence is regarded as the birthplace of the **Renaissance**, a time when art and science flourished. **Michelangelo** created the **David** here from a single large block of marble. The figure is over five metres high. The original now stands in a museum, and a copy stands on a square in the old town. In the **Uffizi** museum hang many world-famous paintings.

For a long time the rich **Medici** family ruled over Florence. The Medici were **bankers** and became very powerful through their business. They supported many artists, builders and scholars. Without their money, many of the city’s works of art would not exist today. Some popes also came from the Medici family.

In Florence the poet **Dante Alighieri** was born, who lived over 700 years ago. He is regarded as the most important poet of Italy, and his language shaped today’s **Italian**. When Italy became a kingdom, Florence was its capital from **1865 to 1871**. After that **Rome** became the capital. In 1966 Florence suffered a severe **flood** of the Arno, which damaged many works of art.

gewusst: The dome of the cathedral of Florence is over 500 years old and is still one of the largest masonry domes in the world.
Today’s Italian is based to a large extent on the language that was once spoken in Florence.

teile.einleitung: Bulgaria is one of the countries whose population is shrinking fastest. Since the end of the 1980s the country has lost about a quarter of its inhabitants. Here you find out why this is and what the consequences are.
wichtigste: In the 2021 census, Bulgaria had about 6.5 million inhabitants.
At the end of the 1980s, almost 9 million people still lived in the country.
The main reasons for the decline are emigration and more deaths than births.
In 1989 about 360,000 Bulgarian Turks left the country for Turkey.
After joining the EU in 2007, many people moved to other EU countries to work.
The capital Sofia is growing, while many villages are emptying.
The north-west is regarded as the poorest region in the whole EU.

abschnitte.text: At the end of the 1980s, Bulgaria reached its peak with almost **9 million** inhabitants. In the 2021 **census** there were only about 6.5 million. Between 2011 and 2021 alone, the number fell by about 840,000 people. A census is a survey in which the state counts all residents. Hardly any other country in Europe has lost so many inhabitants in such a short time.

After the end of communism in 1989, hundreds of thousands went abroad, mainly young people. This is called **emigration**. With **EU accession in 2007**, Bulgarians were gradually allowed to work in other EU states, from 2014 at the latest without restrictions. Many looked there for higher wages. The **health service** is particularly affected: numerous doctors and nursing staff now work, for example, in Germany.

In the 1980s, the communist government forced the **Turkish minority** to change their names and restricted their language and religion. In the summer of 1989, about **360,000 people** therefore left the country for Turkey. The government called this departure, in a whitewashing way, the “Great Excursion”, that is, a big outing. Some of the people later returned to Bulgaria. The event is an important part of the country’s population history.

In Bulgaria, for years clearly more people have died than children have been born. This is also because many young adults have moved away and the population is on average older. Surprisingly, according to Eurostat, Bulgaria had in 2023 the highest **birth rate** in the EU, at about 1.81 children per woman. Even so the country is shrinking, because emigration and the high number of deaths have a stronger effect.

Within the country, many people move from the countryside to the capital **Sofia**. Sofia is the economic centre and one of the few regions with a growing population. Many villages, by contrast, are **ageing**, that is, mainly older people live there. The **north-west** around towns such as Vidin and Vratsa is hit hardest. According to Eurostat, this region has the lowest income per head in the EU.

gewusst: In some villages in Bulgaria, only a few older people still live, and some are even completely empty.
Although Bulgaria had the highest birth rate in the EU in 2023, its population keeps falling.

teile.einleitung: Alpine transit is the name for the traffic of people and goods across the Alps. Switzerland plays an important role in it and relies mainly on the railway.
wichtigste: The first Gotthard railway tunnel was opened in 1882.
The Gotthard road tunnel of 1980 is about 17 kilometres long.
With NEAT, Switzerland built flat base tunnels through the Alps.
The Alps Initiative of 1994 wants to move goods onto the railway.
Lorries have paid the LSVA since 2001.
The Brenner is one of the busiest Alpine passes.

abschnitte.text: For a long time, travellers had to struggle over the Alpine passes. That changed in **1882** with the first **Gotthard railway tunnel**. The tunnel, about 15 kilometres long, links **Göschenen** in the canton of Uri with **Airolo** in Ticino. The building was dangerous and difficult, and over 190 workers lost their lives. The tunnel made the Gotthard one of the most important north-south routes in Europe.

In **1980** the **Gotthard road tunnel** was opened. It is 16.9 kilometres long and also links Göschenen with Airolo. Since then, many cars and lorries drive through it every day. Because the tunnel has to be renovated, a **second tube** has been under construction since 2021. This way traffic can keep rolling during the renovation.

With **NEAT**, the New Rail Link through the Alps, Switzerland built long **base tunnels**. They lie deep down in the mountain, so that trains can run almost on the flat. In 2007 the first to open was the **Lötschberg Base Tunnel**, about 35 kilometres long, between the Bernese Oberland and Valais. In 2016 followed the **Gotthard Base Tunnel**, which at 57 kilometres is the longest railway tunnel in the world. In 2020 the **Ceneri Base Tunnel** between Bellinzona and Lugano completed the flat route.

In **1994** the Swiss people accepted the **Alps Initiative**. It demands that goods traffic through the Alps should go by rail as far as possible instead of by lorry. Since 2001, lorries have paid the **LSVA**, the performance-related heavy vehicle charge. It depends on the kilometres driven and the weight. Part of the money went into building NEAT. On the **Rolling Motorway**, whole lorries travelled on goods trains, and the drivers rode in a carriage for accompanying staff.

Other countries also know Alpine transit. The **Brenner** between Austria and Italy is one of the busiest Alpine passes. Every year millions of lorries drive over the motorway there. Beneath it, a long **Brenner Base Tunnel** is being built for the railway, so that more goods can go by rail there too.

gewusst: At 57 kilometres, the Gotthard Base Tunnel is the longest railway tunnel in the world.
Thanks to the base tunnels, trains between Zurich and Lugano are much faster than they used to be.

teile.einleitung: Very many people live in Europe, but they are unevenly distributed. There are countries with many millions of inhabitants, tiny states and areas where hardly anyone lives.
wichtigste: Germany has the most inhabitants in the EU (as of 2024).
Russia has the most inhabitants overall of all countries with territory in Europe (as of 2024).
Vatican City has the fewest inhabitants.
Monaco has the highest population density in Europe; in the EU it is Malta.
Iceland has the lowest population density.
In Switzerland about 9 million people lived in 2024.

abschnitte.text: In 2024 about **450 million** people lived in the **European Union**. The country with the most inhabitants in the EU is **Germany**. If you count all the countries with territory in Europe, **Russia** has the most inhabitants overall. Most of the Russian population lives in the European part of the country, west of the Urals.

**Vatican City** in Rome is the smallest state in the world and has the **fewest inhabitants** in Europe, only a few hundred. Monaco, San Marino and Liechtenstein also have few inhabitants. But **Monaco** has the **highest population density**: on a very small area many people live close together. Among the EU countries, **Malta** is the most densely populated.

**Population density** tells you how many people live on average on one **square kilometre**. You work it out by dividing the number of inhabitants by the area of the country. The density is lowest in **Iceland**. There is a lot of ice, lava and mountains there, and most people live around the capital Reykjavík.

In 2024 about **9 million** people lived in **Switzerland**. Most live on the **Central Plateau** between Lake Geneva and Lake Constance. In the Alps, by contrast, there are wide areas with only a few inhabitants. About a quarter of the people in Switzerland do not have a Swiss passport. The **Federal Statistical Office** counts the population every year.

Many people in Europe live in **cities**. Among the largest cities are **Moscow**, **London** and **Istanbul**, which lies partly in Europe. In many European countries, people are on average getting older and older. So the share of **older people** is rising, which matters, for example, for the **AVS** (old-age insurance) in Switzerland.

gewusst: Fewer people live in Vatican City than in many Swiss villages.
Monaco is smaller than many Swiss municipalities but has tens of thousands of inhabitants.

teile.einleitung: The Eiffel Tower is a huge iron tower in Paris. It is the best-known landmark of France and is visited by millions of people every year.
wichtigste: The Eiffel Tower was built for the **World Fair** of 1889.
It is about 330 metres tall.
For visitors there are **three levels**.
In the evening it **sparkles** with many lights on every full hour.
About every **7 years** it is repainted.

abschnitte.titel: A tower for the World Fair
abschnitte.text: In 1889 a large **World Fair** took place in Paris. It also commemorated the French Revolution of 1789, which had begun 100 years earlier. The firm of **Gustave Eiffel** built the tower for it. It consists of many thousands of iron parts joined with rivets. The building took only a little over two years.

The Eiffel Tower is about **330 metres** tall, including the antennas on top. When it was built, it was the tallest structure in the world. It held this record for about 40 years. For visitors there are **three levels**. You can take the lift, or as far as the second level you can also take the stairs.

Iron rusts when it gets wet. That is why the Eiffel Tower is repainted about **every 7 years**. For this many tonnes of paint are needed, and the painters work by hand. The paint is a special shade of brown, called “Eiffel Tower brown”.

In the evening the Eiffel Tower is lit up. On every **full hour** it **sparkles** for a few minutes with thousands of small lights. It looks as if it were glittering. Many people come specially in the evening to see this. Originally the tower was meant to be taken down again after 20 years. But because it was useful for radio and science, it stayed standing.

gewusst: In summer the Eiffel Tower can become a few centimetres taller because of the heat, as the iron expands.
Many artists at first found the tower ugly and protested against its building.

teile.einleitung: Lake Victoria is the largest lake in Africa and lies in East Africa. Three countries share its shores: Uganda, Kenya and Tanzania. The White Nile flows out of it, one of the two source rivers of the Nile.
wichtigste: Lake Victoria lies in Africa, more precisely in East Africa.
It is about 68,000 square kilometres in area and so the largest lake in Africa.
By area it is the second-largest freshwater lake in the world.
Uganda, Kenya and Tanzania border the lake.
At Jinja in Uganda, the White Nile leaves the lake.
