It was named after Queen Victoria in 1858 by the Briton John Hanning Speke.
For millions of people the lake is important for fishing and drinking water.

abschnitte.text: Lake Victoria lies almost exactly on the **equator**, at about 1,130 metres above sea level. The largest part belongs to **Tanzania**, followed by **Uganda** and Kenya. At about 68,000 square kilometres, it is about 1.6 times as large as Switzerland. But it is only about 80 metres deep at most, so quite shallow for its size.

At the town of **Jinja** in Uganda, the **White Nile** flows out of the lake. It flows north through Sudan, where it joins the Blue Nile in Khartoum. For a long time European explorers searched for the source of the Nile. John Hanning Speke reached the lake in 1858 and rightly guessed that the Nile begins here.

In the past, hundreds of species of small, colourful **cichlids** lived in the lake, found nowhere else. In the 1950s the large **Nile perch** was introduced, and it ate many of these species. Today the Nile perch is an important food fish that is also sold to Europe. Many fishing families live from catching it in small wooden boats.

Many islands lie in the lake, the largest being **Ukerewe** in Tanzania. On the shore lie larger cities such as Kampala in Uganda, Mwanza in Tanzania and Kisumu in Kenya. Ferries link the harbours of the three countries. Millions of people live around the lake.

Sewage and fertiliser from cities and fields pollute the water. This makes the **water hyacinth** grow, a floating plant that at times covered large parts of the shore. It hinders boats and takes light and oxygen from the fish. The three countries work together to protect the lake.

begriffe.erklaerung: An imaginary line around the middle of the Earth.
One of the two great source rivers of the Nile; it begins at Lake Victoria.
A group of mostly colourful fish, of which Lake Victoria had many species of its own.
A floating plant that spreads very quickly and can make lakes overgrown.

gewusst: In Lake Victoria, hundreds of different cichlid species developed from a few ancestors, which fascinates researchers all over the world.
Only Lake Superior in North America is larger than Lake Victoria as a freshwater lake.

teile.einleitung: Anatolia is the large peninsula between the Black Sea and the Mediterranean. It is also called Asia Minor, and it makes up about 97 per cent of the area of Turkey.
wichtigste: Anatolia is also called Asia Minor.
The name comes from the Greek word for sunrise.
Anatolia makes up about 97 per cent of the area of Turkey.
Mount Ararat is the highest mountain in Turkey.
The Euphrates and the Tigris rise in eastern Anatolia.
The Hittites and the city of Troy belong to the ancient history of Anatolia.

abschnitte.text: The name **Anatolia** comes from Greek: **anatole** means sunrise. Seen from Greece, the land lay in the east, where the sun rises. Another name is **Asia Minor**. The peninsula lies between the **Black Sea** in the north and the **Mediterranean** in the south. In the west it borders the Aegean.

Almost the whole of **Turkey** lies in Anatolia, about 97 per cent. Only a small part in the north-west, **Eastern Thrace**, belongs to Europe. Between them lie the **Bosporus** and the **Dardanelles**. The capital **Ankara** lies in the middle of Anatolia. In the heart of the peninsula there is a wide highland, and in **Cappadocia** stand famous rock formations.

In the east, Anatolia is very mountainous. There stands **Mount Ararat**, a volcano about 5,137 metres high and the highest mountain in Turkey. According to the Bible, Noah’s Ark is said to have come to rest there. In the highlands of eastern Anatolia the great rivers **Euphrates** and **Tigris** also rise. They flow through Syria and Iraq, and between them lies Mesopotamia. **Lake Van** is the largest lake in Turkey and about seven times as large as Lake Constance.

Anatolia has a very long history. In the 2nd millennium BC, the **Hittites** ruled large parts of the peninsula. Their capital **Hattusa** is now a UNESCO World Heritage site. In the north-west near the Dardanelles lay **Troy**, the city from the legend of the fight for Helen. **Heinrich Schliemann** excavated its ruins from 1871. Later Anatolia belonged to the Roman, the Byzantine and the Ottoman Empires.

gewusst: Lake Van is a soda lake in which only very few species of fish can live.
The name Anatolia literally means “sunrise”.

teile.einleitung: Belgrade is the capital of Serbia. The city lies where the Sava flows into the Danube, and its name means “White City”.
wichtigste: Belgrade is the capital of Serbia.
In Belgrade the Sava and the Danube meet.
The Kalemegdan fortress sits above the rivers.
The name means “White City”.
The Temple of Saint Sava is a huge church with a large dome.
The money in Serbia is called the dinar.

abschnitte.text: **Belgrade** lies where the **Sava** flows into the **Danube**. The city is the capital of **Serbia** and one of the largest cities in the Balkans. Its name means **“White City”**, probably because of pale stone walls. Belgrade is very old and in its history was often conquered and rebuilt.

High above the confluence stands the old **Belgrade Fortress**. The park around the fortress is called **Kalemegdan**. From there you have a wide view over both rivers. In the fortress there are walls, gates, towers and a military museum. Today Kalemegdan is a popular place for walks.

The **Temple of Saint Sava** is a huge church with a large dome. It is dedicated to Saint **Sava**, an important saint of the **Serbian Orthodox Church**. The building is among the largest Orthodox churches in the world. Inside, large mosaics gleam in gold.

In Serbia two scripts are used: the **Latin** and the **Cyrillic script**. On many signs you see both. People pay with the **dinar**. Belgrade’s airport is named after the famous inventor **Nikola Tesla**. In Belgrade there is also a museum about him and his inventions.

gewusst: In the Sava near Belgrade lies the peninsula of Ada Ciganlija with a lake where people swim in summer.
The unit of magnetic flux density is called the “tesla”, after Nikola Tesla.

teile.einleitung: The Göta Canal is an artificial waterway right across Sweden. It links the great lakes Vänern and Vättern with the Baltic Sea. Together with rivers and lakes, it forms a shipping route from Gothenburg to the Baltic Sea.
wichtigste: The Göta Canal runs right across Sweden.
It links the lakes Vänern and Vättern with the Baltic Sea.
It was completed in 1832.
The canal has 58 locks.
Today it is used mainly by excursion boats and leisure boats.

abschnitte.text: The **Göta Canal** runs right across the south of **Sweden**. It links the two largest lakes in the country, **Vänern** and **Vättern**, with the **Baltic Sea**. Together with rivers and other lakes, it forms a waterway from **Gothenburg** on the west coast to the east coast. Ships no longer had to sail around the southern tip of Sweden.

The canal was completed in **1832**. It was built mostly by hand, with shovels and wheelbarrows, and many **soldiers** helped. Because the land between the lakes is higher than the sea, the canal needs **58 locks**. A **lock** is like a water lift: a chamber is filled or emptied until the ship is at the right height.

For freight, the canal was soon overtaken by railways. Today it is used mainly by **excursion boats** and leisure boats. Many people walk or cycle along the old **towpaths** on the bank, where horses used to pull the boats. In Sweden the canal is also called the “blue ribbon”.

gewusst: An excursion boat needs several days to travel the whole length of the canal.
In the past, horses pulled the boats along the canal from the bank.

teile.einleitung: The Dalmatian coast lies in the south of Croatia on the Adriatic. It is so typically shaped that geographers have named a whole type of coast after it.
wichtigste: The Dalmatian coast is a **longitudinal coast**: islands and mountains run parallel to the shore.
The long islands are the ridges of mountain chains that were flooded by the sea.
The mountains belong to the **Dinarides** and run from north-west to south-east.
The most important rock is **limestone**, so there are many karst features.
The city of Split grew out of the palace of the Roman emperor Diocletian.
Since 2022 the Pelješac Bridge has linked southern Dalmatia directly with the rest of Croatia.

abschnitte.titel: A type of coast of its own
abschnitte.text: On the Dalmatian coast, mountain ridges, islands and sea channels run in the same direction as the coastline. This is called a **longitudinal coast** or channel coast. Between the islands lie narrow sea channels. Well-known islands are, for example, Brač, Hvar and Korčula. From above, the coast looks as if someone had laid long stripes into the sea.

After the last ice age, huge masses of ice melted, and the sea level rose sharply. The water of the Adriatic filled the valleys between the mountain chains. Only the crests of the mountains still stick out and today form the islands. The mountains belong to the **Dinarides**, a mountain range that reaches from the Slovenian Karst to Albania. Because the Dinarides run from **north-west to south-east**, the islands lie that way too.

The mountains and islands consist mainly of **limestone**. Rainwater contains a little carbonic acid and slowly dissolves the limestone. This creates caves, sinkholes and rivers that flow underground. This landscape is called **karst**. Behind the Makarska Riviera rises the steep limestone range of **Biokovo**; its highest peak, Sveti Jure, is about 1,760 metres high. The river **Krka** forms waterfalls of tufa in a national park near Šibenik.

Around the year 300 AD, the Roman emperor **Diocletian** had a large palace built on the coast as a retirement home. Later people moved into the palace walls, and the town of **Split** grew out of it. Further south lies Dubrovnik with its famous city wall. Zadar and Šibenik also have beautiful old towns. Many holidaymakers visit the coast every summer.

At Neum a short stretch of coast belongs to Bosnia and Herzegovina. Anyone driving from Split to Dubrovnik therefore used to have to cross a border twice. Since 2022 the **Pelješac Bridge** has linked the mainland with the Pelješac peninsula. So you can reach the south of Croatia without crossing a border.

gewusst: Before the last ice age, the islands off Dalmatia were mountain peaks on the mainland.
In Split, houses and lanes still stand today within the walls of a Roman imperial palace.

teile.einleitung: England is the largest and most populous part of the United Kingdom. The capital London lies here, and the English language, modern football and many famous poets come from here.
wichtigste: England belongs, with Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, to the United Kingdom.
Over 80 per cent of the people in the United Kingdom live in England.
The capital is London on the Thames.
The flag is the St George’s Cross: a red cross on a white background.
The Pennines are called the “backbone of England”.
In England the Industrial Revolution began in the 18th century.

abschnitte.text: The **United Kingdom** consists of four parts: England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland. England is the largest of them, both in area and in population. Over **80 per cent** of the kingdom’s inhabitants live here. The capital **London** lies on the **Thames** and is one of the largest cities in Europe. The parliament and the king are also based there.

abschnitte.titel: The flag with the St George’s Cross
abschnitte.text: The flag of England is called the **St George’s Cross**. It shows a red cross on a white background. The Swiss flag is coloured exactly the other way round: a white cross on a red background. The St George’s Cross is also part of the **Union Jack**, the flag of the whole kingdom. At football matches you see the English flag especially often.

The south and the middle of England are rather flat or hilly. The **Pennines** stretch from central England almost to the Scottish border. Because they run from south to north, they are called the **backbone of England**. In the north-west lies the **Lake District** with many lakes and the highest mountain in England, Scafell Pike. On the south coast there are pale chalk cliffs, for example near Dover.

In England the **Industrial Revolution** began in the 18th century. Steam engines and factories were built that changed the whole world. Very old is the stone monument **Stonehenge**, which was built thousands of years ago. The poet **William Shakespeare** came from England and is regarded as one of the most important writers in the world. The English language is spoken on all continents today.

England is regarded as the motherland of modern **football**. Here the first fixed rules were written down in the 19th century. Rugby, cricket and tennis also have a long tradition in England, for example the tournament at **Wimbledon**. Typically English are afternoon tea and the red double-decker buses in London. On the roads people drive on the left.

gewusst: The Swiss flag and the English flag have exactly swapped colours.
The English Football Association was founded as early as 1863.

teile.einleitung: Budapest is the capital of Hungary. The Danube flows through the middle of the city and divides it into Buda and Pest. Budapest is known for its huge parliament, its bridges and its warm baths.
wichtigste: Budapest is the capital of Hungary.
The Danube divides the city into Buda and Pest.
In 1873 Buda, Óbuda and Pest were united into one city.
The first underground line was opened in 1896.
The parliament on the Danube is one of the largest in the world.
Many warm springs feed large thermal baths.

abschnitte.text: The **Danube** flows through the middle of Budapest. On the right bank lie the hilly **Buda** and **Óbuda**, on the left bank the flat **Pest**. In **1873** the three towns were united into one city. Many bridges link the banks. The most famous is the **Chain Bridge** with two pairs of stone lions. It was the first permanent bridge between Buda and Pest.

On **Castle Hill** in Buda stands the large **Castle Palace**, where the kings of Hungary once lived. Beside it lies the **Fisherman’s Bastion**, a viewing terrace from around 1900. Its **seven small towers** recall the seven Hungarian tribes that once came into the land. From there you can see far over the Danube to the parliament.

On the bank of the Danube in Pest stands the Hungarian **parliament** with its large **dome**. It is among the largest parliament buildings in the world. It looks especially beautiful in the evening when it is lit up and reflected in the water. In the middle of the Danube also lies the green **Margaret Island**, a large park where hardly any cars drive.

Beneath Budapest there are many **warm springs**. Their water fills large **thermal baths**, for example the **Széchenyi Baths**, where you can sit outside in the warm water even in winter. Budapest also has one of the oldest underground railways in Europe: the first line ran in **1896**. It was the first electric underground railway on the European continent and is still running today.

gewusst: In the Széchenyi Baths some people play chess in the warm water, even when there is snow outside.
The old underground line of Budapest is part of the UNESCO World Heritage together with the banks of the Danube.

teile.einleitung: Benelux stands for Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg. The three neighbouring countries have worked closely together since the Second World War and were thus a model for European unification.
wichtigste: The Benelux Union consists of Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg.
In 1944 the governments in exile in London agreed a customs union.
Belgium is a federal state with three regions.
About a quarter of the Netherlands lies below sea level.
The Randstad is the urban area with Amsterdam, Rotterdam, The Hague and Utrecht.
The language border in Belgium was fixed by law in 1962 and 1963.

abschnitte.text: During the Second World War, the governments of Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg sat **in exile in London**. There in **1944** they agreed a **customs union**. Goods were to be traded between the three countries without customs duties. From this idea the **Benelux Union** arose. Later all three were among the founders of the European community from which the **EU** grew.

**Belgium** is a **federal state** with **three regions**: Flanders, Wallonia and Brussels. The **language border** between the Dutch-speaking north and the French-speaking south was fixed by law in **1962 and 1963**. The highest point of Belgium, the **Signal de Botrange**, lies in the **High Fens**, an upland moor in the east. In the north-east lies the sandy landscape of **Kempen**, which in the 20th century was a **coalfield**.

In the **Netherlands**, **about a quarter** of the area lies **below sea level**. Dykes, pumps and canals protect the country from water. In the west lies the **Randstad**, a large urban area with **Amsterdam**, **Rotterdam**, **The Hague** and **Utrecht**. Very many people live here in a small space.

After a severe storm surge in 1953, the Netherlands built large flood defences, the **Delta Works**. The **Oosterschelde** was not closed off completely. Instead a **storm surge barrier** with movable gates was built. They stay open most of the time and are closed only in a storm. This way **tides** and the **salt-water habitat** are preserved.

The port of **Antwerp** in Belgium is linked to the **North Sea** by the river **Scheldt**. But the mouth of the Scheldt lies in the Netherlands. So the two countries have to work together here. Rotterdam at the mouth of the Rhine is the largest port in Europe, and goods from **Switzerland** are also shipped through it.

gewusst: The word Benelux is made up of the beginnings of Belgium, Nederland and Luxembourg.
Luxembourg is the only grand duchy in the world.

teile.einleitung: The Dovrefjell is a mountain range in the middle of Norway. It is a wide, bare plateau and famous for its wild musk oxen.
wichtigste: The Dovrefjell lies in the interior of **Norway**.
Wild **musk oxen** live here.
The musk oxen were brought here from **Greenland** in the 20th century.
A large part of the range is a **national park**.
Wild **reindeer** also live in the Dovrefjell.

abschnitte.titel: A high mountain range in Norway
abschnitte.text: The Dovrefjell is a high plateau; in Norwegian such a thing is called a **fjell**. There are hardly any trees there, but mainly moss, lichen and low shrubs. The highest mountain is the **Snøhetta**, whose name means “snow cap”. For a long time important routes, and today also a railway line, have crossed the Dovrefjell. It links the south of Norway with the area around Trondheim.

Musk oxen are large, shaggy animals with a thick coat that protects them from great cold. In the past they no longer lived in Norway. In the 20th century animals from **Greenland** were brought to the Dovrefjell. Today a wild herd lives there. Hikers must keep a good distance, because musk oxen can attack if you get too close.

A large part of the range belongs to the **Dovrefjell-Sunndalsfjella National Park**. Here animals and plants are especially protected. Besides the musk oxen, wild **reindeer** and the rare **Arctic fox** also live in the area. Many people come to hike and to watch the animals.

gewusst: When in danger, musk oxen form a circle with their horns pointing outwards to protect their young.
The Dovrefjell appears in old Norwegian legends and songs and is regarded as the home of the trolls.

teile.einleitung: Gibraltar is a small territory at the southern tip of Spain with a mighty limestone rock. It has belonged to Great Britain for over 300 years. Just a few kilometres across the water lies Africa.
wichtigste: Gibraltar is a British overseas territory at the southern tip of Spain.
In the Peace of Utrecht in 1713, Gibraltar went to Great Britain.
The Strait of Gibraltar is only about 14 km wide at its narrowest point.
People pay with the Gibraltar pound, which is tied to the British pound.
In 2002 almost 99 per cent rejected shared sovereignty with Spain.
Spain still claims Gibraltar to this day.

abschnitte.text: Gibraltar lies at the southern tip of the **Iberian Peninsula**. The **Rock of Gibraltar** rises above the small town. At its narrowest point, the **Strait of Gibraltar** separates Europe from Africa by only about **14 km**. In clear weather you can see Morocco. In ancient times the Greeks called the rocks on both sides the **Pillars of Hercules**. For them they marked the end of the known world.

In the **War of the Spanish Succession**, British and Dutch troops captured Gibraltar. In the **Peace of Utrecht** of **1713**, Spain gave the territory to Great Britain. Spain still wants it back. In **1969** Spain under Franco closed the land border completely. From 1982 pedestrians were allowed to cross again, and the border was fully opened in 1985.

Today Gibraltar is a **British overseas territory** with its own government. The United Kingdom is responsible for foreign policy and defence. The people have voted several times: as early as 1967 a large majority was in favour of Great Britain. In the **referendum of 2002**, almost **99 per cent** rejected shared British and Spanish sovereignty. People pay with the **Gibraltar pound**, and British pounds are accepted as well.

At Gibraltar's airport there is something unusual: **pedestrians cross the runway**. In the past the main road to the Spanish border crossed the landing strip. Since 2023 cars have driven through a **tunnel**. On foot, though, you can still cross the runway when no aircraft is taking off or landing. On the African side opposite lies **Ceuta**, a city that belongs to Spain.

gewusst: Barbary macaques live on the Rock of Gibraltar, the only wild monkeys in Europe.
The name Gibraltar comes from Arabic and means “mountain of Tariq”.

teile.einleitung: The Apennines are the long mountain range that runs the length of Italy. They are often called the backbone of Italy.
wichtigste: The Apennines lie in Italy.
They run the length of the Apennine Peninsula.
The highest mountain is the Corno Grande.
The range continues in Sicily.
Wolves survived in the Apennines.
The Alps are higher than the Apennines.

abschnitte.text: The **Apennines** run like a **backbone** from north to south through Italy. They are over a thousand kilometres long. The peninsula on which they lie is named after them, the **Apennine Peninsula**. In the north they join the Alps, in the south they reach as far as Calabria. On the island of **Sicily** the range continues.

The highest mountain is the **Corno Grande** in the **Gran Sasso** massif in the Abruzzo. It is a good 2,900 metres high. This makes the Apennines clearly lower than the **Alps**, whose highest peaks reach over 4,000 metres. Many mountains are wooded and have rounded shapes. Because Earth’s plates meet here, there are repeated **earthquakes** in the Apennines.

In the Apennines rise important rivers of Italy. The **Arno** flows through **Florence** and Pisa to the sea. The **Tiber**, the river of Rome, also begins in the Apennines. The rivers are mostly shorter than in the Alps, because the sea is never far away.

In the forests of the Apennines the **wolf** survived when it had vanished from many other areas of Europe. From here wolves have spread again as far as the Alps and **Switzerland**. In the Abruzzo, rare **brown bears** also live. Several **national parks** protect this nature.

On the edge of the Apennines lies the small country of **San Marino**. Its capital sits on Monte Titano. San Marino is entirely surrounded by Italy and is regarded as one of the oldest republics in the world.

gewusst: The wolves in Switzerland originally descend from wolves of the Apennines.
Geologically, the Apennines count as a younger mountain range that is still moving.

teile.einleitung: The Channel Tunnel (Eurotunnel) connects England and France under the English Channel. Passenger trains, freight trains and car shuttle trains run through it, and it is one of the greatest structures in Europe.
wichtigste: The tunnel runs from Folkestone in England to Coquelles near Calais in France.
Construction began in 1988 on both sides at the same time.
In December 1990 the construction teams met under the sea.
About 38 kilometres of the tunnel lie under the seabed.
The boring went mainly through chalk marl.
By car shuttle the journey takes about 35 minutes.

abschnitte.text: The **Eurotunnel**, also called the Channel Tunnel, runs under the **English Channel**. It begins at **Folkestone** in England and ends at **Coquelles** near Calais in France. The tunnel is about 50 kilometres long, of which about **38 kilometres** lie under the seabed. That is the longest underwater section of any railway tunnel in the world. It was opened in **1994**.

Construction work began in **1988** at the same time on the British and the French side. Huge **tunnel boring machines** dug towards each other. In **December 1990** the **breakthrough** was made in the service tunnel. A British and a French worker shook hands through the hole. With that, Great Britain and the European mainland were connected by land for the first time since the Ice Age.

The tunnel follows a layer of **chalk marl**. This rock is soft enough to be bored easily. At the same time it lets hardly any **water** through, which is very important under the sea. The engineers had to find the layer exactly and follow it. The lowest point lies about 75 metres below sea level.

The Eurotunnel consists of **three tubes**: one for the trains in each direction and a **service tunnel** in the middle. The service tunnel is used for maintenance and as an escape route. With the **car shuttle** you drive your car straight onto the train and stay sitting in it. The journey from terminal to terminal takes about **35 minutes**, and by ferry it takes much longer. High-speed trains go on from there to London, Paris and Brussels.

gewusst: Before the Eurotunnel, you could not get from England to the mainland with dry feet since the Ice Age.
The Gotthard Base Tunnel in Switzerland is longer, but does not run under the sea.

teile.einleitung: The Elbe is one of the great rivers of central Europe. It rises in the Czech Republic, flows through Germany and enters the North Sea.
wichtigste: The Elbe rises in the **Czech Republic**, where it is called the **Labe**.
It is about 1,100 kilometres long.
The **Vltava**, which flows through Prague, joins the Elbe.
On the Elbe lie **Dresden**, **Magdeburg** and **Hamburg**.
It flows through the **Elbe Sandstone Mountains**.
At **Cuxhaven** it enters the **North Sea**.

abschnitte.text: The Elbe rises in the **Giant Mountains** in the **Czech Republic**. In Czech it is called the **Labe**. In the Czech Republic the **Vltava** flows into the Elbe. The Vltava comes from the south and flows through the middle of Prague. After that the Elbe becomes a large river and flows into Germany.

On the border between the Czech Republic and Germany, the Elbe flows through the **Elbe Sandstone Mountains**. There stand oddly shaped rocks of sandstone, like towers and tables. Part of it is called **Saxon Switzerland**. It was given this name in the 18th century by two Swiss artists, who were reminded of their homeland by the landscape.

Soon after the mountains the Elbe reaches **Dresden**. There stands the famous **Frauenkirche** (Church of Our Lady), which was destroyed in the Second World War and later rebuilt. Further downstream lies **Magdeburg**, the capital of Saxony-Anhalt. Then comes the large port city of **Hamburg**. Its port is one of the largest in Europe.

After Hamburg the Elbe grows ever wider. At **Cuxhaven** it enters the **North Sea**. In all it is about 1,100 kilometres long. The ebb and flow of the North Sea can be felt as far as Hamburg. That is why even large container ships can sail from the sea into the port of Hamburg.

gewusst: Saxon Switzerland got its name from two Swiss painters, Adrian Zingg and Anton Graff.
In the flood of August 2002 the Elbe in Dresden rose to over 9 metres.

teile.einleitung: Greece has thousands of islands, but only a small number of them are inhabited. Most lie in the Aegean Sea and the Ionian Sea. Each group of islands has its own history and landscape.
wichtigste: The Aegean Sea between Greece and Turkey is full of islands.
Santorini, Mykonos and Naxos belong to the Cyclades.
The ancient palace of Knossos is on Crete.
Corfu is one of the Ionian Islands and lies close to Albania.
Euboea is the second largest island of Greece after Crete.
People usually travel between the islands by ferry.

abschnitte.titel: The Aegean Sea and the Cyclades
abschnitte.text: The **Aegean Sea** is a part of the Mediterranean between Greece and Turkey. Very many Greek islands lie in it. A well-known group is the **Cyclades**. They include **Santorini**, **Mykonos** and **Naxos**. On Mykonos, round white **windmills** stand on a hill, where grain was once ground.

**Crete** is the largest island of Greece. The **Palace of Knossos** is there, which is very old and is one of the best-known excavations in the country. On **Rhodes** there once stood the **Colossus of Rhodes**, a giant statue of the sun god **Helios**. It was one of the **Seven Wonders** of the ancient world. An earthquake knocked it over long ago.

Off the west coast of Greece lies the **Ionian Sea**. The **Ionian Islands** include **Corfu**, Kefalonia and Zakynthos. Corfu lies in the north-west, very close to **Albania**, and from there you can see the Albanian coast. **Ithaca** also lies in this sea. In the ancient legend it is the home of the hero **Odysseus**, who travelled for ten years before he got home.

The sea lies between the islands, so many people travel from island to island by **ferry**. Large ships link the islands with the port of Athens. The second largest island, **Euboea**, on the other hand, lies close to the mainland, north-east of Athens. It is connected to the mainland by **bridges**. Many islands today depend heavily on **tourism**.

gewusst: The Colossus of Rhodes was one of the Seven Wonders of the ancient world.
You can drive to the island of Euboea by car over a bridge.

teile.einleitung: Lake Zug is a lake in Central Switzerland on which the city of Zug lies. At its southern end rises the Rigi, the Queen of the Mountains. The area is also known for the Zug cherry cake and for a disaster in 1887, when part of the town slid into the lake.
wichtigste: Lake Zug is about 38 square kilometres in area and up to about 200 metres deep.
It lies in the cantons of Zug, Schwyz and Lucerne.
On the north shore lies the city of Zug, and at the southern end rises the Rigi.
The Lorze flows into the lake and leaves it again at Cham.
In 1887, in the Vorstadt disaster, part of Zug slid into the lake.
The famous Zug cherry cake comes from Zug.
A special fish in the lake is the Zug Rötel.

abschnitte.text: Lake Zug lies at about 413 metres above sea level between the **Zugerberg** and the **Rigi**. It is about 14 kilometres long and is divided into a northern and a southern part by a peninsula at Immensee. On the shore lie places such as Zug, Cham, Walchwil, Immensee and Arth. Most of its area belongs to the canton of Zug, the south to Schwyz and a small piece to Lucerne.

The **Lorze** flows into the lake and leaves it again at Cham. Because only a little water flows through the lake, it is exchanged only slowly. In the depths there is therefore very little oxygen. In the past, fertiliser and sewage led to a lot of **algae growth**; today much is being done to make the water cleaner.

On 5 July 1887, a piece of shore in Zug broke off and slid into the lake, houses and all. This disaster is called the **Vorstadt disaster** because the Vorstadt district was affected. Several people died, and many families lost their homes. The cause was soft, loose ground on the shore that had become unstable through building work.

The **Zug cherry cake** was invented in the early 20th century by the pastry chef Heinrich Höhn in Zug. It consists of nut layers, sponge and buttercream and is soaked in **kirsch**, a spirit made from cherries. Around Lake Zug there have long been many cherry trees. The cake is known all over the world today.

In Lake Zug lives the **Zug Rötel**, a species of char whose belly shimmers reddish. In Zug it counts as a speciality. In summer passenger ships sail on the lake, and you can swim, row and sail. From the shore at Zug you can often watch beautiful sunsets over the lake.

begriffe.erklaerung: A well-known viewpoint mountain between Lake Zug and Lake Lucerne.
When a piece of ground suddenly slides away.
A spirit distilled from cherries.
A fish from the salmon family that lives in cold, clean lakes.

gewusst: In the Vorstadt disaster of 1887, houses disappeared into Lake Zug within a few minutes.
The Zug cherry cake is cut into small pieces because the kirsch makes it taste quite strong.
The Hollow Lane, where William Tell is said to have lain in wait for Gessler, lies only a few minutes from Lake Zug.

teile.einleitung: The Ebro is a large river in the north-east of Spain. It flows from the Cantabrian Mountains to the Mediterranean and gave its name to the whole Iberian Peninsula.
wichtigste: The Ebro flows entirely within **Spain**.
It is about 900 kilometres long.
It rises in the **Cantabrian Mountains** and enters the **Mediterranean**.
It is the longest river that runs entirely in Spain.
The large city of **Zaragoza** lies on the Ebro.
At its mouth it forms a **delta** where a lot of **rice** is grown.

abschnitte.text: The Ebro rises in the **Cantabrian Mountains** in the north of Spain. From there it flows south-east through a wide depression, the Ebro Basin. At the end it reaches the **Mediterranean** between Barcelona and Valencia. At about 900 kilometres it is the longest river that runs **entirely in Spain**. The Tagus is longer, but also flows through Portugal.

The largest city on the Ebro is **Zaragoza**, the capital of the region of Aragon. There, right on the river, stands the large Basilica del Pilar. Logroño, known for the wine of the Rioja region, also lies on the Ebro. The water of the river is used for fields, cities and power stations. In the dry landscape it is very important.

At its mouth the Ebro deposits sand and mud. So a large **river delta** has formed that juts far out into the sea. On the flat, damp areas a lot of **rice** is grown. In the delta there are also lagoons and beaches where many birds live, for example flamingos. A large part is protected as a **nature park**.

The ancient Greeks and Romans called the river **Iber** or Iberus. After it they named the land and the people who lived there. This is where the name **Iberian Peninsula** comes from, to which Spain and Portugal belong today. So the river gave its name to a whole peninsula.

gewusst: The Ebro Delta is among the largest wetlands on the western Mediterranean.
In the Ebro live very large catfish, which attract anglers from all over Europe.

teile.einleitung: The Alps are the highest mountain range lying entirely in Europe. They sweep in a great arc through eight countries and cover about 60 per cent of the area of Switzerland.
wichtigste: The Alps form an arc about 1,200 kilometres long.
Eight countries have a share of the Alps.
About 60 per cent of Switzerland lies in the Alps.
The highest mountain is Mont Blanc.
Most of the 4,000-metre peaks of the Alps lie in Switzerland.
The ibex and the marmot are typical Alpine animals.

abschnitte.text: The Alps stretch in a **great arc** from the Mediterranean coast near Nice to the **Vienna Woods** near Vienna. The arc is about 1,200 kilometres long. Eight countries have a share of it: **France**, **Monaco**, **Italy**, **Switzerland**, **Liechtenstein**, **Germany**, **Austria** and **Slovenia**. In Austria almost two thirds of the country lie in the Alps, in Switzerland about 60 per cent.

The highest mountain in the Alps is **Mont Blanc** on the border between France and Italy, at over 4,800 metres. Mountains more than 4,000 metres high are called **four-thousanders**. Most of the four-thousanders in the Alps lie in Switzerland, especially in **Valais**. The best known is the **Matterhorn** near Zermatt, which looks like a sharp pyramid. The highest mountain entirely in Switzerland is the **Dom**, and the highest point of Switzerland is the **Dufourspitze**.

The Alps are a **fold mountain range**. They formed because the African Plate slowly pressed against the European Plate. Over millions of years, layers of rock were folded and pushed upwards. Later, huge **glaciers** shaped the valleys in the ice ages. The largest glacier in the Alps is the **Great Aletsch Glacier** in Valais.

High up in the rocks climbs the **Alpine ibex**. The males have long, curved horns. The **marmot** warns its family with a loud whistle when an eagle or fox approaches. Then they all quickly vanish into the burrow. Other Alpine animals are the chamois, the golden eagle and the bearded vulture.

The Alps are a home for millions of people and an important **water tower** of Europe: great rivers such as the **Rhine**, the **Rhône** and the Inn rise here. So that nature and people can live together well, the Alpine countries signed the **Alpine Convention** in **1991**. It works for the protection of nature and for **sustainable development** in the Alpine region.

gewusst: The ibex was wiped out in Switzerland in the 19th century and was later reintroduced.
Because of the pressure of the Earth’s plates, the Alps are still growing by a few millimetres a year.

teile.einleitung: The Azores are a group of volcanic islands in the middle of the Atlantic. They belong to Portugal, and the Azores High, which also influences the weather in Switzerland, is named after them.
wichtigste: The Azores consist of nine main islands.
They belong to Portugal.
The largest island is São Miguel.
At about 2,351 metres, the volcano Pico is the highest mountain in Portugal.
The Azores High is named after the islands.
At the Azores, three of the Earth’s plates meet.

abschnitte.text: The **Azores** lie far out in the Atlantic, far west of the Portuguese mainland. They consist of **nine main islands** and belong to **Portugal**. The island group is an **autonomous region**, so it decides many matters itself. The largest island is **São Miguel** with the town of Ponta Delgada. On São Miguel even tea is grown.

The Azores were formed from **volcanoes**. Near them, three **lithospheric plates** meet: the **North American**, the **Eurasian** and the **African Plate**. That is why there are earthquakes and hot springs here. On the island of Pico stands the volcano **Pico**, at about **2,351 metres** the highest mountain in Portugal. In 1957 and 1958, the volcano **Capelinhos** erupted off the island of **Faial**. Afterwards many people emigrated from the Azores to the **USA**.

Over the Atlantic near the Azores there is often a **high-pressure area**. It is called the **Azores High**. When it extends in summer as far as central Europe, it also brings sunny, warm weather to **Switzerland**. Weather experts therefore watch it closely.

On the island of **Terceira** lies the town of **Angra do Heroísmo**. Its old town has been a UNESCO World Heritage site since **1983**. In the past many ships stopped here on the way between Europe and America. Today visitors come for the green landscape, the crater lakes and the **whales** that can be watched off the islands.

gewusst: On São Miguel, a stew is cooked in the hot volcanic ground.
The Azores lie so far out in the Atlantic that part of them lies on the North American Plate.

teile.einleitung: The Gulf of Bothnia is the northernmost part of the Baltic Sea. It lies between Sweden and Finland and is often covered with ice in winter.
wichtigste: The Gulf of Bothnia lies between Sweden in the west and Finland in the east.
It is the northernmost part of the Baltic Sea.
Its water has very little salt.
In winter it often freezes over.
It consists of the Bothnian Bay in the north and the Bothnian Sea in the south.
Between them lies the strait of Kvarken.

abschnitte.text: A **gulf** is a large bay of the sea. The **Gulf of Bothnia** reaches far north from the Baltic Sea. To the west lies **Sweden**, to the east **Finland**. In the north it is called the **Bothnian Bay**, in the south the **Bothnian Sea**. The two parts are separated by a narrow place full of islands, the **Kvarken**. At the southern end lie the Åland Islands.

Many rivers bring fresh water into the gulf. That is why its water has very **little salt**, in the north almost like fresh water. Water with little salt freezes more easily than salty water. Because it also gets very cold so far north, the gulf is often covered with **ice** in winter. **Icebreakers** then keep the shipping channels to the ports open.

In the last **ice age**, a thick sheet of ice pressed the land down. Since the ice melted, the ground has been slowly rising again, in some places by almost a centimetre a year. This is called **land uplift**. As a result new islands appear and the coast shifts. The High Coast in Sweden and the islands of the Kvarken in Finland are therefore part of the **UNESCO World Heritage**.

gewusst: Because of the land uplift, some old port towns now lie some distance from the sea.
In cold winters you can even walk on the sea ice in parts of the Bothnian Bay.

teile.einleitung: Gotland is the largest island in the Baltic Sea. It belongs to Sweden and is known for its medieval capital Visby. The island is flat and sunny and has special rocks made of limestone.
wichtigste: Gotland is the largest island in the Baltic Sea.
The island belongs to Sweden.
It covers around 3000 square kilometres.
The capital Visby has a medieval city wall.
Visby is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

abschnitte.titel: The largest island in the Baltic Sea
abschnitte.text: **Gotland** lies in the **Baltic Sea**, east of the Swedish mainland. It covers around **3000 square kilometres**, so it is a little bigger than the canton of Ticino. The island belongs to **Sweden** and can be reached from the mainland by ferry. The ground is mostly made of **limestone**. Gotland is considered one of the sunniest parts of Sweden.

The capital **Visby** was a rich trading town of the **Hanseatic League** in the Middle Ages, an alliance of merchants and towns around the North Sea and the Baltic Sea. Even today a long **medieval city wall** with many towers surrounds the old town. There are also many church ruins. Because of its good condition, Visby is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.

On the coasts of Gotland and the neighbouring island of **Fårö** stand strangely shaped **limestone pillars**. They are called **raukar**. They formed because waves and weather wore away the softer rock around them over a very long time. A small, sturdy breed of horse also lives on Gotland, the **Gotland pony**.

gewusst: The city wall of Visby is more than three kilometres long and is still almost completely preserved.
From a distance, the limestone pillars on Gotland's coasts look like figures.

teile.einleitung: Belgium is a small kingdom in western Europe. It is known for waffles, chocolate, comics and for three languages being spoken here, similar to Switzerland.
wichtigste: Belgium has three official languages.
At the head of the country stands a king.
The flag is black, yellow and red.
Belgium became independent in 1830.
The praline and the Smurfs come from Belgium.
Antwerp is famous for the diamond trade.

abschnitte.text: Belgium lies in the west of Europe on the **North Sea**. Its neighbouring countries are **France**, Luxembourg, Germany and the Netherlands. The capital is **Brussels**. Important institutions of the **European Union** and **NATO** have their seat there. At **Waterloo**, south of Brussels, **Napoleon** was finally defeated in 1815.

Belgium became independent in **1830**. It is a **monarchy**: a **king** stands at its head, but the country is governed by an elected government and the parliament. Belgium has **three official languages**: **Dutch** in the north, **French** in the south and **German** in a small area in the east. Like Switzerland, it is therefore a multilingual country.

The Belgian flag has three vertical stripes in **black**, **yellow** and **red**. Well-known cities are Brussels, Ghent, Bruges, Liège and **Antwerp**. Antwerp has one of the largest ports in Europe and is famous for the trade in **diamonds**. Bruges is sometimes called the “Venice of the North” because of its canals.

Belgium is known for **waffles** with a grid pattern and for fine **chocolate**. The **praline**, a filled chocolate sweet, was invented in Belgium. Chips are also regarded as a Belgian speciality. People often eat them with mayonnaise.

In Belgium, comics have a great tradition. The **Smurfs**, small blue creatures, come from Belgium. They were invented by the artist **Peyo**. **Tintin and Snowy** by Hergé also come from Belgium. In Brussels many house walls are painted with comic characters.

gewusst: In Brussels there is a large museum just for comics.
The Atomium in Brussels shows an iron crystal enlarged to a huge size.

teile.einleitung: The Dinaric Alps, also called the Dinarides, run along the Adriatic from Slovenia to Albania. They are famous for their karst landscapes of limestone.
wichtigste: The mountains run parallel to the Adriatic coast from Slovenia to Albania.
They are named after the mountain **Dinara**.
The highest peak is **Maja Jezercë** in Albania.
The technical term **karst** comes from the landscape of Kras between Slovenia and Trieste.
In Montenegro the river **Tara** has cut one of the deepest gorges in Europe.
The cold downslope wind **bora** plunges in winter from the mountains to the Adriatic.

abschnitte.text: The **Dinaric Alps** reach from the Slovenian Karst through Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Montenegro to Albania. They run from north-west to south-east, parallel to the coast. They are named after the mountain **Dinara** on the border between Croatia and Bosnia. The highest peak is **Maja Jezercë** in the Albanian Alps at almost 2,700 metres. The largest mountain range in Croatia is the **Velebit** on the coast.

The Dinarides consist for the most part of **limestone**. Water containing carbonic acid dissolves the limestone and shapes caves, gorges and sinkholes. This landscape is called **karst**. The word comes from the plateau of **Kras** between Slovenia and Trieste. Researchers first described many karst features there, which is why they are named with Slavic words all over the world.

A **polje** is a large, flat basin in karst. Often it is flooded for a time, for example after heavy rain or snowmelt. A **ponor** is a swallow hole in which a river suddenly disappears into the ground. The water then flows on underground and comes out again at another place. In Croatia lie the **Plitvice Lakes**, which are separated step by step by barriers of **tufa**.

The river **Tara** in Montenegro has cut one of the deepest gorges in Europe, in some places over 1,000 metres deep. In winter cold air flows down from the mountains to the coast. This strong, cold downslope wind is called the **bora**. It can be so violent that roads and bridges have to be closed.

gewusst: Words such as polje, ponor and doline are used in geology all over the world and come from Slavic languages.
The Plitvice Lakes have been part of the UNESCO World Heritage since 1979.

teile.einleitung: The Acropolis is a rock in the middle of Athens on which the ancient Greeks built magnificent temples. The most famous of them is the Parthenon, the temple of the goddess Athena.
wichtigste: The Acropolis stands in Athens, the capital of Greece.
“Acropolis” means “high city”.
The Parthenon is the most famous temple on the Acropolis.
It was built about 2,500 years ago from white marble.
On the Erechtheion, six female figures, the caryatids, carry the roof.
The Acropolis is part of the UNESCO World Heritage.

abschnitte.text: The word **Acropolis** comes from Greek: **akros** means high or upper, and **polis** means city. The Acropolis is therefore the “high city”. It is a steep rock that rises above the houses in the middle of **Athens**. In the past it was a fortress to which people could retreat in times of danger. Later it became a sacred place with temples.

The **Parthenon** is the largest and best-known temple on the Acropolis. It was built in the **5th century BC**, about 2,500 years ago. At that time **Pericles** was the most important politician in Athens. The temple is made of white **marble** from a quarry near Athens. On the short sides stand eight columns each, on the long sides 17 each.

The Parthenon was dedicated to the goddess **Athena**. She was the goddess of wisdom and the protector of the city that bears her name. In the temple there once stood a huge statue of her, decorated with gold and ivory. Her symbol was the **owl**. This statue no longer exists today.

You entered the Acropolis through a large gate, the **Propylaea**. Beside it stands the small **Temple of Athena Nike**. At the temple called the **Erechtheion**, six stone female figures instead of columns carry the roof of a porch. They are called **caryatids**. The originals are now in the museum, and at the temple you can see copies.

Over the centuries the buildings were badly damaged, for example by an explosion in 1687. For many years they have been carefully **restored**. Since 1987 the Acropolis has been a **UNESCO World Heritage** site. At the foot of the rock, the **Acropolis Museum** shows many original figures.

gewusst: The columns of the Parthenon lean slightly inwards and are a little thicker in the middle, so that they look straight to the eye.
Many temples on the Acropolis used to be painted in bright colours.

teile.einleitung: The British Isles are a group of islands in the north-west of Europe. They include Great Britain, Ireland and thousands of smaller islands with exciting nature and history.
wichtigste: The two largest islands are Great Britain and Ireland.
There are also thousands of smaller islands, such as Orkney, the Shetland Islands and the Hebrides.
Two states lie on the islands: the United Kingdom and Ireland.
Great Britain became an island about 8,000 years ago through the rising sea level.
Volcanoes shaped places such as the Giant’s Causeway and Arthur’s Seat.
The Isle of Man, Jersey and Guernsey belong to the British Crown but not to the United Kingdom.

abschnitte.text: The largest islands are **Great Britain** and **Ireland**. There are also thousands of smaller islands. In the far north lie the **Shetland Islands**, the northernmost part of Scotland, with the main town Lerwick. On the islands there are two states: the **United Kingdom** and the **Republic of Ireland**. Not everyone in Ireland likes to hear the name British Isles, because Ireland is an independent state.

abschnitte.titel: How Great Britain became an island
abschnitte.text: During the last **ice age** the sea level was much lower. Great Britain was then linked to the European mainland by a land bridge. This land bridge in what is now the North Sea is called **Doggerland**. When the ice sheets melted, the sea rose sharply. About **8,000 years ago** Doggerland was flooded, and Great Britain was an island.

Many millions of years ago there were violent **volcanoes** here. At the **Giant’s Causeway** in Northern Ireland, a sheet of lava cooled slowly, contracted and broke into mostly **hexagonal basalt columns**. **Fingal’s Cave** on the island of Staffa, which inspired the composer Felix Mendelssohn to write a piece of music, is also made of such columns. In the middle of Edinburgh, the hill **Arthur’s Seat** is the remains of an extinct volcano. The **Cuillin** mountains on the Isle of Skye were also formed from volcanic rocks.

The **Isle of Man** and the Channel Islands of **Jersey** and **Guernsey** belong to the British Crown but are not part of the United Kingdom. They are called **Crown dependencies**. They have their own parliaments and laws; the parliament of the Isle of Man is called Tynwald. The United Kingdom is responsible for foreign policy and defence. On Orkney lies the Stone Age village of **Skara Brae**, which was inhabited about 5,000 years ago and is a UNESCO World Heritage site.

gewusst: Skara Brae lay hidden under sand for a long time and was uncovered only in the 19th century after a storm.
The basalt columns of the Giant’s Causeway look as if someone had built them by hand, but they formed entirely naturally.

teile.einleitung: The European Single Market is a shared economic area in which goods, people, services and money cross borders almost as freely as within a single country. It has been regarded as completed since 1993 and affects Switzerland strongly too.
wichtigste: The Single Market rests on four fundamental freedoms: goods, people, services and capital.
The Single European Act of 1986 set the goal for the end of 1992.
Since 1 January 1993 the Single Market has been regarded as completed.
The Cassis de Dijon ruling of 1979 established the mutual recognition of products.
Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein take part through the EEA.
Switzerland rejected the EEA in 1992 and concluded Bilateral Agreements.

abschnitte.text: The Single Market rests on **four fundamental freedoms**: the free movement of **goods**, of **people**, of **services** and of **capital**. A company can therefore sell its products in all the member states. People may work and live in another country. The aim is for the Single Market to work like one single national market.

abschnitte.titel: The road to the Single Market
abschnitte.text: The EU is a **customs union**: between the members there are no customs duties, and towards other countries a **common external tariff** applies. In a pure free trade area, by contrast, each country sets its own customs duties. But even without customs duties, many obstacles remained. That is why the **Single European Act** of 1986 set the aim of completing the Single Market by the end of 1992. It made majority decisions easier, and on **1 January 1993** most border checks on goods were dropped.

An important step was the **Cassis de Dijon ruling** of the European Court of Justice in 1979. It was about a French liqueur that had too little alcohol for the rules in Germany. The court decided: a product that is lawfully sold in one member state may in principle also be sold in the others. This is called **mutual recognition**. In this way many **non-tariff barriers to trade** were removed, that is, obstacles such as different standards or approvals.

Through the **European Economic Area** (EEA), **Norway**, **Iceland** and **Liechtenstein** take part in the Single Market without being EU members. The EEA has existed since 1994. **Switzerland** rejected joining the EEA in the popular vote of **6 December 1992**. Instead it concluded the **Bilateral Agreements I** with the EU, which were signed in 1999 and came into force in 2002. They include the **free movement of persons**, land transport and the removal of technical barriers to trade.

Since July **2010**, Switzerland too has applied the **Cassis de Dijon principle**, though only one way. The basis is a revision of the federal act on technical barriers to trade. Since then many products from the EU may be sold in Switzerland as well without extra checks. The aim was for goods to become cheaper. For some products, for example foodstuffs, special rules apply.

gewusst: A French blackcurrant liqueur gave its name to one of the most important principles of European trade.
Switzerland applies the Cassis de Dijon principle even though it does not belong to the EU.

teile.einleitung: Finland is a country in the north of Europe with many lakes and great forests. The Finns call their country Suomi, and the sauna and the Moomins come from here.
wichtigste: Finland is called the “land of a thousand lakes”, but has well over a hundred thousand.
The flag shows a blue cross on a white background.
Finland is the only Nordic country with the euro.
About three quarters of the country is forest.
In Finnish the country is called Suomi.
Finland became independent from Russia on 6 December 1917.

abschnitte.text: Finland is often called the **land of a thousand lakes**. In reality there are even **well over a hundred thousand** lakes. About **three quarters** of the country is covered with **forest**, which makes Finland one of the most heavily forested countries in Europe. In the east Finland has a long border with **Russia**, and in the west lie Sweden and Norway. The capital is **Helsinki** on the Baltic Sea.

The Finnish flag shows a **blue cross on a white background**. People often say that blue stands for the lakes and white for the snow. In Finnish the country is called **Suomi**, which is why stamps and coins often say “Suomi Finland”. Finland is the **only Nordic country** that pays with the **euro**. Since 2002 there have been euro coins and notes there.

For a long time Finland belonged to **Sweden**. From 1809 it was a **Grand Duchy** under the Russian tsar. On **6 December 1917** Finland declared its **independence**, and this day is still the national holiday today. Since 1995 Finland has been a member of the EU, and since 2023 of NATO too. The official languages are **Finnish** and **Swedish**.

The word **sauna** is Finnish. In Finland there are about three million saunas, so almost one in every house. Also world famous are the **Moomins**, friendly troll creatures with round noses. They were invented by the author **Tove Jansson**. Her books and comics exist in many languages.

In the north of Finland lies **Lapland**. There the sun does not set for weeks in summer, and in winter you often see the **northern lights**. In the town of **Rovaniemi** there is a **village of Father Christmas**. Every year many children from all over the world come to visit. Rovaniemi lies right on the Arctic Circle.

gewusst: In Finland there are about three million saunas, so more than one sauna for every two people.
Father Christmas in Rovaniemi receives letters from all over the world every year.

teile.einleitung: The European flag is blue and shows a circle of golden stars. It is the symbol of Europe and is used by the Council of Europe and by the European Union.
wichtigste: The European flag always has 12 golden stars in a circle.
Each star has five points.
The 12 stars stand for perfection and unity, not for individual countries.
The Council of Europe introduced the flag in 1955.
Later the EU adopted the flag.
Switzerland has been a member of the Council of Europe since 1963.

abschnitte.text: The European flag has a **blue** background. On it stand **12 golden stars** in a circle. Each star has **five points**. The middle of the flag is empty and simply blue. The circle looks like the face of a clock, with the stars standing where the hours would be.

Many people think each star stands for one country. But that is not true. The number **12** has long been seen as a sign of **perfection** and **unity**, think of 12 months or 12 hours on the clock. That is why the number always stays the same, even when new countries join. The circle stands for togetherness and solidarity among the peoples of Europe.

abschnitte.titel: The Council of Europe and the EU
abschnitte.text: The flag was chosen in **1955** by the **Council of Europe**. The Council of Europe is an organisation that works for **human rights**, democracy and the rule of law. It has its seat in **Strasbourg**. Later, in the 1980s, the European Communities, from which the **EU** grew, also adopted the flag. That is why you see it today above all in front of **EU buildings** and next to the flags of the member countries.

**Switzerland** has been a member of the Council of Europe since **1963**. So it belongs to the organisation from which the European flag comes. But Switzerland is not a member of the **EU**. That is why the European flag is rather rarely seen flying in Switzerland, for example at international events. On car number plates in EU countries, however, you see the circle of stars very often.

gewusst: The number of stars was already 12 before the EU had 12 members, and it stayed 12 when there were more.
The European flag also has an anthem: Beethoven’s “Ode to Joy”.

teile.einleitung: The Drogden Tunnel is a tunnel under the sea between Denmark and Sweden. It is part of the Øresund Link, which links Copenhagen with Malmö.
wichtigste: The Drogden Tunnel is part of the **Øresund Link**.
It begins in Denmark near Copenhagen Airport.
The tunnel is about 4 kilometres long.
It ends on the artificial island of **Peberholm**.
From there the Øresund Bridge continues to Sweden.
The link was opened in the year 2000.

abschnitte.text: The **Øresund Link** consists of three parts. From Denmark, first the **Drogden Tunnel** runs under the sea. Then comes the artificial island of **Peberholm**, which was specially built up for the link. From there the **Øresund Bridge** leads to the Swedish coast near Malmö. Since the opening in 2000 you can travel back and forth between the two countries by car and train.

Right next to the Danish shore lies **Copenhagen Airport**. A tall bridge there would have been in the way of the aircraft. In addition, an important shipping channel runs through the strait of **Drogden**. With a tunnel the way stays free for large ships. That is why a tunnel was chosen for this stretch.

The Drogden Tunnel is an **immersed tunnel**. The individual tunnel sections were built of concrete on land. Then they were towed by ships to the right place and lowered into a dredged trench in the sea bed. Under water the parts were joined together. In the tunnel there are tubes for the motorway and for the railway.

gewusst: The island of Peberholm was built specially for the Øresund Link and today is a habitat for many plants and birds.
Through the Øresund Link many people commute daily between Denmark and Sweden to work.

teile.einleitung: Airbus is a European company that makes aeroplanes, helicopters and space technology. Alongside Boeing of the USA, it is the largest maker of passenger aircraft in the world.
wichtigste: Airbus Industrie was founded in 1970.
At the start there were French and German firms; later Spain and Great Britain joined.
The first Airbus aircraft was the A300.
The A380 is the largest passenger aircraft in the world.
Important sites are Toulouse and Hamburg-Finkenwerder.
The biggest competitor is Boeing.

abschnitte.text: **Airbus Industrie** was founded in **1970** by French and German companies. Later, firms from **Spain** and **Great Britain** joined. The aim was to create a European counterweight to the big aircraft makers of the USA. Today Airbus and **Boeing** largely share the market for large passenger aircraft between them. This is called a **duopoly**, a market with only two big suppliers.

The first model was the **A300**. It first flew in 1972 and was the world’s first twin-engine **wide-body aircraft**. Later came the **A320 family**, which very many airlines use for shorter routes. The **A380**, with two full-length passenger decks, is the largest passenger aircraft in the world. Because too few were ordered, its production ended in 2021 after fewer than 300 aircraft.

The heart of Airbus lies in **Toulouse** in southern France. In the municipality of **Blagnac**, by the airport, stand large assembly halls and the operational headquarters. Toulouse is the capital of the region of **Occitanie**, where aerospace is very important. In Germany, **Hamburg-Finkenwerder** is a main site for the final assembly of the A320 family. Plants such as Bremen and Stade make components.

The parts of an Airbus are made in different countries. To bring them to the assembly halls, Airbus uses a special transport aircraft, the **Beluga**. It has a huge, bulging fuselage that recalls a **beluga whale**. Whole wings and fuselage sections fit inside. It got its nickname from this whale, which is also called a beluga.

Even before Airbus, Toulouse was a city of aircraft building. The French examples of **Concorde**, the famous **supersonic aircraft**, were assembled there. Concorde was developed together with Great Britain, and the British examples were built near Bristol. Airlines from Switzerland also use many Airbus aircraft.

gewusst: The A300 was the first wide-body aircraft in the world with only two engines.
The Beluga can carry whole aircraft wings in its belly.

teile.einleitung: In many countries of Europe, fewer children are born today than in the past. This is called a falling birth rate. It changes how old a society is on average, and has consequences for schools, work and pensions.
wichtigste: The total fertility rate shows how many children a woman would have on average.
For a population to stay the same size without immigration, about 2.1 children per woman are needed.
In 2023 the EU stood at about 1.4 children per woman, according to Eurostat.
In 2023 Malta had the lowest fertility rate in the EU at about 1.06, and Spain was at about 1.1.
In 2023 about 3.7 million children were born in the EU.
When few children are born, the population pyramid becomes narrow at the bottom like an urn.

abschnitte.text: Experts use the **total fertility rate**. It adds together the birth rates of all age years from about 15 to 49. In this way it shows how many children a woman would have if today’s rates applied throughout her whole life. For a population to stay the same size in the long run without immigration, in countries with low mortality about **2.1 children per woman** are needed. This is called the **replacement level**. The value is slightly above 2 because not all girls grow up to be adults and slightly more boys are born.

According to the statistics office **Eurostat**, the whole EU stood in 2023 at about **1.38 children per woman**. The lowest value was in **Malta** at about 1.06, closely followed by **Spain** at about 1.12 and Lithuania. In 2023 about **3.67 million** children were born in the EU, around 5 per cent fewer than the year before. This was the sharpest fall since the series began in 1961. In Switzerland too the value in 2023, at about 1.3, was clearly below 2.1.

If the fertility rate stays below 1.3 for a long time, experts speak of **“lowest-low fertility”**. The term arose in the early 2000s, when countries such as **Italy** and **Spain** reached such values for the first time. Without immigration this leads to a rapid **fall in population**. Each new generation is then clearly smaller than that of its parents.

There are many reasons for falling birth rates. In **southern Europe**, young adults often leave their parents’ home only around the age of 30. **Insecure jobs**, high youth unemployment and **expensive housing** delay starting a family. In addition, many people stay in education for longer and decide later to have children. Experts discuss which measures could help, for example cheaper childcare.

The **population pyramid** shows how many people live at each age. If fewer children are born over decades, the lower steps become narrower than the middle ones. The pyramid then looks like an **urn**. There are more older people and fewer young ones. This affects, for example, **old-age provision**: in Switzerland the people in work pay into the **AVS** (old-age insurance), from which the pensions are paid.

gewusst: The fall in births in the EU from 2022 to 2023 was the sharpest since counting began in 1961.
For a population to stay the same size, 2 children per woman are not quite enough, about 2.1 are needed.
Many countries in Europe are growing in spite of fewer births, because people move in.

teile.einleitung: Lake Titicaca is a huge lake high in the Andes of South America, on the border between Peru and Bolivia. It lies at over 3,800 metres above sea level, higher than almost all the peaks of the Alps except the highest. It is known for the floating reed islands of the Uros.
wichtigste: Lake Titicaca lies in the Andes between Peru and Bolivia.
It lies at about 3,812 metres above sea level.
At about 8,300 square kilometres, it is about 15 times as large as Lake Constance.
It is regarded as the highest navigable lake in the world.
The Uros people live on floating islands made of reeds.
According to an Inca legend, the first Incas rose out of the lake.
In the lake lives the Titicaca water frog, which exists only here.

abschnitte.text: Lake Titicaca lies on the **Altiplano**, a high plain in the Andes. The border between **Peru** and **Bolivia** runs right through the lake. It is about 190 kilometres long and up to about 280 metres deep. Around the lake rise snow-covered peaks of the Cordillera Real.

The **Uros** people build islands from **totora reeds**, which grow in the lake. They keep piling up fresh reeds, because the lower layers rot in the water. They also make houses and boats from reeds. The islands lie mainly in the bay near Puno in Peru and are visited by many tourists today.

For the **Incas** the lake was sacred. According to a legend, the sun god and the first Incas rose out of Lake Titicaca. On the **Isla del Sol**, the Island of the Sun, you can still find ruins from the time of the Incas today. Even before the Incas, cultures such as Tiwanaku lived by the lake.

In the lake lives the **Titicaca water frog**, which uses its skin to take in oxygen in the cold water. That is why it has very wrinkled skin. On the shore, llamas and alpacas graze, and many water birds breed in the reeds. Because the air is so thin and the sun so strong, the climate is mild by day and very cold at night.

Many people who speak **Quechua** or **Aymara** live by the lake. They fish, grow potatoes and quinoa, and keep animals. Important places are Puno in Peru and Copacabana in Bolivia. Bolivia has no access to the sea, but it keeps a small navy on Lake Titicaca.

begriffe.erklaerung: A very high, flat plain in the Andes of Peru and Bolivia.
A reed that grows in Lake Titicaca and is used for islands and boats.
A people who traditionally live on floating reed islands in Lake Titicaca.
An Indigenous people with their own language in Bolivia and Peru.

gewusst: Bolivia has a navy although the country has no access to the sea, and it practises on Lake Titicaca, among other places.
Anyone arriving at Lake Titicaca often gets a headache because of the thin air, which is called altitude sickness.
The reed islands of the Uros feel soft and springy to walk on.

teile.einleitung: Bar is a port town on the coast of Montenegro. It has the country’s most important port and is linked by a railway line to Belgrade in Serbia.
wichtigste: Bar lies on the Adriatic in Montenegro.
Bar has the most important port in Montenegro.
A railway line links Bar with Belgrade.
Ferries sail from Bar across the Adriatic to Italy.
Above the town lie the ruins of the old town, Stari Bar.

abschnitte.text: **Bar** lies in the south of Montenegro on the **Adriatic**. The town has the largest and most important **port** in the country. Goods are loaded here, and **ferries** sail across the Adriatic to **Italy**, for example to Bari. Behind the town steep mountains rise.

Bar is linked by a **railway line** with **Belgrade**, the capital of Serbia. The line was opened in the 1970s. It runs through the mountains over very many **tunnels** and **bridges**. This gave Serbia access to the sea through the port of Bar. The journey is regarded as one of the most impressive railway trips in the Balkans.

Some kilometres from the sea lies **Stari Bar**, the old town. Today what is left of it is mainly **ruins** with walls, churches and houses. People later moved to the coast, where the new town grew. In the area there is also a very old **olive tree**, which is many hundreds of years old.

gewusst: The railway line from Belgrade to Bar crosses one of the highest railway bridges in Europe, the Mala Rijeka Viaduct.

teile.einleitung: Andorra is a very small country high in the Pyrenees between Spain and France. It has two heads of state and is popular with skiers and shopping tourists.
wichtigste: Andorra lies between Spain and France.
The capital is called Andorra la Vella.
The official language is Catalan.
Andorra has no sea; it is a landlocked country.
People pay with the euro.
Andorra has two co-princes as heads of state.

abschnitte.text: Andorra lies in the **Pyrenees**, a mountain range between Spain and France. In the south it borders Spain, in the north France. The country is very small and has fewer inhabitants than the city of Bern. It has no coast and, like Switzerland, is a **landlocked country**. Many valleys and peaks are over 2,000 metres high.

The capital is called **Andorra la Vella**. It lies at over 1,000 metres and is one of the highest capitals in Europe. The only official language is **Catalan**. But many people also speak Spanish and French. People pay with the **euro**, although Andorra does not belong to the European Union.

Andorra is a **principality** with a peculiarity: it has two heads of state, the **co-princes**. One is the **President of France**, the other the **Bishop of Urgell**, a town in Spain. This rule is many centuries old. Today the co-princes mainly have a ceremonial role. The country is governed by its own government and an elected parliament.

In winter there is a lot of snow in the mountains, so many visitors come for **skiing**. In summer many people hike in the valleys. Andorra is also popular for **shopping**, because many goods are cheaper there thanks to low taxes. **Tourism** is the most important branch of the country’s economy.

gewusst: Andorra is divided into seven municipalities, which are called parishes (Parròquies).
Andorra has no airport of its own; you arrive by road from Spain or France.

teile.einleitung: Great Britain is the largest island of the British Isles and the largest island in Europe. England, Scotland and Wales lie on it. Together with Northern Ireland they form the United Kingdom.
wichtigste: Great Britain is the largest island of the British Isles.
It is also the largest island in Europe.
Ireland is the second largest island of the British Isles.
England, Scotland and Wales lie on Great Britain.
The United Kingdom also includes Northern Ireland.
The Channel Tunnel has linked the island with France since 1994.

abschnitte.text: The **British Isles** lie in the north-west of Europe. The largest of them is **Great Britain**, which is also the **largest island in Europe**. The second largest is **Ireland**. There are also many smaller islands, such as the Hebrides and the Orkney Islands. Great Britain is separated from the European mainland by the **English Channel** and the North Sea.

abschnitte.titel: Three parts of the country on one island
abschnitte.text: **England**, **Scotland** and **Wales** lie on the island. Together with **Northern Ireland**, on the island of Ireland, they form the **United Kingdom**. In everyday speech people often say “Great Britain” when they mean the whole state. Strictly speaking, though, Great Britain is only the island. The capital of the United Kingdom is **London**, on the Thames.

The south and east of England are rather flat and hilly. In the north and west there are mountains, especially in **Scotland** and Wales. The highest mountain on the island is **Ben Nevis** in Scotland, at just over 1300 metres. That is much less than the peaks of the Swiss Alps. The climate is mild and often damp, because the sea is never far away.

For a long time Great Britain could only be reached by ship or aeroplane. Since **1994** the **Channel Tunnel** under the English Channel has linked the island with **France**. Trains run through it from London to Paris and Brussels. Cars are also carried through the tunnel on trains.

gewusst: Great Britain is one of the ten largest islands in the world.
Nowhere on the island are you more than about 120 kilometres from the sea.

teile.einleitung: At 1,345 metres, Ben Nevis is the highest mountain in Great Britain. It stands in Scotland near the town of Fort William and is often wrapped in cloud.
wichtigste: Ben Nevis is 1,345 metres high, the highest mountain in Great Britain.
It lies near the town of Fort William in Scotland.
It belongs to the Grampian Mountains.
It consists largely of volcanic rock.
From 1883 to 1904 there was a weather station on the summit.
At the foot of the mountain runs the valley of Glen Nevis.

abschnitte.text: At **1,345 metres**, **Ben Nevis** is the highest mountain in Great Britain. It lies in the Scottish **Highlands** and belongs to the **Grampian Mountains**. At the foot of the mountain lies the town of **Fort William**. By Swiss standards it is not very high: the **Säntis**, at 2,502 metres, is about 1,150 metres higher.

Ben Nevis consists largely of **volcanic rock**. It is the remains of an ancient volcano that was active a very long time ago. Glaciers of the ice ages later smoothed the mountain and shaped deep valleys. The **north face** drops away steeply and is popular with climbers.

On the summit the weather is often rough. Because of the **damp, cool maritime climate**, there is frequently **fog** there, and even in summer snow can still lie. On most days of the year the summit is in cloud. From **1883 to 1904** there was a **weather station** at the top, where researchers observed the weather closely. Today only its ruins can be seen.

At the foot of the mountain runs the valley of **Glen Nevis**. From there a much-used footpath leads to the summit. Very many people climb up every year. Because the weather can change quickly, you need good equipment, warm clothing and a map.

gewusst: Once a year there is a hill race from Fort William to the summit and back.
The summit of Ben Nevis is a broad, stony plateau.

teile.einleitung: Cetinje is a small town in the mountains of Montenegro. For centuries it was the capital of the country and the seat of its princes and kings.
wichtigste: Cetinje used to be the capital of Montenegro.
For centuries the princes and later the king lived here.
The present capital is Podgorica.
In Cetinje the president of Montenegro still has an official residence.
The monastery of Cetinje is very old and important for the country.

abschnitte.text: **Cetinje** lies in a high valley at the foot of the mountain **Lovćen**. For centuries the town was the centre of **Montenegro**. The princes ruled here, and from 1910 Montenegro was a **kingdom** with Cetinje as its capital. Today **Podgorica** is the capital of the country. But Cetinje bears the title of the old royal capital, and the president still has an official residence here.

An important building is the **Cetinje Monastery**, which was founded in the 15th century and later rebuilt. For a long time Montenegro was ruled by **prince-bishops**. They were at once head of the church and of the country. The best known of them is **Petar II Petrović-Njegoš**. He was also a famous poet and lies buried in a mausoleum high up on Lovćen.

When Cetinje was still the capital, many countries of Europe had an **embassy** there. Some of these buildings still stand today and house, for example, museums or colleges. In the former royal palace there is also a **museum**. So the small town still shows today what role it once played.

gewusst: For such a small town, Cetinje once had a surprising number of foreign embassies.
