teile.einleitung: The Delta Works are a huge system of protection against the sea in the south-west of the Netherlands. They consist of dams, locks and storm surge barriers and count as one of the largest flood protection structures in the world.
wichtigste: The impulse for building was the **Holland flood** of February 1953.
At that time around 1,800 people died in the Netherlands.
The province of **Zeeland** was flooded the worst.
By closing off the sea inlets, the line of dykes was greatly shortened.
The **Oosterschelde Barrier** is about 9 kilometres long and has 62 movable gates.
The **Maeslantkering** protects Rotterdam with two huge gates.

abschnitte.text: In the night of 1 February 1953, a severe storm pushed the water of the North Sea against the coast. At the same time it was spring tide, so the water stood especially high. Many dykes broke, and large parts of **Zeeland** and other areas were flooded. Around 1,800 people lost their lives, and very many lost their homes. This disaster is called the **Holland flood**.

Shortly after the flood, the government decided on the **Delta Plan**. In the estuary area of the Rhine, Meuse and Scheldt there were many sea inlets. Instead of raising all the dykes along these inlets, the sea inlets themselves were to be closed off with dams. This greatly shortened the line of dykes that has to be protected. The building took several decades.

The **Oosterschelde** too was originally meant to be closed with a solid dam. Fishers and nature conservationists opposed this, because tides and the salt-water habitat would then have been lost. So a **barrier** with 62 movable gates was built. These are large gates that normally stand open and are closed only in a storm surge. The structure is about 9 kilometres long and was inaugurated in 1986.

Rotterdam has one of the largest ports in Europe, and the Nieuwe Waterweg must stay open to ships. That is why the **Maeslantkering** was built there. It consists of two huge gates that lie on the banks. If a water level of 3 metres above **NAP**, the Dutch height reference, threatens at Rotterdam, they swing in automatically and close the waterway. It was completed in 1997.

gewusst: The two gates of the Maeslantkering are among the largest moving structures in the world.
A large part of the Netherlands lies below sea level and would be flooded without dykes.

teile.einleitung: Germany is one of the most important car countries in the world. The modern car was invented here, and well-known brands such as Volkswagen, Mercedes-Benz, BMW, Audi and Porsche have their seats here.
wichtigste: In 1886 Carl Benz applied for a patent for a car with a gas engine.
Volkswagen has its headquarters in Wolfsburg.
Mercedes-Benz and Porsche are based in Stuttgart, Audi in Ingolstadt.
Bosch is the largest car supplier in the world.
In 2015 an emissions scandal shook the industry.
The switch to electric mobility is the biggest challenge.

abschnitte.text: In **1886** **Carl Benz** applied for a patent for a vehicle with a gas engine. His **Patent Motor Car** had three wheels and counts as the first modern car. At about the same time, Gottlieb Daimler and Wilhelm Maybach were also building vehicles with engines. From their companies the **Mercedes-Benz** brand later emerged.

**Volkswagen AG** has its headquarters in **Wolfsburg** in Lower Saxony. In **Stuttgart** are **Mercedes-Benz** and **Porsche**. **Audi** has its seat in **Ingolstadt** in Bavaria, and **BMW** comes from Munich. These brands sell their cars all over the world, including very many to Switzerland.

A car consists of thousands of parts. Many of them are made by **suppliers**. The German company **Bosch** is the largest car supplier in the world. In the factories the principle of **just-in-time** often applies: the parts are delivered to the assembly line exactly when they are needed. This way little storage is needed, but any delay can stop production.

In **2015** it became known that the **emissions figures** of many **diesel cars** had been **manipulated**. Software made sure that the cars gave off few pollutants only in the test. The scandal first affected Volkswagen and cost the company billions. As a result, many customers lost trust in the industry.

Since the 2010s the car industry has faced the **switch to electric mobility**. Instead of petrol and diesel engines, batteries and electric motors are needed. This changes factories and jobs. New companies are also pushing into the market: **Tesla** opened its first European car factory in **2022** in **Grünheide near Berlin**.

gewusst: Bertha Benz, the wife of Carl Benz, was the first person to drive a longer distance in a car, in 1888.
The name Volkswagen simply means “people’s car”.

teile.einleitung: The Gulf of Finland is a long arm of the sea in the east of the Baltic Sea. On its shores lie three well-known cities: Helsinki, Tallinn and St Petersburg.
wichtigste: The Gulf of Finland is an eastern arm of the Baltic Sea.
To the north lies Finland, to the south Estonia, to the east Russia.
Helsinki lies on the north coast, Tallinn on the south coast.
Right in the east lies St Petersburg, where the Neva flows in.
In winter the gulf often partly freezes over.

abschnitte.text: The **Gulf of Finland** is a long, narrow arm of the **Baltic Sea**. It reaches far to the east as far as **St Petersburg** in Russia. To the north lies **Finland** with its capital **Helsinki**. On the south coast lies **Estonia** with its capital **Tallinn**. A gulf is a large bay that reaches deep into the land.

Large rivers flow into the gulf, above all the **Neva** at St Petersburg. That is why the water is only slightly salty, and is called **brackish water**. Because it contains so little salt, it freezes more easily in winter. Often the gulf is partly covered with **ice**. Then ships sometimes need the help of **icebreakers**.

Between **Helsinki** and **Tallinn** many **ferries** run every day. The crossing takes only a few hours, so many people visit the other city for a day trip. Even in the Middle Ages the region was important for the **trade** of the Hanseatic League. Today too, many cargo ships pass through the gulf, for example to the ports near St Petersburg.

gewusst: Helsinki and Tallinn lie almost directly opposite each other across the gulf.
Because the water is only slightly salty, the Gulf of Finland freezes more easily than the open sea.

teile.einleitung: The Folketing is the parliament of Denmark. The laws of the country are passed here. In English the name means roughly “people’s assembly”.
wichtigste: The Folketing is the parliament of the Kingdom of Denmark.
It has 179 seats.
Two seats each belong to members from Greenland and from the Faroe Islands.
The parliament meets in Christiansborg Palace in Copenhagen.
The Folketing consists of only a single chamber.

abschnitte.titel: A parliament for the whole kingdom
abschnitte.text: The **Folketing** is the representation of the people of Denmark. It has **179 seats**. Most members come from Denmark itself. Two seats each are reserved for **Greenland** and the **Faroe Islands**, which belong to the kingdom but run many things themselves. In this way these distant territories also have a voice in Copenhagen.

The members are elected by the people, at the latest every four years. The seats are distributed by **proportional representation**, that is, roughly according to the share of votes of each party. The Folketing passes the **laws** and the state budget. It also keeps watch over the government. Denmark is a **monarchy**, but the political decisions are made by parliament and government.

In the past Denmark had a parliament with two chambers. Since a change to the constitution in 1953 there has been only the Folketing. It meets in **Christiansborg Palace** in Copenhagen. In the same building are also the office of the head of government and the supreme court. Switzerland, by contrast, has two chambers: the **National Council** and the **Council of States**.

gewusst: In Christiansborg Palace, parliament, head of government and supreme court sit under one roof.
The Danish constitution dates from 1849, and its anniversary on 5 June is a public holiday in Denmark.

teile.einleitung: The Brandenburg Gate is the best-known landmark of Berlin. It is over 200 years old and today stands for the reunification of Germany.
wichtigste: The Brandenburg Gate stands on Pariser Platz in Berlin.
It was built over 200 years ago from pale sandstone.
On top stands the Quadriga, a chariot with four horses.
The chariot is driven by Victoria, the goddess of victory.
For almost 30 years the Berlin Wall stood right by the gate.
On New Year’s Eve many people celebrate there every year with fireworks.

abschnitte.text: The **Brandenburg Gate** was built between 1788 and 1791. The architect was called Carl Gotthard Langhans. The gate is made of pale **sandstone** and has twelve large columns. Between them there are five passages. In the past it was one of several city gates of Berlin. It stands on **Pariser Platz**, which is named after the capital of France.

On top of the gate stands the **Quadriga**. This is the name for a chariot pulled by **four horses**. On it stands **Victoria**, the goddess of victory. She holds a staff with an eagle. In 1806 Napoleon had the Quadriga taken to Paris. In 1814 it came back to Berlin, and the square in front of the gate afterwards got the name Pariser Platz.

From 1961 to 1989 Berlin was divided by the **Berlin Wall**. It ran right by the Brandenburg Gate, and nobody could pass through. After the **fall of the Wall** in November 1989, the gate was opened again in December. Since then it has been a symbol of the **reunification** of East and West Germany. Many pictures of cheering people at the gate went around the world at that time.

Today the gate is a meeting place for people from all over the world. On the night of 1 January there is a big **New Year’s Eve party** in front of it with **fireworks**. Concerts and sports festivals also take place there, for example at the Berlin Marathon. The gate is also shown on German euro coins.

gewusst: The Quadriga spent a few years in Paris because Napoleon had it taken away after his victory.
The Brandenburg Gate can be seen on the German 10, 20 and 50 cent coins.

teile.einleitung: Albanian is the language of the Albanians. It belongs to the large Indo-European language family, but has no close relatives there and forms a branch of its own.
wichtigste: Albanian belongs to the Indo-European language family.
Within this family it forms a branch of its own.
It is spoken mainly in Albania and in Kosovo.
There are two large dialect groups: Gheg in the north and Tosk in the south.
Albanian is written with Latin letters.

abschnitte.text: Many languages of Europe belong to the **Indo-European language family**, for example German, French, Italian and Greek. Within this family there are groups of closely related languages, such as the Germanic or the Romance languages. Albanian fits into none of these groups. It has no close relatives and therefore forms a **branch of its own**. Over the course of history, however, it has taken over many words from Latin, Greek, Slavic and Turkish.

Albanian is an official language in **Albania** and in **Kosovo**. Many people also speak it in **North Macedonia**. In southern Italy, communities have lived for centuries who speak an old form of Albanian, called **Arbëresh**. There are two large dialect groups: **Gheg** in the north and **Tosk** in the south. Today’s standard language is based mainly on Tosk.

Today Albanian is written with **Latin letters**, plus signs such as **ë** and **ç**. The alphabet was fixed in 1908. In **Switzerland**, Albanian is among the most common languages spoken besides the national languages. Many children in Switzerland grow up with Albanian and German, French or Italian.

gewusst: The Albanian word for Albania, Shqipëria, is often linked with the word for eagle.
The Albanian alphabet has 36 letters, more than the German or English alphabet.

teile.einleitung: A fjell is a wide, treeless upland in Norway. It lies above the tree line and is typical of the Scandinavian Mountains.
wichtigste: In Norway, fjell is the name for the treeless upland above the tree line.
Fjells are typical of the Scandinavian Mountains.
Mainly grass, mosses, lichens and low shrubs grow there.
In Sweden such a landscape is called fjäll.
The Hardangervidda is a well-known plateau in Norway.

abschnitte.text: A **fjell** is a wide, bare upland above the **tree line**. It is so cold and windy there that no large trees grow any more. Instead of pointed peaks there are often **gentle hills** and wide high plains. Fjells are typical of the **Scandinavian Mountains** in Norway and Sweden. In Sweden it is called **fjäll**.

On the fjell grow mainly **grasses**, **mosses**, **lichens** and low shrubs such as dwarf birches. In summer many small flowers bloom, and there are berries. **Reindeer**, ptarmigan and other animals that are used to the cold live here. On the **Hardangervidda**, a large plateau in Norway, even herds of wild reindeer roam. In winter snow lies for a long time.

For many people in Norway the fjell is a popular place for outings. In summer they hike there and stay overnight in **huts**. In winter they go **cross-country skiing** over the wide plains. But the weather can change quickly, so you have to be well equipped. In Switzerland the terrain above the tree line with its alpine pastures is a little like the fjell.

gewusst: In Finland too there are such bare mountains, and there they are called tunturi.
On the Hardangervidda lives one of the largest herds of wild reindeer in Europe.
